title: Jim Harbaugh tries to extend Week 1 record to 7-0
summary: When it comes to the first game of football season, Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh does indeed attack the day with an enthusiasm unknown to mankind.
full_text: When it comes to the first game of football season, Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh does indeed attack the day with an enthusiasm unknown to mankind. Except for someone named " Potsy ." Harbaugh has a 6-0 record in Week 1, from his four seasons in San Francisco and two in L.A. With a win on Sunday against the Cardinals, he'll be 7-0 in Week 1. And that will put him one more Week 1 win away from tying the all-time record. Via NBC Sports research, George "Potsy" Clark had a record of 8-0-2 in Week 1, from 1931 to 1940. Clark's run started with the Portsmouth Spartans, who became the Detroit Lions. In 1937 and 1938, he coached the Brooklyn Dodgers. In 1940, his last year as an NFL head coach, Clark returned to the Lions. It would be a surprise if the Chargers don't win today. They host the Cardinals (who have lost nine straight Week 1 games), and the home team is a 9.5-point favorite.
author: Mike Florio

title: Justin Herbert needs 180 passing yards to be fourth-fastest to 25,000
summary: The quarterback whom Jim Harbaugh believes will be remembered as the greatest of all time has a chance to join the all-time greats on Sunday.
full_text: The quarterback whom Jim Harbaugh believes will be remembered as the greatest of all time has a chance to join the all-time greats on Sunday. With 180 passing yards, Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert will reach 25,000 yards for his career. It would make him the fourth-fastest quarterback in NFL history to get there, via NBC Sports research. Herbert, if he does it, will have done it in 96 games. Patrick Mahomes got there in 83. Matthew Stafford crossed the 25K boundary in 90 games. And Dan Marino did it in 92. It'll take much more than statistical achievements to earn "GOAT" status for Herbert. His first career playoff win, for example, would be a useful starting point. Before that can happen, the Chargers have to qualify for the playoffs again. In a very competitive division and a conference featuring multiple wild-card contenders, it won't be easy. Between the Bills, Patriots, Bengals, Ravens, Steelers, Texans, Jaguars, Broncos, Chiefs, and Chargers, at least three will have their seasons end in Week 18.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Lamar Jackson, Ravens have not had substantive contract talks
summary: Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will play his first game under offensive coordinator Declan Doyle on Sunday and he's set to do so without a contract extension.
full_text: Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will play his first game under offensive coordinator Declan Doyle on Sunday and he's set to do so without a contract extension. Jackson has a cap hit of more than $84 million for the 2027 season, which is the final year of his current deal. The Ravens have expressed desire to get a new deal done, but nothing has come together and Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that no substantive conversations have taken place about an agreement. As a result, Jackson, who does not employ an agent, is expected to start the season under his current pact and will likely end it with the same deal as he prefers not to discuss contract matters during the season. Ravens General Manager Eric DeCosta recently expressed optimism about reaching agreement on an extension before March 2027 and Sunday's report suggests that any deal will wait until much closer to that time.
author: Josh Alper

title: Alvin Kamara is not expected to play on Sunday
summary: The Saints are set to open the 2026 season without running back Alvin Kamara.
full_text: The Saints are set to open the 2026 season without running back Alvin Kamara. Kamara suffered a sprained MCL last month and returned to practice this week. He was a limited participant for two days before fully participating in Friday's practice, but was listed as questionable on the team's final injury report. Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that Kamara is not expected to play against the Lions as he continues to recover. Free agent acquisition Travis Etienne will be the top back for New Orleans. Kendre Miller is the other running back on the 53-man roster and the Saints elevated CJ Donaldson from their practice squad for Sunday's game.
author: Josh Alper

title: Report: Joey Porter Jr. is unlikely to play today, trade is possible
summary: Porter, who is listed as questionable with a back injury, looks like he won't go today against the Falcons.
full_text: Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. is unlikely to play today against the Falcons. Porter, who is listed as questionable with a back injury, is unlikely to go, according to Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport. The same report says Porter could be traded, as he and the Steelers have still not come to terms on the new contract Porter is seeking. The Steelers have said they won't negotiate with Porter during the season. Porter said during the week that if he didn't play, it would be because of both his back and because he still has some conditioning work he needs to do after sitting out training camp. He has not said that he will sit out games in protest of his contract status, although that's certainly an inference some will take if he doesn't play today. Porter is heading into the final season of the four-year contract he signed as the Steelers' second-round draft pick in 2023. He's slated to make $3.9 million this year, and any team trading for him would need to be prepared to pay him a whole lot more than that.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Ryan Day: Ohio State considered letting Texas score, but decided we'd play defense
summary: With 1:23 remaining in the fourth quarter on Saturday night, Ohio State led 23-17, but Texas had first-and-goal at the 1-yard line.
full_text: With 1:23 remaining in the fourth quarter on Saturday night, Ohio State led 23-17, but Texas had first-and-goal at the 1-yard line. What Ohio State coach Ryan Day did from there will be one of the most-scrutinized decisions of this college football season. Day could have called Ohio State's final timeout as soon as Texas got to first-and-goal, and then allowed Texas to score. That would have given Ohio State the ball back, down 24-23, with well over a minute remaining to mount a game-winning drive. Instead, Ohio State stopped Texas on first and second down before Texas scored the game-winning touchdown on third down, with just 25 seconds left. Ohio State's desperation final drive lasted just two plays. Day said after the game that letting Texas score was a consideration but he and his team ultimately thought they could play for a goal-line stand. "I considered it, but I felt like at that point we were gonna go play defense and see if we could get off the field, but it didn't work out," Day said. Day said he ultimately decided to have faith in his defense. "We did, we talked about it, and decided that we were gonna play defense," Day said. "When we got that stop right there we said, alright, we're going to take our chances, put the ball down for one yard and see if we can stop them." Ohio State couldn't stop them, and by the time Ohio State got the ball back, the Buckeyes were almost out of time — even though Ohio State also benefited from Texas snapping the ball too fast before scoring, when the Longhorns could have run even more time off the clock. Day decided to give his defense a chance to win the game, and that cost his offense the time to win the game.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Dante Moore struggles as Oregon loses to 24-point underdog Oklahoma State
summary: Oregon quarterback Dante Moore is a potential first overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft, but today he had a rough outing.
full_text: '' Oregon quarterback Dante Moore is a potential first overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft, but today he had a rough outing. Moore and Oregon lost 39-31 to 24-point underdog Oklahoma State today, with Moore completing less than 50 percent of his passes: Moore finished 14-of-29 for 191 yards, with two touchdowns and no interceptions. How big a surprise is that? Oregon entered today ranked No. 6 in the country. Oklahoma State entered today on a 12-game losing streak, the longest in the country. Never before in college football history had a team on a losing streak of more than 10 games beaten a Top 10 opponent. Last year Oregon beat Oklahoma State 69-3. Moore had moments when he showed off his elite arm talent, including touchdown passes of 38 and 36 yards. But he also struggled with his accuracy and had a hard time dealing with Oklahoma State's pass rush. One bad game doesn't mean Moore won't be a top pick, but for a much-hyped prospect, today was a major disappointment.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Arch Manning puts "nightmares" behind him as Texas beats Ohio State
summary: "I couldn't lose to them again. I had nightmares about that game last year," Manning said.
full_text: A year ago, Texas entered the college football season ranked No. 1 and quarterback Arch Manning was viewed as a strong candidate to win the Heisman Trophy and be the first overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft. A loss to Ohio State derailed that. So when Manning and his Longhorns fell behind Ohio State 23-3 on Saturday night, it felt like déjà vu. This time, however, things were different: Manning and the Texas offense marched down the field on three fourth-quarter touchdown drives to beat Ohio State 24-23. "I couldn't lose to them again. I had nightmares about that game last year. So, we're glad to win tonight," Manning said on the field immediately after the game. By the postgame press conference, Manning had settled down a bit, but he told reporters it was the same emotion about desperately wanting to beat the Ohio State team that had given him nightmares. “I did not want to come in here after a loss at home, to Ohio State again, and have y'all tell me we’re not good, all that stuff. I could not let that happen," Manning said. "So that was going through my mind, let's not let that happen. Had to get something going. I always knew we were going to be in it at the end, we just had to get something going, and whatever it takes at the end of the game. I'm so glad we won." Manning made some excellent throws but also missed some open receivers. He finished completing 23 of 37 passes for 195 yards, with one touchdown and one interception. "It wasn't very pretty, but we found a way to win. That's what good teams do," Manning said. Manning is now the favorite to be the first overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft. He still has a lot of football to play before then, but he's now earned his biggest win as a college quarterback, and put his biggest nightmare behind him.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Kyler Murray will be the ninth Vikings' starting QB since 2023
summary: On Sunday, Kyler Murray will make his first start for the Vikings.
full_text: '' On Sunday, Kyler Murray will make his first start for the Vikings. And he'll be the ninth quarterback to start a game for the Vikings since 2023. Via NBC Sports research, that's tied for the most in the NFL during that stretch, with (not surprisingly) the Browns. (Cleveland has had 42 starters since returning to the NFL in 1999; no other team has started more than 30 during that same period of time.) In 2022, coach Kevin O'Connell's first year with the Vikings, Kirk Cousins started all 17 regular-season games. He started the first eight in 2023, before tearing an Achilles tendon at Green Bay. Since then, it's been Jaren Hall (two games), Joshua Dobbs (four), Nick Mullens (four), Sam Darnold (all 17 in 2024), J.J. McCarthy (10), Carson Wentz (five), and Max Brosmer (two). Given that Wentz and McCarthy are currently on the roster and Brosmer is on the practice squad, the Vikings likely won't start a tenth different quarterback in 2026. In 2022 and 2024, when the same guy started every game, the Vikings made the playoffs. The hope will be that Murray manages to start all 17 in 2026 — and that the Vikings get back to the postseason.
author: Mike Florio

title: To no surprise, the Texans and C.J. Stroud will kick the contract can to 2027
summary: Nothing says "football is back" like the issuance of Sunday Splash!
full_text: Nothing says "football is back" like the issuance of Sunday Splash! reports on a Saturday. Per ESPN, the Texans and quarterback C.J. Stroud won’t get a deal done before the start of the season . Which means they'll now wait until after the season ends to assess the situation. The notion that there won't be an in-season deal was already known. G.M. Nick Caserio recently said so . The idea that there won't be a deal before Week 1 wasn't etched in stone, but the handwriting was written on the wall in permanent marker. Would the Texans sign Stroud to a deal based on his performances to date? Yes. Would Stroud accept it? No. Houston's preferred range likely won't get any lower based on 2026. A strong year from Stroud could push it much higher. Even after the coming season, there may be no reason for the Texans to rush it. Stroud remains under contract through 2027. They'd be negotiating against themselves, like the Dolphins did when they gave Tua Tagovailoa what turned out to be a disastrous the-market-is-the-market deal in 2024. Actually, the Texans could let it ride for two more years, with the franchise tag in their back pockets in the event Stroud suddenly reaches a higher level of performance. If he was already there, the Texans wouldn't hesitate to pay him. They did it after three seasons with cornerback Derek Stingley Jr. They did it after three seasons with linebacker Will Anderson. They would have done it with Stroud, too. But only at the number that properly reflects his spot in a range that now extends from $20 million per year to $64 million annually. The Texans remain committed to Stroud. They didn't bench him at halftime of a disastrous divisional-round game against the Patriots, even though they arguably should have. They want him to become a player who forces the Texans to pay him big money. For now, Stroud has to go out and show that he deserves it.
author: Mike Florio

title: Our opposition to the Protect College Sports Act prompted a phone call from Randy Levine
summary: Earlier today, we posted an item about ESPN's advocacy for the Protect College Sports Act.
full_text: Earlier today, we posted an item about ESPN's advocacy for the Protect College Sports Act. The latest example of ESPN's effort to turn the bill into a law was a one-sided interview with Senator Ted Cruz (R-Texas), one of the act's sponsors. I said what I had to say. I heard from multiple members of the media, who agreed with the sentiments that were expressed. But not everyone agreed. At 5:45 p.m. ET, I got a phone call from a number I didn't recognize. It was Randy Levine, president of the New York Yankees and vice-chair (along with Ron DeSantis) of President Trump's Saving College Sports Roundtable. Did I immediately know who Randy Levine was? No. Did that set the stage for a call that didn't go very well? Possibly. He said he wanted to correct some of the statements made in our article about the Cruz interview, by ensuring that I have the facts. I told him that I always want to operate within the confines of any and all relevant facts. Levine then explained that, in his view, collective bargaining is an impossibility for college sports. He pointed to the fact that most universities are public institutions, that the federal labor laws do not apply to public employment, and that it would require a change in the Federal Labor Relations Act, which dates back to the 1930s. When I observed that the NCAA is instead trying to change federal antitrust laws that have been on the books even longer than that, Levine didn't seem to appreciate my point. I wanted to explain to him that the prevalence of commentary regarding the possibility of collective bargaining from various corners of the college-sports ecosystems suggests that it's hardly a non-starter. Laws can be changed. Private entities can be created. Conferences, which aren't public entities, could be the conduit for an acceptable model that would give the NCAA and its members the antitrust exemption that flows from maintaining a multi-employer bargaining unit — which is how the NFL has managed to engineer a path around the antitrust laws. Indeed, Pac-12 Commissioner Teresa Gould said in June 2026 testimony before the Senate Commerce Committee that it’s time for “honest conversations” about collective bargaining . Common sense suggests that, if collective bargaining is impossible, there are no conversations to be had. My conversation with Levine didn't get to that point, however. After I allowed him to speak his mind on the collective bargaining issue, I began to respond, by pointing out the effort to change long-settled federal antitrust laws. He interrupted me. I asked him to let me finish my point. He then launched into the "do you want pro athletes going back to college?" talking point. I told him, bluntly but politely, that the "pro athletes" in question had signed tryout contracts and opted to try to make more money by returning to college football, after they were not offered NFL roster spots. I also told Levine that the entire "pro athlete going back to college" argument is a fallacy, and that college athletes are already pro athletes. And, at that point, he ended the call. Before doing so, Levine pointed out he'd tell everyone that I don't know what I'm talking about, or words to that effect. Good luck with that, Randy. Many people already think I don't know what I'm talking about. That has rarely stopped me from talking, however. Bottom line? We've apparently struck a nerve. Really, why would Levine have taken the time to call me on a Saturday afternoon? The Saving College Sports Roundtable is apparently concerned that this small corner of the Internet may have a little bit of influence when it comes to calling the Protect College Sports Act what it is, and when it comes to mustering real opposition to a flawed bill that will be bad for players.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Parker Washington, Jaguars unlikely to come to agreement
summary: The Jaguars and wide receiver Parker Washington are unlikely to reach a contract extension before the start of the season, Cameron Wolfe of NFL Media reports.
full_text: The Jaguars and wide receiver Parker Washington are unlikely to reach a contract extension before the start of the season, Cameron Wolfe of NFL Media reports. The Jaguars explored a deal in the range of the three-year, $75 million deal that Michael Wilson signed with the Cardinals, per Washington. Washington is in the final year of his rookie deal, scheduled to make $3.722 million this season. The 2023 sixth-round pick posted career highs last season with 58 catches for 847 yards and five touchdowns. He also returned a pair of punts for touchdowns.
author: Charean Williams

title: Patriots place WR A.J. Brown on IR, officially sign DT DaQuan Jones
summary: The Patriots made official the signing of veteran defensive tackle DaQuan Jones.
full_text: The Patriots made official the signing of veteran defensive tackle DaQuan Jones. To get him on the roster, the Patriots needed to open a spot. New England did that by placing wide receiver A.J. Brown on injured reserve. Brown, who has a high-ankle sprain, will not be eligible to return until missing at least four games. He will not play against the Steelers, Jaguars, Bills and Raiders. Brown caught three passes for 26 yards and drew a 34-yard pass interference penalty that set up the team's lone touchdown in the loss to the Seahawks. Veteran Mack Hollins and second-year WR Kyle Williams are the next players up at the X receiver spot.
author: Charean Williams

title: Broncos have no injury designations for Monday night
summary: The Denver Broncos' shot at an appearance in Super Bowl LX arguably was derailed by an injury to quarterback Bo Nix.
full_text: The Denver Broncos' shot at an appearance in Super Bowl LX arguably was derailed by an injury to quarterback Bo Nix. As the 2026 season begins, Nix and the rest of the team are healthy. Denver has no injury designations in advance of the Monday night opener against the Chiefs in Kansas City. Only receiver Marvin Mims appeared on the Week 1 injury report. He fully participated in practice on Thursday, Friday, and Saturday with a foot injury. No team will be much healthier than it is in Week 1. The Broncos are good to go, as they try to win the AFC West for the second straight year. The extent to which they can stay that way will be a major factor in whether they can get back to the Super Bowl for the first time since 2015.
author: Mike Florio

title: NAACP takes issue with ESPN's handling of the Protect College Sports Act
summary: On Saturday, ESPN gave Senator Ted Cruz (R-Texas) a platform to push for the passage of the Protect College Sports Act.
full_text: On Saturday, ESPN gave Senator Ted Cruz (R-Texas) a platform to push for the passage of the Protect College Sports Act. There was no balance, no equal time . And ESPN is receiving the criticism it deserves for its ongoing effort to support the bill. The NAACP has responded. The organization, which seeks to " achieve equity, political rights, and social inclusion by advancing policies and practices that expand human and civil rights, eliminate discrimination, and accelerate the well-being, education, and economic security of Black people and all persons of color," has posted the following statement on Twitter: "Surprised [ESPN] so willing[ly] lent their platform to political performance today. But we’ll play. We’d love to have [NCAA president Derrick Johnson] join you in his home state of Miss. next week to express why the Protect College Sports Act is dangerous to Black Athletes and the Black community." The proponents of the Protect College Sports Act don't want you to think of it that way. They want you to see unrestrained chaos in college sports — created by the reckoning for years of antitrust violations — and they believe the only answer is to give the NCAA and its members an antitrust exemption that will allow the earning power and mobility of players to be limited. The broader point is that ESPN is clearly in the tank for the passage of the Protect College Sports Act. If it isn't, it will give Derrick Johnson a chance next weekend to state the case against it, when College GameDay goes to Oxford for LSU vs. Ole Miss.
author: Mike Florio

title: Judge seals video in Josh Jacobs case
summary: The video of the altercation that resulted in Packers running back Josh Jacobs pleading no contest to multiple misdemeanor charges could complicate his football career, if/when it's ever released.
full_text: The video of the altercation that resulted in Packers running back Josh Jacobs pleading no contest to multiple misdemeanor charges could complicate his football career, if/when it's ever released. For now, it won't be. Via James Stratton of WISN, Judge Marc Hammer has signed an order “temporarily” sealing the evidence in the case. Including the video. The sealing of the evidence was requested not by the prosecution or by the victim but by Jacobs. From the order: "The Court finds that public disclosure of the Discovery Material would threaten or substantially impair Defendant’s and [the victim's] privacy, dignity, personal security, emotional wellbeing, or ability to participate safely in the criminal-justice process. This protection is not to impede any legitimate law-enforcement function, criminal prosecution judicial proceeding, or disclosure otherwise required by law, but to prevent unnecessary public dissemination of information that identifies [the victim], reveals intimate or sensitive details of [the victim] or the Defendant, or creates a material risk of harm." The order was granted "pending a further Motion to be filed by [the victim] and/or Defendant." The situation creates a quandary for the NFL. Will the league tell Jacobs he can't play until he asks for the video to be released? Or will the league welcome the reality that the video won't be seen by the general public? The situation conjures instant memories of the notorious Ray Rice video. The league didn't insist on seeing it. Then, TMZ obtained it. All hell broke loose for the NFL, with Rice's career ending and the Commissioner spending a week or so wondering whether he'd have to resign, after the Associated Press reported that the NFL had seen the video before it was published. Video changes everything . Knowing what happened is one thing; seeing it is another. Why else would Jacobs want it to be hidden from view? It will be interesting to see whether the league tries to force Jacobs to secure the video's release, or whether it shrugs at the fact that it's not available. For now, Jacobs is on paid leave. He'll remain there until the NFL determines the discipline to be imposed under the Personal Conduct Policy. How can it properly determine the discipline without seeing the video?
author: Mike Florio

title: Giants sign WR Dalen Cambre off of practice squad
summary: The Giants have added a pair of wide receivers to the roster for Sunday night's game against the Cowboys.
full_text: '' The Giants have added a pair of wide receivers to the roster for Sunday night's game against the Cowboys. They announced that they have signed Dalen Cambre to the active roster off of the practice squad and they have elevated Braxton Berrios on a temporary basis. No corresponding move was needed to add Cambre as the Giants never filled the roster spot they opened by releasing Darius Slayton this week. Cambre spent most of last season on the practice squad and appeared in one game. The two additions come with Malik Nabers listed as questionable to make his return to action after last season's torn ACL. The Giants are also elevating linebacker Malik Harrison. He and Berrios will return to the practice squad after the game.
author: Josh Alper

title: Vikings elevate Kyle Van Noy, DeeJay Dallas for Sunday
summary: Kyle Van Noy is set to make his Vikings debut on Sunday.
full_text: '' Kyle Van Noy is set to make his Vikings debut on Sunday. The team announced that they have elevated the veteran linebacker from the practice squad for their game against the Packers. Van Noy signed with the Vikings earlier this month. Van Noy has 57 career sacks and will give the team some experienced depth behind Dallas Turner and Andrew Van Ginkel in the season opener. The Vikings also elevated running back DeeJay Dallas on Saturday. He joins Aaron Jones, Jordan Mason, and sixth-round pick Demond Claiborne in the offensive backfield. Both players will revert back to the practice squad after the game.
author: Josh Alper

title: Eagles place second-round pick Eli Stowers on IR
summary: Eagles second-round pick Eli Stowers won't be making his regular season debut against the Commanders on Sunday.
full_text: Eagles second-round pick Eli Stowers won't be making his regular season debut against the Commanders on Sunday. Stowers was placed on injured reserve Saturday, so the earliest the tight end will be able to play is in Week 5. Stowers was listed as questionable due to a hamstring injury, but the team says that a quad injury is also part of the reason why he was placed on injured reserve. Grant Calcaterra is also on injured reserve, so the Eagles will have Dallas Goedert, Johnny Mundt, and E.J. Jenkins as their tight ends in the coming weeks. The Eagles elevated wide receiver Britain Covey from the practice squad. He'll revert back to that roster after Sunday's game.
author: Josh Alper

title: Cooper Rush is dealing with back spasms, Falcons still expect him to start Sunday
summary: The list of healthy Falcons quarterbacks keeps getting shorter.
full_text: '' The list of healthy Falcons quarterbacks keeps getting shorter. The team announced on Saturday that Cooper Rush is dealing with back spasms. Rush was installed as the Week 1 starter after Tua Tagovailoa was ruled out with the oblique injury he suffered during Thursday's practice and the Falcons say he is still expected to play against the Steelers. Michael Penix has been ruled out as he continues to recover from last season's torn ACL, so undrafted rookie Jack Strand is the only other available quarterback in Atlanta. The Falcons also announced that they have elevated linebacker Bralen Trice and tight end Nick Muse from the practice squad. Offensive tackle Cameron Williams was placed on injured reserve to round out Saturday's roster moves.
author: Josh Alper

title: With Joey Porter Jr.'s status unclear, Steelers elevate CB Doneiko Slaughter
summary: The Steelers aren't sure if Joey Porter Jr. will play against the Falcons on Sunday, so they have added some more help at cornerback.
full_text: The Steelers aren't sure if Joey Porter Jr. will play against the Falcons on Sunday, so they have added some more help at cornerback. Doneiko Slaughter has been elevated from the practice squad for Week 1. Slaughter was signed by the Jaguars after going undrafted in 2025 and signed a future contract with the Steelers in January. Porter is listed as questionable to play due to a back injury that limited him in practice all week. Porter is also looking for a contract extension and the Steelers have a policy that they won't negotiate after the season is underway, so there are multiple reasons for uncertainty about his Sunday status. An answer to Porter's availability will come no later than 90 minutes ahead of kickoff.
author: Josh Alper

title: Saints put RB Audric Estime on IR
summary: The Saints announced a few roster moves ahead of Sunday's opener against the Lions.
full_text: The Saints announced a few roster moves ahead of Sunday's opener against the Lions. Running back Audric Estime has been placed on injured reserve. He was ruled out on Friday with a thigh injury and will have to miss four games before he will become eligible to return to action. The Saints elevated running back C.J. Donaldson from the practice squad. Alvin Kamara is listed as questionable to play with a knee injury, so Donaldson may be joining Travis Etienne and Kendre Miller as the available backs for New Orleans. The Saints also elevated wide receiver Kevin Austin and signed tight end Treyton Welch to the active roster from the practice squad.
author: Josh Alper

title: Bears sign QB Miller Moss to practice squad, elevate him for Sunday's game
summary: The Bears listed backup quarterback Tyson Bagent as questionable for Sunday's game against the Panthers with a back injury and it looks like they're expecting him to be inactive.
full_text: The Bears listed backup quarterback Tyson Bagent as questionable for Sunday's game against the Panthers with a back injury and it looks like they're expecting him to be inactive. The team announced that they signed quarterback Miller Moss to the practice squad on Saturday and then elevated him for their season opener. Moss will have to be active on Sunday in order to be eligible to play because emergency third quarterbacks have to be on the active roster, although the Bears could just go with Case Keenum as the backup to Caleb Williams if Bagent is unavailable. The Bears also elevated wide receiver Kaden Davis from the practice squad. Both players were with the team during training camp and will revert to the practice squad after Sunday's game. Defensive back Keidron Smith was released from the practice squad to make room for Moss.
author: Josh Alper

title: Josh Simmons is ruled out for the Chiefs on Monday night
summary: Undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson will start at left tackle vs. the Broncos.
full_text: When Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes makes his return on Monday night after a December 2025 torn ACL, his left tackle will be an undrafted rookie. Josh Simmons, a first-round pick in 2025, has been ruled out for the game against the Broncos with a back injury. Kahlil Benson will start at left tackle in his first career game. Also out for the Chiefs will be defensive back Chamarri Conner, who has a knee injury. No other Chiefs player has an injury designation. Which means that Mahomes will indeed play. And that the Broncos will test Benson in an effort to get to Mahomes. The Chiefs, who finished 6-11 in 2025, are 2.5-point favorites against the Broncos, who won the division and secured the No. 1 seed in the AFC.
author: Mike Florio

title: Packers elevate WR Bo Melton, LB Kristian Welch
summary: Wide receiver Bo Melton lost his spot on the Packers' 53-man roster this week, but he'll be available for Sunday's game against the Vikings.
full_text: Wide receiver Bo Melton lost his spot on the Packers' 53-man roster this week, but he'll be available for Sunday's game against the Vikings. Melton re-signed to the Packers' practice squad after being released late in the week and the Packers announced that he has been elevated on a temporary basis for Week 1. Melton has appeared in 38 games for the Packers the last three seasons. He has 28 catches for 416 yards and two touchdowns in that action. The Packers have also elevated linebacker Kristian Welch. He played in eight games and recorded three tackles last season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Amon-Ra St. Brown needs only 33 catches for most ever through six NFL seasons
summary: Five years after entering the NFL as a fourth-round pick, Lions receiver Amon-Ra St.
full_text: Five years after entering the NFL as a fourth-round pick, Lions receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown won't need much time in his sixth season to make history. Again. St. Brown already has the record for the most catches by any player through five seasons, with 547. It's an average of 109.4 per season. And his production through five years will make it easy to set the record for the most catches through six seasons. Via NBC Sports research, St. Brown needs only 33 catches in 2026 to break the current record of 579, which was set last year by Vikings receiver Justin Jefferson. St. Brown is a four-time Pro Bowler, a two-time first-team All-Pro, and a one-time second-team All-Pro. Coupled with Jameson Williams, the Lions have one of the top one-two punches at the receiver position. Throw in running back Jahmyr Gibbs, and it truly is amazing that the Lions not only missed the playoffs in 2025 but also finished last in the NFC North. That should change in 2026, especially with the Lions getting the benefit of a fourth-place schedule. With the Bears drawing the Texans, Eagles, and Seahawks and the Packers getting the Jaguars, Cowboys, and Rams, the Lions will face the Titans, Giants, and Cardinals. In a division that had first place and fourth place separated by only two games, those three games could be all the difference the Lions need.
author: Mike Florio

title: Cowboys place RB Malik Davis on injured reserve
summary: As expected, Cowboys running back Malik Davis will miss some time with a hip injury suffered at practice on Friday.
full_text: As expected, Cowboys running back Malik Davis will miss some time with a hip injury suffered at practice on Friday. The team announced on Saturday that Davis has been placed on injured reserve. He'll be required to miss at least four games. Taking his spot on the active roster is running back Israel Abanikanda, who was signed from the practice squad. Abanikanda, a fifth-round pick of the Jets in 2023, first joined the Cowboys' practice squad last November. He spent all of the offseason, training camp, and preseason on the 90-man roster before being waived on August 30. Davis was undrafted in 2022. He has spent his entire career with the Cowboys. In 2025, he had 52 carries for 250 yards and two touchdowns. The other running back on the active roster (other than starter Javonte Williams) is Emari Demarcado, who was claimed off waivers after being released by the Chiefs on August 30. He's best known for dropping the ball early during what would have been a 72-yard touchdown run in a game the Cardinals were dominating against the Titans. Tennessee eventually won the game. The Cowboys visit the Giants on Sunday night.
author: Mike Florio

title: ESPN continues its not-so-subtle advocacy for the Protect College Sports Act
summary: I said it this week on PFT Live.
full_text: I said it this week on PFT Live . And I'll say it again now. Anyone who supports the Protect College Sports Act opposes player rights. Those who are speaking out in support of the bill won't admit it. We'll do it for them. Under the guise of ending chaos tracing to decades of antitrust violations that denied the players the ability to earn anything for their skills, sacrifices, and fame, the proponents of the bill want to limit the amount of money that goes to players, diverting it to the programs. That's the fundamental problem none of them will ever acknowledge. There are only so many dollars that can be siphoned from the piggybanks of the boosters. Every dollar that goes to an NIL fund is one less dollar that can go to the program. They want to reduce what can go to the players, maximizing what can go to the programs. Unwilling to embrace a nationwide union that would allow the creation of a salary cap, transfer limits, and other rules aimed at creating order, the powers-that-be crave an exemption from the laws that prevent the universities from coming together and crafting anticompetitive — and anticapitalist — restrictions on the players' earning power and freedom to transfer. And ESPN has been leading the conga line, with influential voices like Nick Saban and Pat McAfee openly pushing the Protect College Sports Act. On Saturday, ESPN gave Senator Ted Cruz (R-Texas), one of the sponsors of the bill, an extended interview during College GameDay to press the case for passage of the proposed law. Cruz, not surprisingly, opened by pointing to the LSU and Brendan Sorsby situations as evidence of the current chaos. The loud reaction to those specific situations was always about mustering political momentum to get the bill passed. Cruz also claimed that there currently is a "[s]piral of costs that is bankrupting almost every college program in the country. . . . They’re losing tens of millions of dollars." That contention, to use a technical term, is horseshit. There was no opposing viewpoint offered in response, other than the organic and incessant booing of Cruz (which included a one point a "Ted you suck!" chant). No time was provided for those who have concerns about the bill. At one point, host Rece Davis posed a perfunctory question to Cruz regarding the absence of limits on compensation and mobility for coaches and administrators. Cruz offered an evasive word salad in response, and he received no pushback. Contrary to what ESPN is leading its viewers to believe, the bill has real opposition. On Monday, Senator Chris Murphy (D-Conn.) will conduct a press conference at noon ET with "college athletes, professional athlete unions, families and advocates" to address the problems with the bill. From the email announcing the event, "participants will detail how the bill denies college athletes the rights and protections they are owed as workers and cuts off any path these athletes have to advocate for themselves — all so the NCAA, college athletic conferences and schools can consolidate money and power over athletes’ lives." Why wasn't Murphy given equal time on College GameDay ? Cruz and Murphy could have debated the merits and problems with the bill. While there are no safe bets in this age of bet! bet! bet! , it would be safe to wager the farm on ESPN not preempting McAfee's show and taking Murphy's press conference live as it happens on Monday.
author: Mike Florio

title: Inside the Michael Mayer deal
summary: Despite the presence of Brock Bowers, the Raiders have decided to keep tight end Michael Mayer — with an extension just before the first game of his contract year.
full_text: Despite the presence of Brock Bowers, the Raiders have decided to keep tight end Michael Mayer — with an extension just before the first game of his contract year. The details of the Mayer deal have emerged quickly. And it's a solid agreement, especially since he has a mere 783 receiving yards in his first three NFL seasons. Here are the full specifics, per a source with knowledge of the terms: 1. Signing bonus: $9 million. 2. 2026 base salary: $2.5 million, fully guaranteed. 3. 2026 per-game roster bonus: $10,000 ($170,000 total). 4. 2027 base salary: $11 million, fully guaranteed. 5. 2027 per-game roster bonus: $10,000 ($170,000 total). 6. 2028 base salary: $11.735 million, $7.5 million of which is guaranteed for injury at signing. It becomes fully guaranteed in March 2027. 7. 2028 per-game roster bonus: $10,000 ($170,000 total). 8. 2029 base salary: $12.105 million. 9. 2029 per-game roster bonus: $10,000 ($170,000 total). The three new years pay $45 million, an average of $15 million per year. From signing, it's a four-year, $47.02 million deal, with an average of $11.755 million. Mayer has $22.5 million fully guaranteed at signing. The full $30 million in guarantees will vest within six months. It puts him among the highest-paid tight ends in the league — and it will surely prompt plenty of other tight ends to call their agents. Listed behind Bowers on the depth chart, Mayer will enter the starting lineup during Bowers's short-term absence due to a recent knee surgery to trim his meniscus.

title: Colts downgrade LB Austin Ajiake to out, elevate one
summary: The Colts have made a couple of Saturday moves in advance of Sunday’s matchup against the Ravens.
full_text: The Colts have made a couple of Saturday moves in advance of Sunday’s matchup against the Ravens. Linebacker Austin Ajiake has been downgraded from questionable to out. He popped up on the injury report on Friday as a non-participant. Ajiake appeared in 16 games for Indianapolis last season, playing 70 percent of special teams snaps in those contests. Additionally, Indianapolis has elevated cornerback Kenneth Harris to the gameday roster from the practice squad. An undrafted rookie out of Oklahoma State, Harris will be making his pro debut.

title: Jaguars vs. Browns: Deshaun Watson makes first start in almost two years
summary: A look at where to watch the Week 1 matchup in Jacksonville, as well as the top storylines to follow
full_text:
Football season is here (finally), and we have a full slate of games over the course of four days this week to tune into. If you're like me, you're about to spend a lot of time yelling at the television, and I couldn't be happier to do so.
There are a lot of great games this week, and while Cleveland Browns vs. Jacksonville Jaguars may not immediately stand out as one of the top games to watch, I believe it's one you should tune in to ( here's why ). This game has all the drama and intrigue of new coaches, quarterback returns, on-edge fans and the potential for a major — yet unlikely — upset.
The Browns are entering their first year under head coach Todd Monken, while the Jags are in their second year under Liam Coen and need to prove last year's major season-to-season improvement wasn't a fluke. Their defense gave up the fewest points per game in the NFL in the last eight games, and quarterback Trevor Lawrence excelled during that time as well.
They're coming off an AFC South title; Trevor Lawrence was in the MVP conversation last year, and he put up some of his best numbers. They have Travis Hunter back and a solid overall team, and CBS Sports has them at 10-7 and in the playoff picture. Jacksonville hasn't made the playoffs in back-to-back seasons since 1998-99.
Now to the Browns. Cleveland's offseason has been nothing short of a soap opera.
Veteran Deshaun Watson came out on top of the quarterback competition , but not without some — or a lot of — criticism. Watson, who signed a historic five-year, $230 million fully guaranteed contract with the Browns in March 2022, has had a complicated, injury-plagued history with the team . Needless to say, Watson's journey with the Browns has not been a smooth one and fans have made it known they haven't been a fan of what they've seen on the field so far this summer.
After a rocky training camp and preseason, fans booed the 30-year-old. He responded by calling the fans' boos "personal" and "disrespectful," which the Dawg Pound did not take well and eventually led to an apology from Watson.
The team's other option at QB was Shedeur Sanders , who famously dropped to the fifth round in the 2025 NFL Draft after once being believed to be a first-rounder.
Watson's history of unpredictable and unreliable play means the chances of Sanders coming in at some point this season are good. With so much going on at quarterback, this game will be intriguing to watch. Will the Browns crumble like many think they will , or will Watson step up to the challenge and make his first game back one to remember?
I have to give this one to the Jaguars. If Jacksonville doesn't come up with a win here, after all the offseason and training camp dysfunction with the Browns, it'll be a surprising loss for Duval County. The Jaguars defense is strong, and the Browns offense is...well, not. This mismatch should mean the home team wins in front of their own fans.
The Browns have not been good against the spread on the road in the last two seasons, going an NFL-worst 4-13 ATS.
Pick: Jaguars 30, Browns 10
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: Colts vs. Ravens: Lamar Jackson and Daniel Jones lead teams in Week 1 matchup
summary: Lamar Jackson and Daniel Jones look to bounce back from injury-plagued seasons
full_text:
The NFL is back, and so, too, are Super Bowl expectations for the Baltimore Ravens . This time, though, things look a little different. The Jesse Minter era opens Sunday with a visit to the Indianapolis Colts , who are out to prove last season's strong start was no fluke.
Both teams feature quarterbacks hoping to bounce back from up-and-down 2025 seasons. Lamar Jackson struggled with injuries all year, and he rarely looked like himself. He had the highest sack rate of his career and averaged 26.8 rushing yards per game, less than half of his career average. The Ravens' stop-and-start season came to a sudden end when Tyler Loop missed a game-winning field goal attempt in Week 18 against the Steelers , sending Pittsburgh to the playoffs.
Daniel Jones , meanwhile, was playing the best football of his career by far—and some of the best football in the NFL, in fact—before a midseason leg fracture (he played through it) and, a few weeks later, a torn Achilles. Through 10 weeks, Jones led the NFL in passing yards and was fourth in yards per attempt. The Colts fell into disarray after the injuries, slipping from 8-2 to 8-9 and missing the postseason for the fifth straight year.
Both teams have several reasons to be optimistic they'll put their respective disappointing finishes in the past, and that starts Sunday. Here's what you need to know.
Lamar Jackson in a new offense: Each of the two times Jackson's changed offensive coordinators, he's won MVP. Can he make it three for three? Declan Doyle is only 30 and is calling plays for the first time, but he was the Bears ' offensive coordinator under Ben Johnson last year, and Jackson has drawn rave reviews from him. Expect more under-center play-action passes—an area Jackson has excelled—and other notable shifts in the approach.
Superstar running back meeting: Over the past five seasons, Derrick Henry and Jonathan Taylor rank first and second, respectively, in rushing yards. Sunday, they'll go head to head. Henry is coming off another monster statistical year—1,595 rushing yards, 16 rushing touchdowns—but he had some costly, uncharacteristic fumbles as well. Taylor was averaging 113.9 rushing yards per game through 10 weeks, but Jones' injury threw a wrench into things, and he averaged just 63.9 yards per game over the final seven contests. Still, 1,585 rushing yards and a league-high 18 rushing touchdowns is hardly anything to sneeze at.
Jesse Minter's impact on the defense: Minter will call defensive plays for Baltimore, which makes sense given he was excellent as the Chargers ' defensive coordinator the past two years. He should immediately help patch up a leaky pass defense. The Ravens allowed an NFL-high 64 passes of 20+ yards last year. Minter's Chargers allowed just 37, tied for second-fewest in the league.
By all accounts, Jones has looked outstanding, physically, even after such a major injury. That is crucial in Shane Steichen's offense. Jones' ability to throw on the run via play action and even scramble when needed finally allowed Steichen to run the ideal version of his offense. Adding Taylor into the mix made Indianapolis one of the NFL's most explosive offenses over the first half of the season. Defensively, the healthy returns of DeForest Buckner , Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward cannot be overstated.
But there's simply more talent in Baltimore, where Jackson is finally healthy again and the defense has plenty of individual talent, especially up front. The Colts' excellent offensive line against the Ravens' defensive front should be a terrific battle throughout. Minter's play calls should unlock the best version of Baltimore's secondary, too.
There will be some starts and stops for both offenses, but Henry should be in line for a monster day, and Indianapolis' linebackers could have some trouble against the run and the play-action pass. Minter's coaching debut is a winning one.
Pick: Ravens 23, Colts 20; UNDER 47.5
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Titans vs. Jets: Robert Saleh makes debut as Tennessee coach against team that fired him
summary: Saleh begins his tenure in Tennessee against his former team as both squads feature overhauled rosters and starting quarterbacks looking for a fresh start in Week 1
full_text:
One of the most competitive games during Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season might be Sunday's showdown between the New York Jets and the Tennessee Titans .
Both teams have tangible reasons to believe that they will make significant jumps this season following disappointing 2025 campaigns. The Titans are being led by new coach Robert Saleh and new offensive coordinator/former Giants head coach Brian Daboll. The Jets are entering their second season under Aaron Glenn, whose first season at the helm included upset wins over the Bengals and Falcons .
Sunday will mark Saleh's first game against the Jets as an opposing head coach. Saleh served as the Jets' coach from 2021-24. After going 4-13 in his first season, Saleh guided the Jets to consecutive 7-10 campaigns and was fired just five games into the 2024 season with the Jets sitting at 2-3.
While the Jets didn't have much success under his watch, it's worth noting that Saleh inherited a mess. He was also dealt a bad hand when Aaron Rodgers sustained a season-ending injury just minutes into the 2023 season. The Jets still managed to win seven games that season and were just a game under .500 the following season before he was let go.
After a season back as the 49ers ' defensive coordinator, Saleh is getting a second chance to lead an NFL team . He'd surely love to get it started with a win over his former employer.
One of the things that makes this game interesting is all the new faces on both sides. The Titans and Jets have nine and eight new starters, respectively.
Tennessee invested heavily in free agency with the acquisitions of former Jets pass rusher Jermaine Johnson II , wideout Wan'Dale Robinson and center Austin Schlottmann , among others. The Titans' starting defense includes five players who weren't on the team in 2025. That doesn't include first-round pick Keldric Faulk and second-round pick Anthony Hill Jr .
The Titans also made a concerted effort this offseason to improve the situation surrounding quarterback Cam Ward , who was sacked a league-high 55 times during his rookie season. They spent their first-round pick on Carnell Tate , who is hoping to join the long list of former Ohio State receivers who went on to enjoy successful NFL careers. Tennessee also drafted two offensive linemen, including new starting right guard Fernando Carmona .
The Jets had even more roster turnover, especially on defense, with the addition of 11 new players and six new starters, which include former All-Pro safety Minkah Fitzpatrick and EDGE David Bailey , the No. 2 overall pick.
The Jets made fewer but equally impactful additions to their offense. They spent two first-round picks on pass-catchers in former Indiana tight end Kenyon Sadiq and former Hoosiers wideout Omar Cooper Jr . They also re-signed Geno Smith , a former Pro Bowler who is looking to return to form following a disappointing season in Las Vegas.
Whenever a game is evenly matched, as this one appears to be, it often comes down to quarterback play. While neither quarterback was very good last year, Smith's overall body of work is hard to ignore. If Smith does his part on Sunday, it should be enough for the Jets to win what should be a competitive Week 1 game.
Pick: Jets +1.5 ; Under 38.5
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Bills vs. Texans: Houston seeks fifth consecutive home win over Josh Allen in 2026 season opener
summary: Buffalo has to buck a recent trend in order to start the season in the win column
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills are no stranger to the Lone Star State. For the third consecutive year, the Bills hit the road to square off against the Houston Texans , but history is not on their side in this Week 1 clash between reigning postseason teams. Each of their last four trips to Houston ended in defeat.
Can the Texans keep their home dominance against the Bills rolling? There is plenty of reason to believe that DeMeco Ryans ' crew can open their 2026 campaign with yet another win over the perennial AFC title contenders. Their overwhelming defense has been a problem for Buffalo ever since Ryans took the job, and a few personnel changes on offense suggest the offense can keep pace with the unit on the other side of the ball.
The side that comes away victorious from this marquee opener will start the year with one of the NFL's most impressive early-season wins. To defeat a fellow Super Bowl hopeful right out of the gate is exactly how these teams can assert themselves as top-flight candidates to run the conference.
Not only did the Texans extend their reign of dominance over the Bills the last time these teams met in Houston, but they also did so with a backup quarterback at the helm. If Stroud can be at least as effective as Davis Mills was in the 23-19 victory last November, then the blueprint exists for this to turn into a season-opening win. Buffalo surrendered eight sacks and three turnovers in that contest, and nearly the exact same offense rolls into town in 2026. New wide receiver DJ Moore cannot right that many wrongs.

title: Prisco's Week 1 NFL picks: Bills end skid vs. Texans, Packers edge Vikings
summary: Pete Prisco reveals all of his season-opening picks, including a healthy dose of Patrick Mahomes in a win over the Broncos
full_text:
It's NFL picks time again, which means Week 1 torture.
Figuring out Week 1 picks is as complicated as it gets. We have no idea who will be good and who will be bad. How will new coaches impact teams? How will returning injured players show in their first game back?
That makes picking this week's games even tougher than other weeks.
I had a good season in 2025, so let's see if that can carry over this year. The way I see it, if you can navigate the early weeks and settle in for October and November, you have a chance at a good season.
So let's start strong -- even in the face of Week 1 adversity.
All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET
The Falcons have quarterback issues with Tua Tagovailoa named the starter. The Steelers are trotting out Aaron Rodgers for the start of his final season. With the Falcons having their two top pass rushers down, this will be a chance for Rodgers to start the season right. The Pittsburgh defense will do the rest. Steelers take it.
Pick: Steelers 27, Falcons 17
The Ravens and first-year coach Jesse Minter face a tough road game to open the season. Lamar Jackson and the new-look offense will have success here on the fast track. The Colts won't be able to match that. Look for a lot of points in this one with Jackson winning it.
The Bills have lost the last six meetings in Houston against the Texans . Josh Allen hasn't been himself against that defense either. But this Bills team will be much more aggressive. That will help against that vaunted Houston front. On other side, the Bills will attack C.J. Stroud , which will lead to turnovers. The Bills take it.
Caleb Williams and the Chicago offense should be ready to make big strides this season, starting in this one. The problem is the Chicago defense has issues. But I think that defense will play well enough to find a way to win against Bryce Young . Bears take it on the road.
Pick: Bears 29, Panthers 21
The Browns come to Jacksonville with Deshaun Watson as the starting quarterback. That will be an issue against an improved Jacksonville defense. The Cleveland defense should be solid this year, but Trevor Lawrence and the Jaguars ' passing game should have a big day here. Jaguars big as they get off to a good offensive start.
Pick: Jaguars 30, Browns 13
The Saints and second-year quarterback Tyler Shough will be an improved team this season, but this is a tough way to open. The Lions have a dynamic offense and the venue will make it a challenge. Look for Jared Goff and the Detroit offense to have a big day. The Saints won't keep up. Lions big.
This game features two teams that need to get off to good starts to try and gain some confidence. The Jets will be facing former coach Robert Saleh here. But this game will be about the Jets' defense against Cam Ward . I think the Jets' defense gets the best of him. Jets take it.
This is a tough road game to open the season for the Bucs. They have some injury issues at receiver that could be in play for Baker Mayfield against an improved Bengals defense. Joe Burrow and the Bengals' passing game will face an improved Tampa Bay pass rush. In the end, the Bengals will find a way to win a close one.
Pick: Bengals 29, Buccaneers 28
The Chargers ' new-look offense under Mike McDaniel will be unleashed here against the Cardinals . It should be run heavy, which will help Justin Herbert with some big play-action shots. The Cardinals will counter with Jacoby Brissett at quarterback. This has the look of a blowout.
Pick: Chargers 31, Cardinals 14
This will come down to how well the Packers handle all those Brian Flores pressure looks on defense for Minnesota. That's a challenge on the road. But Jordan Love has been good against the blitz in his career. That matters. The Green Bay defense will manufacture enough pressure -- without Micah Parsons -- to slow down Kyler Murray . Packers win it.
Pick: Packers 26, Vikings 24
This is a game featuring two teams that likely won't be doing a lot this season, so this is a chance to steal a win for both. The Raiders will start Kirk Cousins at home, while Malik Willis makes his first start for the Dolphins . I think this will be close, but the Raiders will win it late.
Pick: Raiders 21, Dolphins 17
The Commanders come into this one with offensive line issues, which is never a good thing against the Eagles ' defense, especially on the road. The Eagles had offensive issues last year, but this will be a game to get them going again like the Super Bowl season two years ago. Look for the Eagles to win thanks to the defense.
Pick: Eagles 30, Commanders 21
The Cowboys have retooled a defense that badly needed it, which will present a tough challenge for Jaxson Dart . On the other side, the Cowboys' offense should be able to have success against the Giants ' defense if they block them. I think they do, even without talented guard Tyler Smith . Cowboys win it.
Pick: Cowboys 30, Giants 17
This will be Patrick Mahomes in his first start since tearing his ACL. How limited will he be? It won't help he's facing one of the best defenses in the league. The Chiefs will counter with a young defense that will try and slow down a good Denver offense. At home, I think they do it. Mahomes wins it late.
Pick: Chiefs 20, Broncos 17

title: NFL anytime TD best bets: Our favorite picks for Week 1, including Emeka Egbuka
summary: Five anytime touchdown bets to consider for Week 1
full_text:
We are back! The first NFL Sunday of the year is here, and it's time to shift our attention from our loved ones to our sports betting apps. There are plenty of ways to win or lose money when it comes to betting on the NFL, but one of the most popular options has become anytime touchdown scorers.
One reason is that the odds are juicier. If you're a Los Angeles Chargers fan and think Keaton Mitchell is going to be Mike McDaniel's De'Von Achane , maybe you'll take a flier on him to find the end zone at +340. If you think rookie running back Jeremiyah Love scores a touchdown in his first NFL game, +205 doesn't seem like a bad bet. Maybe Kyler Murray runs in a touchdown in his first game with the Minnesota Vikings . He's listed at +275.
Below, we will break down five anytime TD bets to consider for Week 1. These will not be predictable choices like a Bijan Robinson or Jahmyr Gibbs score that offer zero value, but they won't be wild long-shots such as a team defense. Let's begin with a wide receiver that dominated right off the bat as a rookie last year.
Odds courtesy of FanDuel Sportsbook .
There's no more Mike Evans in Tampa, and I'm expecting second-year wide receiver Emeka Egbuka to play a major role in Baker Mayfield's offense. The Ohio State product started off his rookie season hot, catching 25 passes for 445 yards and five touchdowns in his first five games of the year. He can get off to a similar start in 2026 against a Cincinnati Bengals defense that still has a few questions to answer.
Check out this insane stat I discovered: Saquon Barkley has scored at least one touchdown in EIGHT STRAIGHT meetings vs. Washington!
I've seen Barkley anytime TD listings around -200 in the past, so getting him at -115 almost qualifies as "value." The Philadelphia Eagles are debuting a new-look offense on Sunday, but expect Barkley to still be an important piece of this attack as both a runner and receiver. Plus, don't forget that the Washington Commanders had what was statistically the worst defense in the NFL last year, allowing 384 yards of total offense per game. I don't bet on first touchdown scorers, but Barkley at +500 is definitely an option to consider as well.
Lamar Jackson's disappointing 2025 campaign was headlined by a hamstring injury that held him back even when he returned to the lineup. His 349 yards rushing marked a career low, as did his two rushing touchdowns. Jackson is now finally healthy and ready to take off. The Indianapolis Colts don't have one of the best defensive lines in the NFL, but with three new starters on the interior of his offensive line, Jackson is probably going to have to get out of the pocket and scramble.
Believe it or not, Jackson is statistically the best Week 1 quarterback in NFL history. The Baltimore Ravens average 33.3 points per game in Week 1s with Jackson starting, so I'm expecting some touchdowns in Indy this Sunday.
Quentin Johnston has now put together back-to-back seasons with 700 yards receiving and eight touchdowns despite the slow start to his NFL career, and the Chargers now have Mike McDaniel at offensive coordinator. I'm not saying Johnston is Tyreek Hill, but could the tall speedster play that kind of role in this new-look offense when it comes to the deep shots? That's what I started thinking about when he caught this 65-yard touchdown from Justin Herbert with the first-team offense in the preseason.
Justin Herbet LAUNCHES it to Quentin Johnston for a 65-yard TD 🎯 Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/h1wr48fiC4
I said no long shots, but I'll pull them out for special occasions. The Jacksonville Jaguars are hosting the Cleveland Browns in Week 1 -- the franchise that traded down in the 2025 NFL Draft to allow the Jags to draft who James Gladstone believes is a generational player.
Travis Hunter is expected to play more cornerback this year, but that doesn't mean he's going to see zero reps on offense. With the Browns in town, I think Liam Coen is going to draw up something interesting for the former No. 2 overall pick in the red zone. Sort of like a, "Hey, we won this trade. Mason Graham can't do that!"
I mean, +950 seems like a decent value. I'm not sure I'd recommend this if it were +400.

full_text:
You know what? Take a second and pat yourself on the back. Why? Because you deserve it. You've waited months for this moment, and it's finally here: the first Sunday of the 2026 regular season.
Sure, you've already dabbled in a couple of games with the Seahawks-Patriots and Rams-49ers playing during the week, but this is different. You're not getting off work; you don't have homework to do the next day. All you have to do is sit on the couch and watch hours of football. It's one of the more beautiful things you can do in this life, so let's relish in the fact that we have an entire season to look forward to, and it truly gets moving right now.
Of course, you live a hectic life, so when you do finally get to sit down and take in the NFL, you may not have the time to do the research to confidently wager on a few contests. Well, we're here to help. Below, you can find our last-minute bets for every game remaining on the Week 1 slate, which includes a breakdown of five games we consider to be our best bets.
All NFL odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook .
Whenever you have a quarterback battle in training camp, you want to enter Week 1 with a firm decision and the confidence that the player selected can get the job done. Does anyone feel confident in Deshaun Watson's ability to keep the offense afloat? Watson didn't look particularly sharp this summer, but beat out Shedeur Sanders anyway, and now he'll face a Jaguars defense that really came on strong down the stretch in 2025, which helped them cover their final eight regular-season games, en route to a league-best 12-5 ATS record.
While Cleveland has a new coach in Todd Monken, the franchise has historically been terrible against the spread on the road over the last two seasons. In that time, they are 4-13 ATS, which ranks as the worst record in the NFL.
I think Cleveland has some solid pieces on the defensive side of the ball, but Trevor Lawrence entering his second year under Liam Coen could make the Jacksonville offense even more high-powered than it was a year ago. If they build up a lead and force Watson into a pass-heavy game script, Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker could feast.
Projected score: Jaguars 30, Browns 17 The pick: Jaguars -8.5
The Laremy Tunsil injury (torn triceps on Aug. 8) was a gut punch to the Commanders, who are hoping to rebound after a disappointing 2025 season that was marred by injury. It looms large in this matchup against Philadelphia, particularly if Jonathan Greenard (who has been dealing with the pec injury) is able to go. When you pair protection issues with a defense that may need a few weeks to fit their new pieces ( Odafe Oweh , K'Lavon Chaisson , and Sonny Styles ) in, there's the possibility that things could get out of hand for Washington as they step into Lincoln Financial Field.
On top of that, Jayden Daniels is 1-7 ATS in his last eight road starts.
The Eagles have routinely started the year off on a strong note, winning five straight Week 1 games entering 2026. They are also 9-1 in their past 10 Week 1 contests. Sure, Philadelphia is dealing with its own set of changes, transitioning to a new offense under OC Sean Mannion and working without A.J. Brown (traded to New England), but this is still a potent group. Most importantly, the offensive line is healthy, which I believe was a key reason for their downfall at the end of last season.
Projected score: Eagles 30, Commanders 20 The pick: Eagles -6
I simply don't understand how the books are assessing the Broncos. They are currently looking up at the Chiefs and Chargers to win the AFC West, despite reaching the AFC Championship a year ago. Had it not been for Bo Nix suffering a fractured ankle that booted him from the title game, they could've reached the Super Bowl. To me, they are the most complete team in the division after bringing everyone back from last year, getting Nix healthy, and adding Jayden Waddle to the receiver room.
Something tells me they'll remind the league of their ceiling with a statement road win in Week 1 on the Monday Night Football stage.
I also have some serious questions about the Chiefs. Patrick Mahomes is returning from a torn ACL and LCL he sustained in Week 15, and I wonder whether his escapability will be where it needs to be, given the shakiness of the offensive line. Specifically, left tackle Josh Simmons is dealing with a back injury, while right tackle Jaylon Moore gave up three sacks and 23 pressures last year despite playing just 42% of the offensive snaps in spot appearances. If Simmons is out, Moore would likely swing to left tackle, which would then elevate undrafted free agent Kahlil Benson to right tackle.
So, if you're scoring at home, Kansas City is starting a quarterback who could have limited mobility in his first game back from a season-ending knee injury and is playing behind an offensive line with clear issues at both starting tackle spots, and they are facing a Broncos defense that has piled up 131 sacks over the last two seasons. That might tell the entire story right there.
Projected score: Broncos 24, Chiefs 20 The pick: Broncos +2.5
I believe DJ Moore being added to the Bills offense will do wonders for Josh Allen this season, but that won't happen in Week 1. I love the Texans as a home dog because they are well-equipped to slow down Buffalo's key offensive pieces. Houston allowed just 17.4 points per game last season (second-fewest in the NFL) and 277.2 yards per game (fewest). Derek Stingley Jr . should help slow down the Bills passing attack; rookie defensive tackle Kayden McDonald could be a key piece against the run; and, of course, you have Will Anderson Jr . and Danielle Hunter both screaming off the edge. That's a lot for Josh Allen to deal with, and Houston has played him well recently.
In his career, Allen is 0-4 on the road against the Texans. In those games, his teams have averaged 17.8 points per game, and he's completed just 52.8% of his passes. Over the past two seasons (no matter the location), here's how Allen has fared against Houston compared to the rest of the league.
All the Texans need from the offense is for C.J. Stroud to protect the football. And they might be able to do that with a stable running game after acquiring David Montgomery this offseason. Buffalo struggled mightily against the run in 2025 and didn't do much this offseason to fix that deficiency. If Houston can get it going on the ground, that should help Stroud immensely in this upset attempt.
Projected score: Texans 26, Bills 23 The pick: Texans +1.5
When you look at the Over/Under win totals for the season, you'll find that the Titans sit at 6.5 and the Jets are at 5.5. Both teams need this game to reach their over, and I think Tennessee will be the one swimming upstream by the end of Sunday afternoon. I don't think New York will make many waves this season, but they are far more talented than they were a year ago on both sides of the ball.  For instance, they ranked last in the NFL with 140.3 passing yards per game. Geno Smith won't be mistaken for an elite quarterback, but he'll improve that figure, especially with a strong offensive line in front of him and some intriguing skill position players like Garrett Wilson and Breece Hall at his disposal.
They also added many veterans to their defense, including linebacker Demario Davis and safety Minkah Fitzpatrick . That's not to mention edge rusher David Bailey , who was the No. 2 pick in the draft.
Tennessee made moves this offseason as well, hiring Robert Saleh as head coach, bringing in Brian Daboll as OC, and adding a slew of veterans on both sides of the ball. The big X-factor will be Cam Ward , who didn't look great this preseason. I think it might take a little longer for the Titans' pieces to come together, which could allow the Jets to surprisingly start the year 1-0.
Projected score: Jets 24, Titans 20 The pick: Jets +1.5

title: Giants vs. Cowboys: NFC East rivals square off on 'Sunday Night Football' in John Harbaugh's debut
summary: The league kicks off the first Sunday night of the season with a familiar matchup that now has plenty of new faces
full_text:
Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season is finally here, and the first "Sunday Night Football" matchup of the year is a familiar one: the Dallas Cowboys at the New York Giants.
This will be the two NFC East rivals' ninth Week 1 meeting across the last 20 seasons, the most common Week 1 meeting between two teams in that span. That stretch includes seven primetime games and six Sunday night matchups. Dallas is a perfect 8-0 all-time in Week 1 primetime games against the Giants, which includes winning the last two by a combined score of 59-3, thanks in large part to a 40-0 beatdown at MetLife Stadium in 2023.
The 2026 edition of this matchup could be different, perhaps because so much has changed for both squads in terms of both coaching staffs and personnel.
Before we dive into some of the key storylines, here is how you can watch the first "Sunday Night Football" matchup of 2026.
The Cowboys were the NFL's worst scoring defense in 2025 , surrendering 30.1 points per game. That's why owner/general manager Jerry Jones and head coach Brian Schottenheimer completely overhauled their defense from the top down. Matt Eberflus was sent packing after just one season, and the Cowboys hired Christian Parker away from Vic Fangio's Philadelphia Eagles defensive staff to rebuild their unit. Parker drastically changed how play calls are communicated on top of turning over essentially half of the defensive personnel. Nearly half, 46.2%, of the snaps taken on the Cowboys' 2025 defense are by players no longer on the team, per the Dallas Morning News .
The new player acquisitions include Pro Bowl edge rusher Rashan Gary , first-round rookies Caleb Downs and Malachi Lawrence , Super Bowl 50 MVP edge rusher Von Miller and the San Francisco 49ers' 2025 tackles leader in Dee Winters (101).
"The growth, it's like night and day. Starting in OTAs, and starting the first week of training camp, getting a chance to go against one of the best offenses in battle every single day has helped us tremendously," Cowboys Pro Bowl defensive tackle Quinnen Williams said. "The mindset coming from the coaches, top down to the players and to the leadership, has been drastically changed. It's just fun, man. I just can't wait to see the process and the results from all the hard work. But, we're not done yet."
The New York Giants have a Super Bowl champion head coach for the first time since Tom Coughlin's last season in 2015 after hiring longtime Baltimore Ravens boss John Harbaugh. He built the team in his image this offseason with a few players from his Ravens days -- fullback Patrick Ricard, tight end Isaiah Likely, punter Jordan Stout -- while reinforcing the front lines of both lines of scrimmage by drafting linebacker Arvell Reese (fifth overall) and offensive lineman Francis Mauigoa (10th overall) in the top 10.
"Yeah, tough. Yeah, tough. He's obviously coached a lot of winning teams. So to me, you expect the game to go into the fourth quarter and it's kind of our message," Cowboys Pro Bowl quarterback Dak Prescott said of Harbaugh. "You can't win it in those first three, so be ready and do whatever it takes to go get it in the fourth. And anytime you're playing a good coach like that and his winning history, you've got to be ready for it."
The Giants' selection of Mauigoa 10th overall led to Ohio State Buckeyes All-American safety Caleb Downs falling to Dallas at No. 11. Since his selection, everyone in the building has raved about Downs' development.
"Man, [I] probably sound like a broken record. The way he prepares, the way he practices is not like, I don't want to say any. It's not like most rookies I've been around. It's different," Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said. "There's a different mindset. There's a different competitive fire in this kid. He craves coaching. He cannot get coached enough. And I think at the end of the day, that's why he's such a good player. I think you look at him and just the way he's always played the game, he plays it with instincts. ... He works his butt off at studying the X's and the O's part of it. So unique young man, very special talent."
Pro Bowl wide receiver CeeDee Lamb, one of Dallas' biggest stars who is accustomed to the massive weight of expectations that come with being a Cowboy, is just as confident in Downs' ability to thrive.
"Just getting confident, man. He's just getting confident within himself," Lamb said. "As you can see, we started in the spring. Just been battling him ever since. The first words that I told him when I saw him was, 'Let's work. I know what I expect of you. I know what I expect of myself and I know what you expect of yourself. So they got you in this position.' We drafted you first round, and I know everything that, all the pressure that he's feeling, I felt and I have no doubt that he's going to go out there and ride."
New York's top playmaker may or may not play on Sunday night despite practicing fully every day this week. The Giants still listed Nabers as officially questionable because the Pro Bowler may or may not be fully comfortable returning from the torn ACL he suffered last season.
"I've been wanting to play for so long now, but at the end of the day, I can't put my career at risk," Nabers said. "I gotta take that into account. There's a lot of football that I still have left to play. Making a split decision on when do I think I'm able to go out there and perform rather than just going out there -- I think the coaches know that, I know that I have a lot more football to play. So just being conscious of making sure I'm at the right standpoint of going back out there."
Nabers' status will significantly tilt the outcome. If he's not playing, Dallas could dominate New York in a big way. If he plays on a pitch count, the Cowboys would still have a pretty sizable edge. Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott lights up when he faces the Giants, winning 14 of his 17 starts against them, including 14 consecutive games that he has started AND finished. Prescott, Lamb and the explosive George Pickens cook New York's inconsistent cornerbacks early and often, per usual, while Dallas' defense limits the damage Jaxson Dart can do with his dual threat abilities.
