title: NFL Week 1 picks: Experts face off Bills at Texans, Packers-Vikings and more
summary: CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games
full_text:
Welcome to the 2026 NFL season, and our league overlords have put together quite the opening slate of games for us to enjoy. The Super Bowl rematch on Wednesday night saw the Seattle Seahawks hand the New England Patriots another loss, while we have football in Australia on Thursday night between the San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams , and then a whopping 13 games on Sunday.
Josh Allen has to open up the season against a scary Houston defense, Lamar Jackson and Daniel Jones face off in Indy, we get an NFC North matchup right off the bat between the Green Bay Packers and Minnesota Vikings , and an AFC West showdown on "Monday Night Football" between Patrick Mahomes and Bo Nix . So, which teams should you pick in Week 1, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Sept. 7 over at DraftKings Sportsbook.
Dajani ( Ravens -3.5): A home dog at 3.5 points sings to me like the sirens to Odysseus, but I'm afraid something has tied me to the ship's mast. For one, the Ravens average 33.3 points per game in Week 1 with Lamar Jackson starting. The two-time NFL MVP has averaged the most yards per attempt (9.1) and registered the highest passer rating (120.1) in Week 1 starts since 1970. Furthermore, I have questions about the Indianapolis Colts . Daniel Jones is coming off a torn Achilles, and his new WR1, Alec Pierce, missed most of the offseason work due to ankle surgery. Jonathan Taylor will be ready to rock, but will this passing game sputter against a Jesse Minter-led defense?  … Prediction : Ravens 27, Colts 23
Dubin (Ravens -3.5): I'm extraordinarily high on the Ravens this year, and comparatively low on the Colts. With Lamar Jackson back at full health, I expect the Ravens to be one of the best teams in the AFC. They always are whenever he makes it through a full season. Their defense should be improved this year with Jesse Minter at the helm, as well. Meanwhile, Jordan mentioned the various injury issues that could hold the Colts back early in the year. It all adds up to a big Ravens win. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Colts 14
Dajani ( Buccaneers +3.5): My logic here is simple. The Buccaneers have won and covered in Week 1 games over four straight seasons, which is the longest active streak in the NFL. The Cincinnati Bengals, on the other hand, are 1-5 against the spread in Week 1 when Joe Burrow starts. It's weird, the Bengals barely beat the Cleveland Browns last year (17-16), lost to Jerod Mayo 's Patriots in 2024, and fell to the Browns in Cleveland, 24-3, in 2023. Meanwhile, the dark cloud that was Baker Mayfield 's future has lifted thanks to a three-year extension. Vibes are high for the Bucs this week.  … Prediction: Bengals 21, Buccaneers 20
Dubin (Bengals -3.5): I know the Bengals always start the season slow. And I know that picking them early in the season always leads to regret. But I like this matchup for them offensively, and I think their defense will be improved after they drop Dexter Lawrence into the middle of the defensive line. With the Bucs having Emeka Egbuka coming off a toe injury that kept him out for a bunch of camp, I don't think they keep pace with Cincinnati in the opener.  … Prediction: Bengals 27, Buccaneers 21
Dajani (Vikings -1.5): Full disclosure, I don't understand why people are relatively high on the Packers this year. Their most reliable wide receiver left in free agency, their star running back is on the commissioner's exempt list, their star pass rusher is on the PUP list, and the offensive line has some question marks. We'll see how Kyler Murray fares in his first start with the Vikings, but he has the backing of some great playmakers, plus what was a top-three defense last year. To be honest, this line just confuses me. Vikings win … Prediction: Vikings 22, Packers 16
Dubin (Packers +1.5): I'm pretty lukewarm on both of these teams this year, but I like Green Bay's chances to get off to a hot start offensively in this matchup. This is going to need to be Brian Flores' best coaching job in recent memory, because the defensive personnel on hand is not what it once was. I can see Jordan Love putting on a fireworks show here in the opener, winning a shootout against an also-improved Vikings offense with Kyler Murray replacing J.J. McCarthy .  … Prediction: Packers 30, Vikings 27
Dajani ( Cowboys -3): The Cowboys are 8-0 all-time in Week 1 primetime games against the New York Giants . The last one came in 2023, when I tried to back Daniel Jones and Saquon Barkley . They lost, 40-0. Yes, the Giants have reasons for optimism with John Harbaugh and Jaxson Dart , but I have much more optimism when it comes to the Cowboys. I even have them winning the division! We all know about Dak Prescott 's offense with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens , but I think the defense is going to be improved. Caleb Downs is going to win Defensive Rookie of the Year, then the other additions of Rashan Gary , Dee Winters , Cobie Durant and Malachi Lawrence will make their impacts as well. Maybe Malik Nabers is fully healed and Dart is actually a franchise quarterback, but I'm going to back the Cowboys here under the lights of the Meadowlands  … Prediction: Cowboys 28, Giants 23
Dubin (Cowboys -3): I never get sucked into the Cowboys. I always maintain that they're going to be an unserious team. I'm a Cowboys fan, so I know exactly how unserious they've been for 30-plus years now. And yet... I can't help myself this year. I'm in on this Dallas team, with one of the most explosive offenses in the NFL backed by what should be an improved defense coordinated by Christian Parker. I'm comparatively low on the Giants, who have multiple key offensive players coming back from injury in a unit led by Matt Nagy, Greg Roman and Brian Callahan, which isn't exactly a murderer's row of a coaching staff.  … Prediction: Cowboys 31, Giants 20
Dajani ( Broncos +3): It's very cool that Patrick Mahomes worked so hard to be ready for the season opener after tearing his ACL in December, and his reward for doing so is having to face one of the best defenses in the NFL that ranked top three in points per game (18.3), yards per game (278.2) and third down percentage (33.8%) last year. Denver has registered 131 sacks over the past two seasons, 33 more than any other team, and will attempt to tee off against a quarterback that probably doesn't have the same mobility he did prior to his injury. It also appears that undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson will start at one of the tackle spots for the Kansas City Chiefs , which is very scary. The Broncos are 7-2 against the spread in their last nine games against the Chiefs, so I'm eyeing an upset here to close out Week 1 … Prediction: Broncos 17, Chiefs 14
Dubin (Broncos +3): I'm excited to see what Patrick Mahomes looks like in his first game back from injury, but something tells me it could be tough sledding against one of the best defenses in the NFL. I think the Chiefs will have to lean into their Kenneth Walker III-led running game, and it remains to be seen how effective that attack will be. I'm not the biggest Bo Nix fan in the world, but the Broncos offense has undeniably been effective with him at the helm, and I think they have enough to get it done against the Chiefs in Week 1.  … Prediction: Broncos 21, Chiefs 20
Dajani (Rams -3.5): This matchup is much more than just two rival contenders kicking off the season in the land down under. You need to know that this game features two international juggernauts. The 49ers are 3-1 in games outside the United States, having won their last three, while the Rams have also won three straight international games, boasting a +25.0 points-per-game differential in those wins!
Honestly, I'm not expecting fireworks in this star-studded matchup. But I'm leaning towards the favorites. George Kittle is attempting to play after tearing his Achilles…

title: Tucker Kraft, Michael Mayer join highest-paid tight ends with contract extensions
summary: Kraft and Mayer came to terms with their teams just over 24 hours out from their season openers
full_text:
Negotiations between the Green Bay Packers and tight end Tucker Kraft went down to the wire, but the sides agreed on a contract extension just in time for the start of the 2026 season. Kraft will sign a four-year, $75 million extension to become the NFL's third-highest-paid tight end on a per-year basis, according to ESPN.
The contract carries an average annual value of $18.75 million, which ranks just behind that of San Francisco 49ers star George Kittle and Arizona Cardinals standout Trey McBride . Incentives can make the deal worth up to $92 million, and it comes with a $26.5 million signing bonus.
Kraft has been among the most pleasant surprises from the middle rounds of the 2023 NFL Draft class. The third-rounder made an impact as a rookie but fully broke out in his second year when he became an every-week starter and amassed 707 receiving yards and seven touchdowns. A torn ACL cut his 2025 campaign short after just eight games, but he was well on his way to setting new career highs in every category, as he was on pace for more than 60 catches, 1,000 yards and 12 touchdowns.
The torrid start to Kraft's career places him in rare company. He joined Rob Gronkowski and Mark Andrews as just the third tight end this century to tally 100 catches, 1,500 receiving yards and 15 touchdowns over his first three NFL seasons.
Kraft joins a slew of players the Packers have taken care of contractually this offseason. Green Bay extended wide receiver Christian Watson (four years, $92 million deal), wide receiver Jayden Reed (three years, $50.25 million) and defensive tackle Devonte Wyatt (three years, $54.9 million) as well. It is clear general manager Brian Gutekunst feels his young nucleus has what it takes to make a leap toward Super Bowl contention as they continue to develop around quarterback Jordan Love and All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons .
Why did Green Bay prioritize getting a deal done with Kraft before he could fully show what he can do fresh off a torn ACL?
They did so because Kraft began showing signs of evolving into one of the league's best prior to his injury. Among his statistical achievements was the averaging of whopping 9.1 yards after catch per reception in 2025, the most among tight ends in the last 15 seasons, minimum 100 catches. San Francisco 49ers All-Pro George Kittle is the next closest player in this metric with a 6.9 yards after catch per reception average.
Saturday was a great day to be a high-performing tight end. Moments after Kraft secured his extension, the Las Vegas Raiders agreed to terms with Michael Mayer on a deal of his own. The team announced a multi-year extension with the 2023 second-round draft pick which, according to ESPN/NFL Media , covers three years and is worth $45 million with $30 million guaranteed.
While Mayer is only the No. 2 tight end on the Raiders' roster behind Brock Bowers , the $15 million average annual value is the fourth-largest at the position. It is also the biggest three-year deal for a tight end in NFL history. He is set to take on a sizable workload over the first few weeks of the season while Bowers recovers from a meniscus trim , which he underwent on Tuesday.
Mayer is more than capable of keeping the Raiders' offense afloat while Bowers is on the mend. He already has 32 starts under his belt and boasts 83 career receptions for 788 yards and three touchdowns, and a meaningful amount of that production came last year when Bowers missed five games with knee issues.
There was some thought that Kraft could reset the tight end market when he eventually secured his first massive contract, but while the deal places him in the top tier of earners at the position, the market still awaits its first $20 million salary. None of Kraft, Mayer or even Atlanta Falcons All-Pro Kyle Pitts cracked that barrier. Pitts' deal earlier in the offseason did, however, set a position record for guaranteed money at $36 million.
If a tight end is to finally break that $20 million threshold, it could be either Bowers or Detroit Lions weapon Sam LaPorta , who are next in line to receive life-changing money.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Lions restructure two contracts: What salary cap flexibility means for Sam LaPorta, Brian Branch extensions
summary: Detroit reworked the deals of Amon-Ra St. Brown and Penei Sewell
full_text:
The Detroit Lions suddenly have as much financial flexibility as nearly any team in the NFL . In the final hours leading up to their 2026 season opener, they reconstructed the contracts of two of their biggest stars: Wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown and offensive tackle Penei Sewell . The salary cap savings could open the door for important contract extensions or the addition of help at positions of need.
Of the two reworked deals, St. Brown's contract is the larger. The Lions converted $26 million of his salary into a signing bonus, which creates $20.8 million in cap space. Detroit also converted $18.6 million of Sewell's salary into a signing bonus, creating $14.8 million in cap savings.
Here are their remaining contracts, per Spotrac :
The restructuring does nothing to impact the size of St. Brown's or Sewell's total earnings but rather spreads it out during and beyond the life of their contracts. They still get paid, and the team has more money to spend against the salary cap. Detroit, in fact, now owns the second-most cap space in the NFL for 2026, behind only the San Francisco 49ers . They are also scheduled to rank sixth in 2027 cap space.
Financial gymnastics do not always mean additional moves are in the works, but they can indicate future plans. Even if the Lions do not intend to spend heavily in the immediate future, they can do so while already boasting an elite offensive roster and a handful of standout young defensive assets.
A couple of expiring contracts and an obvious need in the defensive backfield, however, suggest that Detroit could soon put its cap space to use.
The Lions have decisions to make with the 2023 second-round picks, both of whom developed into stars over the first three years of their careers. Both should be expected to sign contract extensions, even though negotiations will ensue into the regular season.
LaPorta has a chance to become the highest-paid tight end in the NFL if and when he inks his next deal. The tight end market has stalled with young standouts falling short of resetting the market, but LaPorta is the kind of talent who could leapfrog George Kittle and Trey McBride as the top earners at the position. A pair of fellow 2023 draftees landed second contracts on Saturday when Tucker Kraft and Michael Mayer became two of the five highest-paid tight ends . LaPorta and Kraft are represented by the same agent.
Branch, a fellow one-time Pro Bowler, is also in line to crack the upper echelon of earners at his position. The Lions could be more hesitant to extend the star safety, though, considering he sustained a torn Achilles in Week 14 of the 2025 season. Branch opened 2026 on the PUP list and may not be available until the final stages of the campaign, and there is the obvious question of whether he will be the same player after such a significant injury.
The salary cap savings Detroit made through its contract restructuring freed up enough money to pay both players.
In addition to Branch's injury, their other starting safety is also set to miss the start of the season as Kerby Joseph deals with an ongoing knee issue. Compounding the problems on the back end of a defense that struggled mightily in 2025 is the departure of cornerback Terrion Arnold . Allegations of kidnapping and armed robbery led to Arnold's release and created a glaring hole in the Lions' secondary.
The defensive backfield is thin and light on starting-caliber talent. Since there are a couple of standouts waiting to return at safety, the more pressing need is at cornerback. The Lions now have the cash to spend on a difference-maker, whether that be during the season by way of a trade or at the end of the year on the free agency market.
This should be a top priority for a team that needs to shore up its pass defense in order to achieve its postseason goals. St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs fuel a high-octane offense, but the team can only outscore so many opponents if it does not keep its foes off the scoreboard.

title: Cardinals practice squad elevation, RB not included. What does this mean for Love?
summary: The Arizona Cardinals submitted their list of the two practice squad guys they would bring up for the opener against the Los Angeles Chargers. It was expected that OG Matt Pryor would be one since RG Isaiah Adams is ruled out, and the second guy would be RB Evan Hull in order to give the […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - JULY 28: Jeremiyah Love #4 of the Arizona Cardinals participates in a team practice ahead of the NFL season at State Farm Stadium on July 28, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Arizona Cardinals submitted their list of the two practice squad guys they would bring up for the opener against the Los Angeles Chargers. It was expected that OG Matt Pryor would be one since RG Isaiah Adams is ruled out, and the second guy would be RB Evan Hull in order to give the roster three healthy bodies in case Jeremiyah Love can’t go or becomes very limited. Instead, the Cardinals’ coaching staff only brought up CB Kalen King. This makes sense because both Garrett Williams and Rabbit Taylor-Demerson are out. RELATED: LOVE QUESTIONABLE, ADAMS & GARRETT OUT But why only one player? Both Pryor and Hull make a lot of sense here. This means Arizona will only have three running backs available for Los Angeles: Tyler Allgeier, Love, and Bam Knight. What does this mean for Love? Earlier this week, head coach Mike LaFleur stated the Love was “trending well” towards being able to play in the Week 1 matchup. He was still nursing that high ankle sprain as of last weekend, but returned to practice this week. In all likelihood, Love will play. Not bringing up Hull pretty much says it all. Officially, Love will be listed as “questionable.” LaFleur plans to use a split backfield alongside Allgeier and Bam Knight, meaning Love’s snaps may be managed in his debut. Love appears to be closer to recovery, and the team has insisted all along that it is a minor injury. LaFleur is saying that playing the rookie will be a game-time decision. And if that still rings true, do the Cardinals want to go into this game with only two healthy backs? Inactives for Sunday will be 90 minutes ahead of kickoff at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles. For the Cardinals fanbase, it would be a bummer if Love doesn’t play. Part of the excitement for the season surrounds the rookie running back and what he can do at the NFL level. Just remember back in April prior to the NFL draft, the list of needs for Arizona did not include the running back group. With James Conner and Trey Benson on the mend, the thought process was that if each of these two could recover and come back healthy, the Cardinals should have used that #3 overall pick on a pass rusher or an offensive lineman. And Love isn’t damaged, mind you. It’s like playing basketball, and you turn your ankle coming down from a rebound. It will heal. But here’s a question: Should the Cardinals be playing him in the opener? If the coaches’ decision comes down to just prior to kickoff, maybe a little more time to heal should be in order? Plus, the offensive line still isn’t right. The right guard spot will be manned by Jon Gaines, the third guy to be inserted as the starter for this position. If the line is suspect, maybe just kick the can on Love and let him wait it out until there are zero tendencies or issues. If you have played sports in your lifetime, you have injured an ankle at some point. Even after a week, when you are no longer limping, all it takes is to lean the foot the wrong way, and you feel it. Let’s not damage Love before he even gets going. The Chargers have a very good defensive line, and they will hit. If Love plays, he won’t start. Currently, he is listed on the depth chart as RB2. So unbelievably dumb to rush him back and/or play him at anything under 100%. — ~doob~ (@DylanKThompson) September 11, 2026 Keep in mind, this is why Arizona GM Monti Ossenfort signed Allgeier in free agency. This is his job, and he should get the bulk of the carries. We all want to see Love in action and are hoping he will become the Emmitt Smith of the franchise going forward. If Love is not 100% and a game-time decision, it would be irresponsible to play him.

full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - AUGUST 13: Jeremiyah Love #4 of the Arizona Cardinals runs against Hezekiah Masses #35 of the Las Vegas Raiders in the second quarter of a preseason game at Allegiant Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Cardinals defeated the Raiders 27-14. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images What would you do? That’s the question everyone is asking and debating ahead of the Arizona Cardinals debut on Sunday against the Los Angeles Chargers. So, let’s Saturday morning quarterback before we Monday morning quarterback the decision. Jeremiyah Love is questionable, so what would you do if you are Mike LaFleur? I’ve seen a couple of interesting thoughts, so I’ll lay them out. First one was that for LaFleur, if Love isn’t feeling 100% he shouldn’t play. I’m not opposed to that, but I think overall it’s also a great opportunity to work through minor (I know a high ankle isn’t really minor) ailments. If he’s close to where the medical staff wants him (of course we are talking Cardinals medical staff so you may have a point to ignore that). Another one was to let Love decide. I… don’t agree with that one at all. If there is any inkling that Love shouldn’t go, it’s too early and he’s too important to let him make the call. Just my opinion. At the end of the day for me, I am fine with a game time decision from all parties. See how he feels and looks in warmups, and do what is best for the season, not for the first game. But let’s get our opinion out there, good or bad.

title: Falcons 2026 season predictions: What should we expect?
summary: We know the schedule, we’ve circled the games we’re most interested in, and we’ve prepared to slog through some sleep-deprived workdays during that early season stretch of three straight primetime games. Now it’s time to talk about our record predictions, how we think this season will unfold, and what that might mean for 2027. Read […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA - NOVEMBER 16: Atlanta wide receiver Drake London (5) reacts after gaining a first down during the NFL game between the Carolina Panthers and the Atlanta Falcons on November 16th, 2025 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images We know the schedule, we’ve circled the games we’re most interested in, and we’ve prepared to slog through some sleep-deprived workdays during that early season stretch of three straight primetime games. Now it’s time to talk about our record predictions, how we think this season will unfold, and what that might mean for 2027. Read our predictions and then share yours! Kevin Knight Record: 7-10 Team MVP: Bijan Robinson Rookie of the Year: Zachariah Branch Starting QB at the end of 2026: Michael Penix Jr. I’m revising down my previous record prediction by one game. Something about this Falcons team just feels off—not far enough off that I think they’ll plummet to the bottom of the NFC like some, just not quite right. The way this team has been constructed feels like a transitional year to me, and coming away with a top-10 pick in a potentially loaded QB draft would not be the worst case scenario. At the same time, eight wins is all it might take to win this beleaguered NFC South. So even with this relatively pessimistic record prediction, Atlanta is easily within striking distance of winning the division. I do think we’re likely to see a more consistent and better coached team. The loss of Jalon Walker for the season and James Pearce Jr. for half the season will be too much for the pass rush to overcome. This defense will be aggressive and fundamentally sound, but they’ll give up big plays in pursuit of blitz pressure. Unfortunately, that’s a necessity for this team as constructed. How good they are against the run is probably a make or break factor in determining if this is a good defense, or a merely OK one. The bigger concern is the offense, which is now being helmed by Cooper Rush for at least a week or two. I’m not quite sure what to expect from him—there’s a chance that he’s actually a better option than Tua Tagovailoa, based on what we’ve seen so far. Once Penix is back in the lineup, I’d expect a much more aggressive attack, and that should open the door for a more successful offense. Much depends on Bijan Robinson, who is the type of transcendent talent that can completely change the outlook of an offense. It’s possible that Bijan is so good that the QB situation simply isn’t that important, and he carries the team with a legitimate MVP-caliber season. I do think the upgrades at wide receiver will pay dividends, particularly the addition of rookie Zachariah Branch. Atlanta desperately needs a dynamic target in the quick game, and Branch gives them someone who can turn routine touches into explosive plays. With the added emphasis on special teams, Branch and the return game could play a significant role in maximizing opportunities. This team is being set up for a big QB addition in 2027, unless Michael Penix Jr. can come in and prove that he’s the future. I don’t know how likely that is, or how healthy he’ll be over the coming years. What I do know is that Atlanta will give him every opportunity to prove himself. While 2026 could be difficult to endure, expect the Falcons to be one of the most aggressive teams in free agency and the draft in 2027. Tre’Shon Diaz Record: 6-11 Team MVP: Bijan Robinson Rookie of the Year: Avieon Terrell Starting QB at the end of 2026: Michael Penix Jr. It’s a transitional year for the Falcons, and while I do believe in the young talent on this roster, I’m not sure they can overcome the challenges this team will face this year. Going into the season with the belief that multiple quarterbacks will play doesn’t bode well for confidence. On the other side of the ball, the defense will have to prove it can generate pressure with a completely remade EDGE and DL room. I think this team has enough talent to compete in most of their games this year, but I believe they’ll struggle to finish and close out games. QB play has the greatest influence on this, specifically the play of Michael Penix Jr. If he’s able to get under center by Week 4 and live up to his draft selection, I could see this team flirt with 9 wins, possibly 10. However, if the inconsistent play remains, wins will be tough to come by. This young defensive core should be a bright spot, but with youth comes inexperience, and we should expect some growing pains. This 2026 team isn’t a Super Bowl contender, but they can prove they have a legitimate foundation in place to be one and enter 2027 set up nicely. Saivion Mixson Record: 5-12 Team MVP: Bijan Robinson Rookie of the Year: Zachariah Branch Starting QB at the end of 2026: Jack Strand You never want to be the “Debbie Downer” of the group, but I can see this season getting off the rails pretty quickly. Is there enough talent, especially young talent, to be optimistic about the Falcons’ future? Absolutely. Do the young players on defense, along with the magic that Jeff Ulbrich was able to wiggle out of last year’s group, loom large in my mind? Absolutely. (2025 Falcons defense finished 14th in EPA/play and 13th in EPA/dropback) However, with a schedule like ours, that gets difficult in a hurry; it’s easy to see the Falcons heading into the bye week 3-7 (you can choose your favorite three wins) and trying to find themselves amid a mostly horrible division and either the Panthers or Buccaneers have actually grabbed firm control of it. Like last year’s Browns debacle, head coach Kevin Stefanski could have another tricky quarterback situation go south, as none of the three quarterbacks I expect to see play throughout this season live up to the standard of a consistent starting quarterback in the NFL. A more likely story: Both Penix and Tagovailoa don’t make it through the year and Strand is inevitably thrown in to limp us into next season’s draft lottery, chock-full of potential quarterback prospects. All in all, I do believe this looks akin to the 2021 Detroit Lions, which stings more because we’ve now hired three head coaches and two general managers in the same span of their revamped image in the Motor City. But they will show the grit and physicality to stay in games, but won’t have enough high-end talent, including at the quarterback position, to finish it out. Dave Choate Record: 8-9 Team MVP: Bijan Robinson Rookie of the Year: Kendal Daniels Starting QB at the end of 2026: Michael Penix Jr. You can only be burned so many times, right? The team’s uncertainty at quarterback, attrition at EDGE rusher, and number of new faces on the staff and roster conspire to make me think this will be another in a long line of losing seasons. Do I think this will be a terrible team? Absolutely not. Do I think the chances of everything coming together to propel this team to 10 wins and a playoff berth are high, given their very real roster questions? Also no. But I’m probably one of the more optimistic souls here, as I often am. The hope is that by the end of this year, the Falcons know whether they can rely on Penix as their long-term starter, they have their defensive foundation firmly in place, and they’re ready to make noise with plenty of cap space and a nearly full complement of picks in 2027. I’d love to be surprised–and if Penix can live up to his considerable promise and get in the lineup soon, perhaps I will be–but I think this team will not arrive as a true contender in 2026. I do think they’ll be a more cohesive team than they have been in recent years, however, and that eight wins are within their grasp if that happens. If not, well, we’ll be excited to talk about quarterbacks in the spring!

full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 10: Darian Mensah #10 of the Miami Hurricanes looks to pass against the Florida A&M Rattlers during the second quarter of the game at Hard Rock Stadium on September 10, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Atlanta Falcons are in dire straits heading into the first week of the 2026 NFL season, as both projected starters at the quarterback position are out for the first game against the Pittsburgh Steelers. But that’s not why we’re here. Draft season is year-round nowadays, and the Falcons need multiple players throughout the roster if they’re going to build a sturdy foundation to start competing for the division/conference sooner rather than later. Atlanta has done a great job not overextending in the short term, owning the most cap space in 2027, despite extending Drake London, Bijan Robinson, Kyle Pitts and Matthew Bergeron this offseason. However, even with the potential depth that money can bring, general manager Ian Cunningham and President Matt Ryan have to hit on the draft. So, we’re going to get a jump on next year’s draft by pinpointing seven picks in this way-too-early 2027 NFL mock draft. Round 1, Pick 6: Darian Mensah, QB, Miami ​​ https://x.com/NFLPerformances/status/2098258722707407212 I’m buying into the hype early. The former Duke transfer has come out of the gate firing, albeit against Stanford and Florida A&M. Mensah’s 91.1% completion percentage is the second-best start to a college football season for any quarterback with 40+ attempts in the first two games, while his 271.7 Passer Efficiency Rating is the best. 41-of-45 for 653 yards, eight touchdowns, and zero interceptions. Miami is looking to run through the ACC with ease, and hopefully, that means we see plenty of NFL-caliber throws from Mensah that will make him the next transfer quarterback who impresses scouts this season. ​ Round 2, Pick 38: Samson Okunlola, OT, Miami Miami LT Samson Okunlola (#63) cut ups vs Stanford Folks this is what they look like. If Okunlola continues to string together performances like this, then he will be a consensus top 10 prospect before we know it. Rare movement and feet for 330 lbs. pic.twitter.com/gPx9G3NpOh — Jason Lewis (@Jasonlewis54) September 8, 2026 To build the future, you have to fortify the foundation, and that means Atlanta has to acquire a left tackle, so Jake Matthews can be the family man he deserves to be. Samson Okunlola’s movement skills, especially his absurdly quick feet, are just one of his impressive traits that scouts will bet on if he comes out after this season. Okunlola’s 6’6”, 330-pound frame gives him such impressive size and he has experience playing inside as well. Round 3, Pick 70: Tavion Gadson, DT, Kentucky Kentucky iDL Tavion Gadson (#94) has always been a disruptive force in the run game. In 2025 he showed flashes of being the same as a pass rusher. pic.twitter.com/y8I0QM7h3h — Jayyy (@DraftwithJay) April 19, 2026 With Brandon Dorlus heading to the edge, the Falcons lose the interior pressure that Dorlus and, to a lesser extent, Ruke Orhorhoro brought on opposing quarterbacks. Tavion Gadson immediately brings that pass-rush juice back to the Falcons’ line along with a knack for using his athleticism and size (6’4”, 302 pounds) to stuff up the A-gaps. Round 4, Pick 105: Niki Prongos, OT, Stanford I couldn’t help myself, and if Cunningham and Stefanski were met with the same choice, I don’t think they would help themselves either. Niki Prongos hadn’t started playing football until his senior year of high school, choosing to play baseball and basketball instead. Even in high school, he played tight end and defensive tackle alongside his duties at tackle. Prongos is such a fun athlete and would be a stellar pickup for Bill Callahan. Round 5, Pick 179: Bruce Mitchell, C, BYU Chase Roberts? I’m watching Bruce Mitchell clear the alley like a Good Samaritan pushing a Honda out of the intersection. https://t.co/GriHQQqPea — Hans Olsen (@GBSHansO) October 3, 2025 #63 in white and blue has a case to be the best center in college football, and it would not surprise me if he finds a way into day two when it’s all said and done. Mitchell has a stout anchor in pass protection alongside some strong hands in the run game. With this move, the Falcons would solve all three of their “problems” along the offensive line in one draft. Round 6, Pick 216: Fluff Bothwell, RB, Mississippi State Mississippi State RB Fluff Bothwell is a WORKHORSE. He consistently works through arm tackles, adores contact, and finishes runs forward. He even has a bit more phonebooth quick-twitch than you'd expect for a man of his size… oh yeah, he's 5-foot-10 and 230 pounds. pic.twitter.com/EtJGiiVMfq — Cory (@fakecorykinnan) April 28, 2026 Brian Robinson Jr. feels like a rental for this season, but the future of backing up Bijan Robinson can look like a running back like Fluff Bothwell. Don’t let the name fool you; there is absolutely nothing soft about his game. Bothwell is 5’10”, 230 pounds and, for a man of that size, he has impressive agility. Round 7, Pick 220: Duce Robinson, WR, Florida State I don’t see enough Duce Robinson love on my timeline. I know this is an absolutely stacked Wide receiver class, but Robinson broke out in a huge way last season, and is poised to only get better in 2026 👀 📈📈📈 pic.twitter.com/Hm2YO6qXGa — The Draft Hub (@TheNFLDraftHub) July 28, 2026 KJ Duff is one of those players in the 2027 draft you wish had transferred to another team so he could get more eyes on his performance with a quarterback who can get him the ball. The same goes for Florida State receiver Duce Robinson. Robinson is 6’6”, 230 pounds and has an incredibly large catch radius, while allowing Drake London to work more in the slot and Kyle Pitts over the middle of the field.

title: Falcons vs. Steelers: A look at the series history going into 2026
summary: The Falcons open their season by making the journey up to Western Pennsylvania to face one of the NFL’s blue bloods and a team that has absolutely owned them throughout their respective histories. The Steelers are on the shortlist of the most successful NFL franchises in history — tied with the New England Patriots with […]
full_text: (Photo by DAVID MAXWELL/AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images The Falcons open their season by making the journey up to Western Pennsylvania to face one of the NFL’s blue bloods and a team that has absolutely owned them throughout their respective histories. The Steelers are on the shortlist of the most successful NFL franchises in history — tied with the New England Patriots with a league-high six Super Bowl triumphs — while the Falcons have mostly been a punching bag for the rest of the league since their inception in 1966, and the head-to-head record between these teams reflect each of those realities. The Falcons and Steelers have faced off 19 times, and Atlanta has come away the victor just twice, sporting an abominable 2-16-1 record. The .132% win percentage is the lowest the Birds have against any other franchise, and the two victories are their joint fewest against anyone else, along with the Ravens against whom Atlanta has played 12 fewer games. Any way you slice it, the Steelers have always kicked the Falcons’ butts. That makes it even more impressive that Michael Vick went undefeated in his two meetings against Pittsburgh, as Atlanta’s quarterback, lighting up the scoreboard in each game. The first was a 34-34 tie at Heinz Field in 2002 (the only game in Pittsburgh the Falcons ever played without suffering defeat). The second, a dramatic 41-38 triumph at the Georgia Dome in 2006, where Vick had a career high four touchdown passes (three of them going to Alge Crumpler). Atlanta’s only other victory came in 1970. The last time they opened the season in Pittsburgh was a slugfest in 2010, which went to overtime and was ultimately decided by a 50-yard Rashard Mendenhall run for the win. That marked the first of five straight victories over the Falcons that the Steelers have enjoyed as an active streak. When did the Falcons and Steelers play each other last? The Falcons opened the 2024 season and the soon to be short lived Raheem Morris tenure by debuting new major free agent signing Kirk Cousins at home against a Steelers team employing Arthur Smith, whom Atlanta had just fired at the end of the previous season. Normally when one team keeps the other out of the end zone all afternoon it’s a recipe for success, but the Falcons achieved the rare feat of accomplishing this and still losing the game. Atlanta’s first half was far from perfect but was passable, and highlighted a Cousins to Kyle Pitts touchdown pass which was the difference in them having a slender lead at the break. The second half was where disaster struck, as TJ Watt routinely abused right tackle Kaleb McGary and Atlanta saw their best chance at putting up points go up in smoke on a fumble which resulted from the snap hitting a man in motion, as Cousins never looked comfortable in the newly debuted pistol formation. The Falcons defense bent but never broke, but Pittsburgh bent it just enough to the tune of six field goals as Atlanta’s offense suffered a second half shutout. The game was poetically ended and the door shut with TJ Watt finally getting to Cousins for a sack on the final play, after living in the backfield all afternoon. The writer of this article woke up at 2 a.m. to watch every moment of this disaster while vacationing in Kyoto.

title: How Cooper Rush starting at QB changes the Falcons’ offensive game plan
summary: Tua Tagovailoa’s back is tighter than a clam with lockjaw, and Michael Penix Jr. doesn’t trust his knee as far as he can throw it. It’s Cooper Rush time. For some, this feels like the worst-case scenario for the Atlanta Falcons quarterback room, but is the drop-off from Tagovailoa to Rush really all that significant […]
full_text: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Tua Tagovailoa’s back is tighter than a clam with lockjaw, and Michael Penix Jr. doesn’t trust his knee as far as he can throw it. It’s Cooper Rush time. For some, this feels like the worst-case scenario for the Atlanta Falcons quarterback room, but is the drop-off from Tagovailoa to Rush really all that significant in 2026? If we are judging who ran the offense more competently during the preseason, the answer is Rush. Yes, he had a rough outing against the Broncos, but Rush joined the roster only 15 days before the game. Since then, he’s shown command and the ability to keep Tommy Rees’ offense on schedule. His ability to pick up the playbook in that short amount of time is why he’s been able to stick as a backup in this league. Rush to Velling! FOX | NFL+ pic.twitter.com/ibjVS6UxNh — Atlanta Falcons (@AtlantaFalcons) August 29, 2026 However, being a quarterback takes more than knowing the calls; when you look at physical ability and skill sets, Rush and Tagovailoa have been indistinguishable this summer. Neither is known for arm strength, and making plays out of the pocket is a crapshoot. Rush did show a slight willingness to push the ball compared to Tua, who had an ADoT (average depth of target) of 3.3, to Rush’s 6.3. Tua has an edge when it comes to processing, but he didn’t do a great job showcasing that during the preseason. If this feels like a Tua slam piece, that’s not my intent, but it’s important that we establish how similar the two players are at this stage in their careers. These similarities are why I believe that Kevin Stefanski won’t have to tweak the game plan much, if at all. The staff clearly believed Tua could execute the offense better, but they can still ask Rush to run the same plan. The 2026 offense was always going to run through Bijan Robinson, not the Falcons quarterback. He is the clear strength of this offense, a true one-of-one talent, and whoever is under center is here to manage the game. The worry for this offense, especially with Tua, is: what do you do when you get behind the chains or trail in the scoring column? Many have been prepared to hold their breath on third-and-long this upcoming Sunday, and that’s not going to change with Rush. So Stefanski and Rees are still focusing on solving the same problem, which is a good thing. If the team had to adjust to a completely different play style at the last minute, I’d be more concerned about the product we’ll get Sunday. To be clear, I am still concerned to a healthy degree. KP down the sideline! With the @DrakeLondon_ block 👀 FOX | NFL+ pic.twitter.com/5vQ1gLa0gH — Atlanta Falcons (@AtlantaFalcons) August 28, 2026 Rush won’t be expected to win this game with his arm, and neither was Tua before going down. This needs to be the Bijan Robinson show with an overdose of screens and quick-hitting passes. Hopefully, paired with complementary play from the defense, that’s enough to get the Falcons through Week 1.

title: Ravens-Colts Week 1 predictions: how will Jesse Minter attack Daniel Jones?
summary: Let’s face it: odds probably do not mean much to Ravens fans at this point. Last year, Baltimore entered 14 games as favorites and won just half of them. That pattern is likely to play out once again this year given the Ravens’ early slate of opponents, starting with the Colts in Week 1. Baltimore […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - AUGUST 22: Jesse Minter head coach of the Baltimore Ravens looks on against the Minnesota Vikings during the fourth quarter of the preseason game at U.S. Bank Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Let’s face it: odds probably do not mean much to Ravens fans at this point. Last year, Baltimore entered 14 games as favorites and won just half of them. That pattern is likely to play out once again this year given the Ravens’ early slate of opponents, starting with the Colts in Week 1. Baltimore is favored by 3.5 points heading into Indianapolis ( via FanDuel Sportsbook ), indicating plenty of confidence in Jesse Minter’s head coaching debut. The Colts are largely running it back with their 2025 squad, so last year’s tendencies can offer some insights into their plans for Sunday. Head coach Shane Steichen’s offense primarily operates out of the shotgun, relying on running back Jonathan Taylor to churn yards in the run game and suck linebackers in for play action shots to the intermediate areas of the field. Quarterback Daniel Jones rarely pushed the ball downfield, throwing deep balls less than 10% of the time ( via Pro Football Focus ). Most of those targets went to wide receiver Alec Pierce, the NFL’s back-to-back leader in yards per reception; beyond him, Indianapolis lacks another deep threat. That should lead the Ravens to deploy some bracket coverage against Pierce to prevent him from taking the top off the defense. Minter’s three-safety looks will also allow the secondary to shift the coverage picture post-snap. Look out for Baltimore to bait Jones by showing a 1-on-1 matchup against Pierce pre-snap only for Malaki Starks or Jaylinn Hawkins to fly back and cover a potential shot downfield. If Indianapolis tries a high-low route combination on the outside, the boundary corner can try to jump the underneath route with safety help overtop. The Colts’ defensive coordinator is a familar foe: Lou Anarumo, who previously held the same position in Cincinnati from 2019 to 2024. The Ravens offense largely found success against his Bengals defenses during his tenure, able to control games on the ground and keep up with Joe Burrow in a shootout when needed. But Anarumo’s ability to disguise his coverages and pressure packages can attack the Ravens offense in two key ways. First, it will demand Jackson to be on the same page with a revamped offensive line that features a brand-new interior trio, including center Jovaughn Gwyn making his first start. He will already have his hands full with Colts defensive tackles DeForest Buckner and Grover Stewart, but he also has to help Jackson read the defense and communicate adjustments to the rest of the line. Jackson will also have to be careful not to fall into Anarumo’s coverage traps. New offensive coordinator Declan Doyle has worked to re-establish the Ravens’ quick passing game with an emphasis on Jackson’s footwork and timing as he goes through his progression. But just as Minter will try to bait-and-switch Jones, Anarumo will do the same against Jackson. This could become a particularly interesting battle when the Ravens go under center, which has been another of Doyle’s early focal points. Baltimore will no doubt use running back Derrick Henry to set up play-action shots to wide receiver Zay Flowers on his signature deep dig routes. Anarumo can respond with a two-high safety look but sending one of them to buzz the middle of the field. But that will only be possible if his front can stop the Ravens’ ground game, putting pressure on undersized linebackers Jaylon Carlies and Akeem Davis-Gaither to step up and fit the run. Otherwise, the Colts will have to use their safeties in run support, which should give Flowers more room to operate over the middle. Given that this is his first game in Doyle’s system – and his first game back at 100% after last year’s injuries – the two-time MVP could lean on his legs on Sunday as he gets settled in the offense. Some of his most dazzling extended plays came against Anarumo’s Bengals, partially because the coverage look forced him to hold onto the ball. These are just a few elements of the schematic battle set to take place on Sunday. Steichen and Anarumo will offer a solid first challenge to the Ravens’ new-look coaching staff in a game that could come down to Baltimore’s star power advantage on both sides of the ball.
author: Nikhil Mehta

title: 3 Key Matchups for Ravens-Colts Week 1
summary: The Baltimore Ravens open their 2026 season with an opponent that could be considered the franchise’s first rival: the Indianapolis Colts. Jesse Minter will make his head coaching debut against Shane Steichen; the two will face off directly when the former’s offense and latter’s defense are on the field. The Ravens also will also face […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - AUGUST 22: Olaivavega Ioane #71 of the Baltimore Ravens lines up against the Minnesota Vikings during the first quarter of the preseason game at U.S. Bank Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens open their 2026 season with an opponent that could be considered the franchise’s first rival: the Indianapolis Colts. Jesse Minter will make his head coaching debut against Shane Steichen; the two will face off directly when the former’s offense and latter’s defense are on the field. The Ravens also will also face a familiar coordinator on Sunday: Lou Anarumo, who was the defensive coordinator for the Cincinnati Bengals for six years. Against his defenses, the Ravens averaged nearly 29 points a game over 12 regular-season matchups. Can they continue that success under new offensive coordinator Declan Doyle? Winning in the trenches Ravens fans know as well as any fanbase that an offense can only go as far as its offensive line can take it. Lamar Jackson is a truly unique talent, but in crunch time, in the playoffs, he has to be able to rely on his protection. The Ravens’ front office reshaped the interior of the line this offseason with three new starters. The team reunited with left guard John Simpson in free agent, drafted right guard Vega Ioane in the first round of April’s draft, and held a summer-long competition that finally yielded Jovaughn Gywn as the starting center. On Sunday, the trio will face their first test as a unit and begin their journey to ‘being their best when their best is needed.’ The Colts’ formidable trio of defensive tackles will offer stiff opposition. Superstar DeForest Buckner is a do-it-all weapon who’s averaged nearly half a sack a game over his entire career. He recorded six or more sacks in eight of his 10 years, and he’s no less effective in the run game. Since 2020, he has partnered with Grover Stewart to form one of the league’s best interior duos. Stewart is an underrated, perfect complement to Buckner: a run-stuffing, nose tackle specialist who takes on double teams with ease and clears the way for Buckner to make splash plays. The last piece of the puzzle is Adetomiwa Adebawore. The Colts decided not to re-sign Neville Gallimore this offseason after Adebawore took a step in his game in 2025 with a career-high four sacks. He now looks to be a massive part of the rotation, in a contract year nonetheless. Between Buckner and Stewart plugging holes in the run game and Adebawore subbing in for pass rush, the Ravens are going to find out early in the season if their new interior O-line has the stuff to pave the path to a Super Bowl. Best on best: WR1 vs. CB1 The Ravens decided to lock up Zay Flowers with a $35 million APY deal this offseason that will him in Baltimore until 2031, and for good reason. Flowers has improved every year of his career, and after back-to-back 1,000-yard, Pro Bowl campaigns, he looks like true No. 1 receiver in the NFL. He is an elite route-runner, both when separating against man coverage and finding soft spots vs. zone, with the ability to torch defenses with the ball in his hands. Flowers is also just 26 years old entering his fourth season, so he still has room to grow. The expectation is that Flowers will see a ton of Colts cornerback Sauce Gardner on the other side of the line. Gardner, the No. 4 pick in 2022, is one of the better corners in the league. He started out of the gate hot, posting elite PFF grades his first two seasons before taking a step back in 2024 and 2025. He spent more time shadowing opposing teams’ top receivers after arriving in Indianapolis last year, and after a full offseason in the defense, he could do so even more often in 2026. There is still a lot we don’t know about how the Ravens offense will operate, but a hefty target share for Flowers is a virtual certainty. We’ve seen him find success against other elite corners like Christian Gonzalez, Pat Surtain, and Derek Stingley, so keeping that trend up against Gardner would be a great way to open the season. 1st test for Jesse Minter’s secondary On the other side of the ball, the Ravens’ defense will be looking to put two frankly horrendous seasons in the rearview. Their performance was way below the standard in Baltimore. Enter new head coach Jesse Minter, one of the league’s brightest defensive minds. Just look at what he did in Michigan in 2023, with the Chargers the last two seasons, and even in his first preseason games in Baltimore. More specifically, Minter’s speciality is the secondary, and he’s working with the best collection of talent in his career. Last year, the Ravens ranked second-worst in the league against the pass, allowing 247.9 yards per game – tied, coincidentally, with Indianapolis. Meanwhile, when Daniel Jones was healthy, the Colts fielded a top-10 passing attack with Jones posting career-highs in nearly every traditional passing category. He has a ton of weapons, including Alec Pierce, Josh Downs, Tyler Warren, and new addition Keenan Allen, not to mention Jonathan Taylor out of the backfield. That group will be a good first test for the Ravens to see if Minter’s influence can erase the last two years of defensive struggles.

title: New chapter of Buffalo Bills out to set a great first impression
summary: First impressions matter. At least to our psyches they do. They don’t always foreshadow. But they’re often the basis of reputations. Nine years ago, the Bills went bold — very bold — in the draft, trading up twice for the most polarizing quarterback prospect, Josh Allen. Even Brandon Beane probably couldn’t have imagined that day […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - AUGUST 15: Buffalo Bills head coach Joe Brady on the sideline during the first half against the Carolina Panthers at Highmark Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images First impressions matter. At least to our psyches they do. They don’t always foreshadow. But they’re often the basis of reputations. Nine years ago, the Bills went bold — very bold — in the draft, trading up twice for the most polarizing quarterback prospect, Josh Allen. Even Brandon Beane probably couldn’t have imagined that day in April 2018 that his first selection as the Bills GM would work out as amazingly as it has for the organization. And after nine years with the most successful head coach in franchise history since Marv Levy, the Bills went bold — very bold — again, severing ties with Sean McDermott the morning after his team authored another agonizing playoff defeat short of the Super Bowl. Buffalo stayed in-house with its hire after McDermott, and Joe Brady takes the sidelines today with the head coach title for the first time in his career. The defensive coordinator, Jim Leonhard, will also hold his title, in the NFL, for the first time. In years past, different defensive coordinators always shouldered the brunt of postseason-exit criticism in Western New York. Leonhard was arguably the most sought after defensive mind in football, a former overachieving player with a vastly different philosophy — and scheme — than the previous defensive-minded head coach. To trot out a first-time head coach and first-time NFL defensive coordinator to begin a season with Allen’s superpowers at their peak… again, bold from the Bills. And for Brady and Leonhard, what an ideal place to start… in Houston, a locale that, outside of Arrowhead in January, haunted Buffalo’s past regime unlike any other. While undoubtedly a major challenge, it provides an excellent opportunity to make a dazzling first impression. Of course, the Super Bowl can’t be won or lost in Week 1 in the NFL. We have to keep that in mind. It’s a long and arduous rollercoaster of a season. For every team. But for the Bills and their fans they knew exactly what to expect each year of the McDermott era, and it was unquestionably a span when Buffalo had its most prosperous and stable regular seasons in 30 years. And first impressions still take time to shake, even today when opinions morph swiftly in the social-media driven age of the sports world. McDermott won his first game as Bills head coach and ended a 17-year playoff drought in his first season. Allen’s first win, which came in September, was as emphatic as it gets, still the only occurrence in NFL history a 17-point underdog ultimately won by double digits (Buffalo won 27-6 in Minnesota). It also featured Allen’s original trademark highlight, which made quite the first impression. And that’s an understatement. Those first impressions made indelible impacts in Buffalo for McDermott and Allen. And now, just like when McDermott began in Buffalo, and at the inception of the Allen era, none of us know where to set the expectation bar for this new chapter of the team’s modern golden era. We need a first impression to direct us where to start as the Bills venture into a new frontier. Does the unadulterated version of Brady’s scheme, armed with the biggest receiver acquisition since Stefon Diggs, elevate Buffalo’s already well-oiled offense to new heights? Is Leonhard’s attacking style defense precisely what the Bills have needed on that side of the ball? I suspect boldness will be a recurring theme from those two because such on-field evidence exists from their past coaching experiences. And while the previous regime certainly won its fair share of big games, being bold wasn’t something that could always be said about McDermott and Co., especially in key contests. On paper, a bold head coach and bold defensive coordinator align perfectly with Allen, the NFL’s ultimate on-field personification of boldness. Yet football games aren’t played on paper. And the Bills have a significant test right out of the gate, on the road, to begin this new chapter. I’d bet too that the Texans, despite their unusual level of accomplishment to date against Allen and the Bills, understand the significance of the test in front of them today. Because while it’d be sensible for Houston to believe it just needs to run it back against Buffalo, these Bills are out to make a damn good first impression.
author: Chris Trapasso

title: 5 Houston Texans to watch vs. the Buffalo Bills
summary: The Houston Texans host the Buffalo Bills in Week One this season, and they’ll be looking for their third consecutive home victory over Buffalo in the series between these two AFC foes. Buffalo lost close games at NRG Stadium in each of the last two seasons, dropping a 23-20 decision during the 2024 season and […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TX - NOVEMBER 20: Nico Collins #12 of the Houston Texans lines up before the snap during an NFL football game against the Buffalo Bills at NRG Stadium on November 20, 2025 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Houston Texans host the Buffalo Bills in Week One this season, and they’ll be looking for their third consecutive home victory over Buffalo in the series between these two AFC foes. Buffalo lost close games at NRG Stadium in each of the last two seasons, dropping a 23-20 decision during the 2024 season and a 23-19 contest last year. For Houston, much of their success against Buffalo has come thanks to their stifling defense. Houston manages to harass quarterback Josh Allen in ways that most of the NFL has been unable to duplicate. Can the Texans do that again? If so, the Bills could be in a heap of trouble. In order for Buffalo to come out with a win on Sunday, they’ll need to do a better job dictating the game to the Houston defense than they have in he past. However, they’ll also need to put themselves in good situations by limiting what could be a very potent Texans offense, as well. Here are five Texans to watch this Sunday against Buffalo. _____________________________________________________________________________ QB C.J. Stroud Sure, it’s usually a given that the opposing quarterback needs to be controlled in order for your team to win; however, with a Houston team that has big-play potential on each snap, it becomes that much more important to make sure that the quarterback never feels comfortable. Stroud entered the NFL with authority as a rookie in 2023, but his overall numbers and performances have regressed since. The last game Houston played last season was also the worst of Stroud’s professional career, as he mustered just a 28 quarterback rating while throwing four interceptions in a playoff loss to the New England Patriots. If Buffalo’s defensive front can win without blitzing, it’s going to be a long day for Stroud, as he does not perform well when pressured. Defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard can use disguise to fool Stroud into heating himself up in the pocket, as well, as Stroud struggled with that particular method throughout last season. Penning Stroud in the pocket and bringing effective, juducious pressure is a huge key to success this week. WR Nico Collins The Bills have limited Collins to just five catches in their two matchups where he played, which sounds like they’ve done well to keep Collins from wrecking the game. However, Collins has 133 yards and a touchdown on those five catches, which amounts to 26.6 yards per reception. That’s the best mark he has against anyone in his NFL career. Collins is an elite wideout looking to earn his fourth consecutive 1,000-yard receiving season. Whether it’s Christian Benford, Maxwell Hairston, Davison Igbinosun, or some combination of those three plus others in on covering Collins, Buffalo needs to know that he’s a big play waiting to happen. Limiting those shots and forcing Stroud to check down repeatedly will increase the chances of a mistake on the offensive end. The Bills can’t let Collins run wild and free throughout the secondary. I’m interested to see how Jim Leonhard goes about stopping a team’s top wideout—will Benford travel with Collins? Will the Bills rely on combo zones or double teams? Will they keep their corners on one side of the field and let them matchup with whomever lines up across from them? We’ll find out soon enough. RT Trent Brown Houston’s offensive line is generally regarded as one of the worst in the NFL. This gives Bills fans hope that the team can exploit that weakness and win in the pass rush, though years of falling short in that regard (think of the Divisional Round matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals a few years back) might lead to limited optimism. Brown is a reserve tackle who has had some good years, but who has also been beaten rather routinely by faster edge rushers. This is a matchup I love for newly acquired outside linebacker Bradley Chubb, who had a strong season with the Miami Dolphins last year coming off of an ACL tear the year prior. If the Bills send extra rushers, it also wouldn’t surprise me to see that pressure come from this side, as it would serve two purposes: First, it would allow the Bills to attack a backup. Second, it would force Stroud to roll to his left rather than his right. If Brown can hold up in pass protection—and the Texans line can open holes for newly acquired running back David Montgomery, who should add much-needed juice to their rushing attack—then Buffalo could be in for a long day. However, if the Bills can find some early-down wins against a poor protection unit, then they could force Houston into a pass-happy game script. That could lead to some big hits for Buffalo’s pass rushers early. The Whole Defensive Line Yeah, this is cheating, but let’s be honest: it’s really hard to pick just one person up front as the key to this whole Texans pass rush. Will Anderson is phenomenal, Danielle Hunter is phenomenal, Sheldon Rankins is a monster, and Jadeveon Clowney still has plenty left as a situational pass-rusher. I could have skipped this group altogether since they were so problematic last year—and we all know they’re going to be a handful again this season—but it would have been disingenuous of me to pretend like this front isn’t excellent. On the flip side of the Texans, Buffalo’s offensive line generally grades out as one of the better units in the league, yet if you just watched them last season against Houston, you’d never have known it. Josh Allen’s internal clock has to be a little quicker this week, because holding the ball against this defensive front likely leads to the blue medical tent during the game and a flight home nursing an 0-1 record after it. I’d like to see the Bills go with some play-action early in the game followed by some middle screens after it. Last year, Buffalo tried to stress the outside of Houston’s defense via the bubble screen, and it flat-out didn’t work. Test Houston’s discipline up front by giving them a lot to look at, and while it’s a very disciplined unit, planting a small seed of doubt in what the guys up front see could give Buffalo’s offense the split-second advantage it needs to break some plays. DB Jalen Pitre Houston’s top nickel corner is an excellent player, as evidenced by his four interceptions and 12 pass breakups last season. Similarly to the defensive front, we could have talked about any number of secondary players in what is an excellent Houston secondary—shoutouts here to Derek Stingley Jr., Kamari Lassiter, Calen Bullock, and Reed Blankenship—but Buffalo’s offensive strength is in the middle of the field. Pitre is a bigger slot corner, standing at 6’ and 200 lbs., but the Bills have weapons in Dalton Kincaid, Khalil Shakir, and Dawson Knox who should be able to win in that area of the field. At least, if I’m designing the passing attack, I’m trying to feed those players rather than continuing to hammer those All Pro and Pro Bowl players Houston has at other spots in the secondary. I’d try to move DJ Moore into the slot, as well, to see if I could force some favorable matchups his way. Pitre was inactive last year when these two teams played, but I think he’s going to be a big part of the contest on Sunday.

title: Buffalo Bills make two practice-squad elevations ahead Week 1’s game at Houston Texans
summary: We now know who the Buffalo Bills punt returner will be for Week 1… and presumably longer than that. Greg Dortch. The team announced Saturday afternoon they will be elevating Dortch for their season-opening contest against the Houston Texans: This makes all the sense in the world for the Bills, especially because after the preseason, […]
full_text: Cardinals receiver Greg Dortch (4) sprints upfield for a first down against the Commanders during a game at State Farm Stadium in Glendale on Sept. 29, 2024. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co We now know who the Buffalo Bills punt returner will be for Week 1… and presumably longer than that. Greg Dortch. The team announced Saturday afternoon they will be elevating Dortch for their season-opening contest against the Houston Texans: Elevated RB Frank Gore Jr. and WR Greg Dortch from the practice squad for tomorrow’s game vs. Houston. — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) September 12, 2026 This makes all the sense in the world for the Bills, especially because after the preseason, they did not have someone who earned the punt-return job, which led to their acquisition of Dortch after he was surprisingly released by the Detroit Lions. Dortch has 99 punt returns on his NFL resume to date and raised his average in each of the last four seasons. His 11.6 yards-per-return average a season ago was tied for the seventh-best in football. I also love this decision by the Bills because of what Dortch can bring to the field as a receiver . Remember, Buffalo only kept five wideouts on its initial 53-man roster. Dortch makes six. He has established himself as a gadget-y, underneath possession target in the NFL with 145 catches for 1,310 yards in his six-year professional career to date. In the article linked in the previous paragraph, I highlighted Dortch’s excellent YAC capabilities, and I’ll repeat the key metric here — Dortch has forced 25 missed tackles over the past two seasons on just 79 targets and 66 receptions. That’s absurd. We’ll see if Dortch gets any looks on offense against the Texans, but he’s all but officially guaranteed to be returning punts in this game. As for Frank Gore Jr., his elevation hints at Ty Johnson, who’s listed as questionable for this outing in Houston, is unlikely to play. The son of the back with the third-most career rushing yards in the NFL history had his third-consecutive strong preseason with the Bills, as he averaged 4.6 yards per tote on 26 attempts. The 24 year old has yet to carry the ball in regular-season game but was active for Buffalo’s wild-card win over the Jaguars in January and had one reception for six yards. He just might factor into the offense for the Bills in this game against Houston to begin the 2026 regular season.

title: Bradley Chubb seems to be the forgotten Buffalo Bills addition
summary: As the Buffalo Bills get set to visit the Houston Texans on Sunday, this will conclude one of the most eventful offseasons in recent memory. Coaches being fired, awkward press conferences, coaches being hired, free agency, the draft, and a new stadium set to open. But in my opinion there was one move made this […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - AUGUST 22: Bradley Chubb #9 of the Buffalo Bills warms up prior to a preseason game against the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field on August 22, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images As the Buffalo Bills get set to visit the Houston Texans on Sunday, this will conclude one of the most eventful offseasons in recent memory. Coaches being fired, awkward press conferences, coaches being hired, free agency, the draft, and a new stadium set to open. But in my opinion there was one move made this off-season that is not being discussed enough. When it comes to new faces in Buffalo this season, DJ Moore has understandably gotten plenty of attention. The team needed to make a bigger move at receiver, and sending a second round pick to the Bears addressed their biggest need. C.J. Gardner-Johnson has attracted plenty of headlines, and will look to get some revenge against one of his former clubs. But the most notable addition to the Bills might be the player that no one is talking about – Bradley Chubb. The former first round pick signed a three-year deal worth $43.5 million with the Bills this off-season, making him the team’s largest addition to the roster. Chubb was named a captain earlier this week, a testament to the leadership that he immediately brought to the Bills locker room. Maybe it is just me, but no one seems to be talking about Chubb as an important addition to the club. In trying to understand why there has not been more chatter around Chubb, I can only imagine it is because of the fatigue that fans have had around the previous additions. A.J. Epenesa, Von Miller, and Joey Bosa (among others) have failed to live up to varying levels of expectations. Now Chubb, and immediate starter opposite of Gregory Rousseau, comes in with little expectations from fans. As I mentioned earlier, maybe I am just looking in the wrong places for news on Chubb. Regardless of those expectations, I am excited to see what Chubb can bring to Jim Leonhard’s defense. If Chubb can fill the void opposite of Rousseau — along with Michael Hoecht and T.J. Parker — the Bills defensive end group can make an impact early this season.

title: Just in queso you need a tailgating idea for Buffalo Bills at Houston Texans
summary: How the heck long have I been doing this anyway? Doesn’t matter, the mad-kitchen scientist is back for another season of recipes to make your Buffalo Bills gamedays even more memorable. For those of you new to this, it’s pretty simple. We love the Bills. We love food. Every week you’ll get a themed recipe […]
full_text: How the heck long have I been doing this anyway? Doesn’t matter, the mad-kitchen scientist is back for another season of recipes to make your Buffalo Bills gamedays even more memorable. For those of you new to this, it’s pretty simple. We love the Bills. We love food. Every week you’ll get a themed recipe based on the Bills and their opponent. Extra Spicy Queso With all the cheese sauces I’ve made over the years, it hit me that I’ve never made a true queso dip. And when I started looking up recipes to work from it REALLY hit me how much different queso dip is from cheese sauces for other foods I’ve made, well… ever. I’ve done the Houston BBQ route before, and even jollof rice due to Houston’s large population of Nigerian descent. I did a little French cooking to be petty , and even a pho inspired soup because Houston also has a significant population of Vietnamese descent. Somehow I’ve avoided Tex-Mex this entire time. So here we are! Extra Spicy Queso Serves: 6 – 8 Active time: 20 minutes Total time: 30 minutes Ingredients 2 Tbsp butter, unsalted 4 cloves garlic 1 small bundle of green onions 1 Fresno pepper 1 Roma tomato 1/2 tsp black pepper 12 oz can of evaporated milk 2 Tbsp corn starch 1/2 cup water 1/2 cup hot sauce 2 Tbsp weapons grade hot sauce 1 tsp cumin 12 slices of American cheese 8 oz sharp cheddar cheese Salt to taste You will need: Sauce pan, some food to dip into the queso On low heat, melt butter in sauce pan While butter is melting, finely chop the white and light green section of the onions, setting aside the dark green section. Mince garlic and finely chop pepper (seeds optional) Stir onions, garlic, pepper, and black pepper into butter, and cook for 2 – 3 minutes Finely chop half the tomato and stir into the butter (chop and reserve the other half for garnish) Increase heat to medium while combining evaporated milk, corn starch, water, and hot sauces Stir liquid into sauce pan and bring to heat just below a simmer (if you see bubbles back it off) Stir in cumin Slice green sections of onions into little rings (about 1/4 cup) and stir in (you can reserve some of these for garnish too) Add American cheese and stir in Cube Cheddar cheese and stir in Stir frequently until cheese is fully melted and sauce has slightly thickened. Add salt to taste. Service with some dippables Wingin’ It tips This is an incredibly easy recipe and mostly fool proof. I stuck to lower heat to avoid scorching and used the cheese trick from my other cheese sauce styles. A lot of folks will tell you to use shredded cheese and I have two issues with that. You might be tempted to buy it pre-shredded and then you have the added stuff that prevents clumping going in your sauce which dulls the flavor. More importantly, cheese sauces almost always need time to thicken a bit. Even if you shred your own cheese it will melt right away. That’s a good thing, right? Not really. When you do that you then need to stir and wait for the thickening. You need to keep a very close eye on what looks like the same sauce over time. When you use chunks or little blocks of cheese, it becomes a natural timer. By the time cubes melt in this, you’ve had enough time to thicken as well. I have a few pictures, but mainly to show off what I mean with the various chopping/mincing/dicing sizes and what I mean by one bundle of onions. Give me money. Money me. Money now. title: Panthers fan bullish for future, but not for Week 1
summary: This week we asked fans of the Carolina Panthers two simple questions: In short, these were questions about the short term and long term success of the team. It’s hard to look at the work that general manager Dan Morgan and head coach Dave Canales have done and say that this team isn’t improving. It’s […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 06: Bryce Young #9 of the Carolina Panthers and Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears embrace after the game at Soldier Field on October 06, 2024 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images This week we asked fans of the Carolina Panthers two simple questions: Are you confident the Panthers are headed in the right direction? Do you expect them to beat the Bears? In short, these were questions about the short term and long term success of the team. It’s hard to look at the work that general manager Dan Morgan and head coach Dave Canales have done and say that this team isn’t improving. It’s a short stretch from there to saying that you expect things to keep improving in the future. So it’s not surprising that a whopping 80% of Panthers fans are confident the team is heading in the right direction. It’s all hard to look at where the team today came from and say that you expect any sort of success in the near future. Even with last season’s admirable showing in the playoffs against the Los Angeles Rams, saying you expect the Panthers to beat the Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams led Chicago Bears seems like a stretch. Never mind that Johnson is a younger and more recent head coach hire than Canales and that Williams is a younger and less experienced player than Bryce Young. Do mind that the Panthers have yet to translate a hot December/January into an even mildly competent September. That’s how you get only 45% of fans expecting the Panthers to win their first home opener in years. Plenty more probably think they could win, but expecting a positive result is a whole different ball game. We probably could have gotten a stronger result in favor of the Panthers if we asked people if they thought favoring the Bears -3 over the Panthers was overly generous towards Chicago. But that’s not what I’m interested in. I’m interested in the difference between people thinking things are going to be alright eventually and expecting them to be good now. I’m curious to see the drop in confidence after a Panthers loss on Sunday through extremely familiar events in spite of these seemingly low expectations from fans. I guess we only have a few more hours to wait to see how this particular cookie crumbles.
