title: 5 Qs with Windy City Gridiron
summary: The regular season is back and that means weekly interviews with our fellow, opposing bloggers. This week I spoke with Bill Zimmerman of Windy City Gridiron for all things Caleb Williams, Colston Loveland, and Xavier Woods. Read on for the other side’s perspective on the Carolina Panthers vs the Chicago Bears in Week 1. I […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OH - AUGUST 22: Chicago Bears tight end Colston Loveland (84) talks with quarterback Caleb Williams (18) and tight end Cole Kmet (85) during the preseason game between the Chicago Bears and the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Cincinnati, OH. (Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The regular season is back and that means weekly interviews with our fellow, opposing bloggers. This week I spoke with Bill Zimmerman of Windy City Gridiron for all things Caleb Williams, Colston Loveland, and Xavier Woods. Read on for the other side’s perspective on the Carolina Panthers vs the Chicago Bears in Week 1. I have a long running deal with the Panthers where if they play actually good football then I will ask actually serious questions. Since this is the start of the season I struck a largely respectful tone. We’ll see where things go from here. The Carolina Panthers are going to need to start and finish on the ground for most of their wins this season, which gets tricky when their two starting offensive tackles are out for extended time to start the season. How was the Bears rushing defense in 2025 and what has changed about it with this year’s roster? The run defense was not good in 2025. By season’s end, the Bears found themselves 27 th in rushing yards allowed per game, and 29 th in yards per attempt (5.0). They struggled to stop the run for most of the season. They did a better job against the run in the playoffs, but the Packers and Rams still had moments of success. Not a lot has changed with personnel. The Bears traded Gervon Dexter, who was a weaker run defender, away for secondary help and a draft pick, and they replaced Andrew Billings with Neville Gallimore, who, again, I think is a weaker run defender than the player he’s replacing. TJ Edwards is a solid run defender, and he returns, but they let Tremaine Edmunds walk and replaced him with Devin Bush. It’ll be curious to see how Bush defends the run in Dennis Allen’s scheme. The defense is definitely faster, and hopefully with that added speed they can swarm to the ball faster than they did last year, but other than Montez Sweat, who I would call a strong run defender, there are going to be plenty of opportunities for the Panthers’ running backs to get some yards through large holes. Ironically, one of the Panthers few bona fide strengths is their wide receiver corps. What is the strength of the Bears secondary? I think the strength of the Bears secondary is simply Jaylon Johnson. This defense is probably going to struggle in all facets of stopping opponents. Kyler Gordon is an excellent Nickel, but he’s on IR and won’t play. Coby Bryant was brought in to replace Kevin Byard, but he was also injured and is also on IR. The Bears’ starting secondary after Jaylon Johnson is definitely beatable. Johnson has had an excellent camp and looks like he’s a lot closer to his All-Pro year than last season, when he played hurt and struggled. But the other two corners will be Cam Lewis (just a guy) and Tyrique Stevenson. Stevenson has been a playmaker in his three years in Chicago, but he also has lapses in concentration and gives up big plays because of it. Xavier Woods is a decent safety. He steps in for Bryant, and first-round pick Dillon Thieneman will be expected to develop quickly and help stabilize a secondary that is a lot weaker than the team expected it to be back in May. The Panthers defense has, mildly, struggled to limit production from the Tight End position in the past. Is there any chance that Colston Loveland or Cole Kmet will miss the game due to traffic, the birth of their children, or vague astrological distress? Now that’s a great question, haha. That may be the only way to stop Ben Johnson’s passing attack. As critical as I am of the defense, it’s the exact opposite of the offense. This passing game should be poetry in motion, and they are going to live in 12 and 13 personnel. The Bears drafted Sam Roush in the 2 nd round as their TE3, and he’s looked like he belongs in camp. Cole Kmet has become a Swiss Army Knife for this offense, and they use him everywhere, and he can do whatever Ben Johnson needs him to do. Colston Loveland’s second half last year was awesome, and you’d have to be living under a rock in Siberia to not see the hype around Loveland this offseason. I know the Panthers revamped their linebackers a little in hopes of slowing down tight ends, but their first assignment is going to be a very tall order. What improvements does Caleb Williams need to make over his 2025 form to take the next step? There were so many improvements in Caleb’s game from 2024 and even from the first few games of 2025 to the QB he was at the end of the season. As the season went on, he got more comfortable with Ben Johnson and more comfortable in the offense. That went a long way. He went from the most-sacked QB (at a near-record pace) in 2024 to one of the least-sacked QBs in 2025 with elite sack avoidance. And honestly, how he operated the offense in 2025 was also a big improvement from September to January. I say those things (even though you didn’t ask) to show that the growth is there and most expect it to continue. First of all, he doesn’t have to learn Ben Johnson’s complicated offense in the spring; he gets to hone his skills on an offense he already knows. The team as a whole needs to improve on the scramble drill. I think if that happens (and it has been a focus in practice), that’s going to make Caleb’s play-making abilities when he’s on the run even better. Some people will complain about his Time to Throw and his completion percentage. Most analysts who know QB play well don’t worry about those things too much. Caleb was a little inconsistent with his accuracy from the pocket, but his accuracy on the move is absurd. Assuming he’s more comfortable in the offense, I expect the accuracy and play in structure from the pocket to improve. Caleb is probably never going to be a guy with a 68% completion percentage. He’s probably going to be more like a 64% guy, which is totally fine the way he plays the game because he keeps his turnovers insanely low. His time to throw will always be high because of the way he tries to create on the move multiple times a game, but the key is when he does it, the defensive line has to get him to the ground. They could in 2024, and they couldn’t in 2025. The Panthers will have to see which year they can better copy this Sunday. Let’s keep it easy. What do you think the final score will be? I do think the Bears will win this one because I just think the offense is clicking already and will put up some numbers. I do think the Panthers are going to move the ball on the Bears as well, but just not at the same rate. I think we’ll see a 34-24 victory by Chicago on Sunday.

title: Weekly Stat Review: An introduction
summary: The Carolina Panthers had a busy offseason in an attempt to upgrade many elements of what was an unlikely playoff team in 2025. They found some intermittent success, but often struggled in of the most crucial areas of the sport. This series is meant to spotlight the statistics that represent some of these major problem […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NC - AUGUST 28: Panthers flag flies during a preseason NFL football game between the Houston Texans and the Carolina Panthers on August 28, 2026, at Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte, N.C.(Photo by John Byrum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Carolina Panthers had a busy offseason in an attempt to upgrade many elements of what was an unlikely playoff team in 2025. They found some intermittent success, but often struggled in of the most crucial areas of the sport. This series is meant to spotlight the statistics that represent some of these major problem areas the Panthers have tried to resolve and provide a way to keep track of the changes or trends throughout the season. It will be the short and sweet numbers with a dash of context each week; perhaps a deep dive or two once there’s enough of a sample to glean something worthwhile. The Watchlist Offense Explosive Play Rate Percentage of plays that qualify as an explosive play. Explosive plays being a carry of 10 or more yards or a pass attempt gaining 20 or more yards. Brad Idzik has taken over the play-calling duties for the offense and the Panthers have made several investments to try and foster the opportunities that were far too inconsistent in 2025. 2025: 8.8% (23rd in NFL) Pressure Rate Allowed Percentage of dropbacks with a pressure or sack allowed Heavy investments in the offensive line during the NFL Draft and Free Agency along with a handful of notable injuries to the 2025 incumbents make for an interesting stat to watch. Giving plays time to develop is crucial and can’t be done if the protection cannot hold up. 2025: 30.9% 3rd Down Conversion Rate Rate of 3rd downs that converted to 1st downs. Head Coach Dave Canales loves to talk about controlling the football and controlling the game. Hard to do if you are not able to keep the offense on the field. 2025: 36.5% (25th in NFL) Defense Zone Coverage Rate Percentage of coverage snaps spent in a zone defense. The Panthers defense under Ejiro Evero have some of the heaviest usage of zone coverage in the NFL the past few years. Will the changes of personel in all 3 levels of the defense shake the tendency or will it continue to hold true? 2025: 78% zone coverage Pressure Rate Percentage of pass rush opportunities that resulted in a sack or pressure. The Panthers were at the bottom of the league in 2025 and desperately need to improve if they want to consistently stifle opposing offenses. Prized free agent acquisition Jaelen Phillips will need to have a huge impact. 2025: 10.1% (31st in NFL) 3rd Down Stop Rate Rate of 3rd downs allowed to be converted into 1st downs. It’s not ideal if your offense can’t stay on the field and your defense can’t get off it. This stat will focus on the latter and show just how capable the defense is when it matters most. 2025: 48.1% (32nd in NFL) BONUS Stat of the Week This one will change on a weekly basis. Something interesting or noteworthy; could be specific to the most recent match-up or leaguewide ranking that stands out. Hope you enjoy following along and if you’ve got your own stats you’ll be keeping an eye on, feel free to drop them in the comments below.

title: 2026 Season Opener Countdown: 1 Day Remaining
summary: Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NC - SEPTEMBER 23: Carolina Panthers quarterback Cam Newton (1) does his signature superman move after scoring a rushing touchdown during the NFL game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Carolina Panthers on September 23 2018, at Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte,NC. (Photo by Dannie Walls/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to change that up a bit by counting down our own list of the Top 100 Panthers of all time. This does not correspond to jersey number, does not need to be somebody who wore a jersey, and will in no way be controversial. #1. Cam Newton How fitting that the player that comes in at number one on our countdown also wore the number one on his jersey. Serendipity. It’s Super Man himself, Cam Newton. The Panthers and their fans endured a season of Jimmy Clausen to earn the number one pick in the 2011 NFL Draft. The team was almost guaranteed to take a quarterback, and the debate was between dual threat Cam Newton out of Auburn and the more traditional passer Blaine Gabbert out of Missouri. The Panthers elected to take a shot on Newton, and it couldn’t have worked out better. There were all sorts of questions about Newton’s ability to actually throw the football when he entered the league, and the fact that he got very little runway into his rookie season because of the lockout only added to those concerns. He made his debut against the Arizona Cardinals, who clearly believed he couldn’t beat them with his arm, and lit them up for 422 passing yards and two touchdowns while adding a rushing touchdown on what would become his trademark super man dive over the pile on the goal line. He finished that season as the first rookie to ever throw for 4,000 yards, and he simultaneously set the record for rushing touchdowns by a quarterback with 14. Newton continued to redefine the quarterback position throughout his time in Carolina. He paired high difficulty passing productivity with elite rushing efficiency and was one of the best short yardage ball carriers in the league regardless of position. His ascent continued into 2015, where he turned in arguably the greatest season any Panther has put together. He led the team to 15-1 record with the only loss coming just a few days after Newton welcomed his first child into the world. In that season, Newton threw for 3,837 yards and 35 touchdowns against 10 interceptions while adding 636 yards and 10 more touchdowns on the ground. He led a league best four fourth quarter game winning drives. All of that unsurprisingly earned him MVP and Offensive Player of the Year honors. He is the only Panthers in the team’s history to win either award. And all of that happened with Ted Ginn as his number one wide receiver. The Panthers and Newton saw a major regression in 2016 after losing the Super Bowl. Newton missed a game with a concussion and was benched for the start of another because he didn’t wear a tie on the team flight . Derek Anderson started that game, threw an interception on the first play, and the Panthers went on to lose 40-7. The following week, Newton injured his throwing shoulder trying to make a tackle on an interception after wide receiver Kelvin Benjamin made a poor effort to catch the ball and then no effort to tackle the defender . That injury would dramatically impact Newton’s ability to generate velocity on his passes for the rest of his career. Despite his diminishing arm strength, Newton bounced back to lead another hodgepodge offense to an 11-5 record and playoff appearance in 2017, but that season ended with a playoff loss to the Saints. After a strong first half of 2018, Newton took a shot to the shoulder from TJ Watt during a game against the Steelers. His play would rapidly deteriorate from that point through the end of the season before he was deactivated for the final two games to get shoulder surgery. He played just two games in 2019 before a foot injury ended his season. After a year in New England, Newton made a triumphant return to Carolina midway through the 2021 season. He came in for special packages in a game against the Cardinals and was responsible for two touchdowns as the struggling Panthers pulled off a shocking blowout win over the then 8-1 Arizona Cardinals. Newton got more playing time as the season went on, but he was clearly not the player he once was. The Panthers limped to a 5-12 record after losing 12 of their last 14 games. Newton’s contract expired after that season, and he wouldn’t play another down in the NFL. Newton’s career was very enigmatic in a way. On one hand, he redefined the quarterback position and reinforced how much of a weapon the quarterback can be as a runner while still being a threat as a passer. His impact and talent were undeniable. On the other hand, his consistency and counting stats as a passer could fluctuate, though there was a lot of context around that as well. The bulk of Newton’s playing career came with Mike Shula as his offensive coordinator. Shula never received any head coaching interest despite the success of his Newton-led offenses, and he never led successful offenses that didn’t have Cam Newton at quarterback. At the same time, Newton’s best wide receivers were an aging Steve Smith, a rookie DJ Moore, and Ted Ginn Jr. Newton was heavily reliant on Greg Olsen at tight end to be his true number one receiver for most of his career. He rarely if ever had a good supporting cast at the skill positions, and most of his career was marred by subpar offensive coaching. While Newton’s career will go down as far and away the best we’ve seen at quarterback in Carolina, there are still questions about what could have been if the team did more to support him during his prime. Instead, he seemed to carry the weight of the offense on his own while the rest of the organization either did little to help or actively hampered what he was capable of doing. Still, he rose to the level of Most Valuable Player and took the team to a Super Bowl. Cam Newton is the best quarterback the Panthers have ever had, and the best player they have ever had. For that, number one in your programs comes in at number one on our countdown of the top 100 Carolina Panthers of all time.
author: Jonathan DeLong

title: The Chicago Bears are trying to defy history
summary: Chicago hopes to be a contender in 2026, and from Ryan Poles to Ben Johnson to Caleb Williams, the voices of the team are clear that the goal is a championship. But how likely is that? How quickly are championship teams built? General Managers Ten different general managers have been “responsible” for winning the last […]
full_text: Chicago hopes to be a contender in 2026, and from Ryan Poles to Ben Johnson to Caleb Williams, the voices of the team are clear that the goal is a championship. But how likely is that? How quickly are championship teams built? General Managers Ten different general managers have been “responsible” for winning the last sixteen Super Bowls. On average , these general managers needed to have the job for just over five years before they were able to win the big one for the first time, but “average” is a tricky measure when being applied to something so inherently rare. Likewise, while these GMs averaged only 3 years before their first playoff win on the job, there’s something…a little off about that measure, too. First, here’s a look at the GMs in question and how long it took them to reach certain markers. So, what stands out with this list is the success of Reese, Belichick, Veach, and Schneider. They had the fastest path to the Super Bowl, and they set the tone for the idea that Ryan Poles should reasonably be able to deliver a championship soon. However, each of those results needs some significant qualification. Reese (New York Giants): Jerry Reese took over the Giants in 2007 and oversaw the team that won in head coach Tom Coughlin’s fourth year. First-ballot Hall of Pretty Good quarterback Eli Manning was likewise in his fourth year. The team in question was coming off of back-to-back playoff runs, and the position was only open because Ernie Accorsi had retired. Belichick (New England Patriots): Bill Belichick took over the Patriots after Pete Carroll was fired, and in doing so he also supplanted Bobby Grier. Grier had overseen a 44-36 record as the director of player personnel in a run that included three playoff appearances with two different coaches. Grier did not even leave the team until after the 2000 NFL Draft (when Tom Brady was acquired), and the team had only had one losing season in the prior six years. Veach (Kansas City Chiefs): Brett Veach joined the Chiefs in 2013 alongside Andy Reid, and while he took over General Manager duties in 2017, that was only after John Dorsey had drafted Patrick Mahomes amid criticism and had overseen four consecutive winning seasons. Hence, Veach took over a team that already had a 43-21 record, the head coach who would win the Super Bowl for him, and the future 3-time MVP of the Super Bowl at quarterback. Schneider (Seattle Seahawks): John Schneider is a difficult general manager to categorize for multiple reasons, the most important of which is that for the Seahawks’ first run to a Super Bowl, Pete Carroll had authority over personnel. If Carroll is instead considered the general manager for that first Super Bowl run, the question then becomes how to categorize Schneider’s management of the team after Carroll’s departure–is it a new tenure or an extension of the prior one? However credit is assigned, though, the Seahawks went from back-to-back seasons with double-digit losses under Tim Ruskell to an NFL title in just four years. In other words, of the four executives on this list who managed a team to a title in under five years, only one actually took over a struggling team and turned it around that quickly. Clearly, limiting the discussion to general managers is problematic because the actual trend is that GMs either need more time or a strong foundation to build on in order to get their team to a title. Franchises Okay, if the better way of looking at things is by considering the franchise as being built into a winner, how long does it take for a franchise to go from being bad to the best ? What about terrible to best ? How often do bad teams really get turned into champions? Obviously this answer is complicated by the fact that in 2011 the fundamental way the draft fed into team building was permanently changed and also because free agency did not exist in a modern sense prior to 1993. However, for now, it’s simplest to simply look at two groups–the last ten Super Bowl champions and the last twenty Super Bowl champions. The last ten teams to win the Super Bowl had an average winning record of 63% in the five seasons prior to their championship run (mean and median both, conveniently). The last twenty teams see the number drop a little, but not much (to 61%, still both mean and median). In other words, the typical Super Bowl champion of the modern era stacks multiple seasons with double digit wins before they achieve a title. Only five of the twenty championship runs were preceded by average five-season records below .500. Simply put, teams typically need to be stable contenders before they break through. If a team is actually bad when it has back-to-back losing seasons, over the last twenty years the average length of time it takes a franchise to go from bad to best is 12.5 seasons, but that number is skewed heavily by the Denver Broncos winning a Super Bowl in 2016 but not having back-to-back losing seasons since 1972. In this case, the median of 10 seasons is probably more accurate. Narrowed to the last ten years, though, the average is that it takes 11.4 (mean) or 11.5 (median) seasons to go from confirmed losers to the best in the league. Only four teams went from bad to best in under five years (two in the last decade and two in the decade prior). What about really bad teams? What about teams that go from back-to-back seasons with double-digit losses to titles? Then it takes even longer. Over the last 20 years, the average in these cases is 16 years (median 15 years), but that number comes with an asterisk. That’s because the Ravens never had double-digit losing seasons and two other teams, the Broncos (1972) and the Steelers (1970) suffered seasons with comparable losing percentages so long ago that there were only 14 games in the season. Interestingly, those same averages apply over the last 10 years as well, though, when none of those asterisks apply. Only three teams in the last 20 years were less than seven seasons removed from bottoming out as represented by back-to-back 10-plus-loss seasons. Summary If the Chicago Bears were to win a championship in 2026, they would match the fastest turnaround in the last 20 years, wherein the Tampa Bay Buccaneers won a Super Bowl after having only 32 wins in the prior five seasons (the same as Chicago) and only two seasons removed from back-to-back 10-loss seasons (also the same as Chicago). In general , though, the “bottom” the team struck in 2017 would normally suggest that the team would not have been vying for a Super Bowl until 2024 or 2028. However, the team then added four consecutive seasons with at least ten losses under two separate GMs. With very few exceptions, precedent suggests that the team needs to be more focused on building a sustained winner to earn the chance at a title. Of course, it’s even more unlikely that either Ben Johnson or Caleb Williams will be content with anything short of making history.

title: Bears vs. Panthers: How to watch and listen, previews, odds, and more
summary: The Chicago Bears are on the road to face the Carolina Panthers in Week 1, and you might not realize it, but this is a battle between two defending division champs. The Bears took the North (and are never gonna give it back), while the Panthers won the NFC South. Sure, Carolina won it at […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 6: Officials break up a brawl between the Carolina Panthers and the Chicago Bears during the fourth quarter of an NFL football game, at Soldier Field on October 6, 2024 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears are on the road to face the Carolina Panthers in Week 1, and you might not realize it, but this is a battle between two defending division champs. The Bears took the North (and are never gonna give it back) , while the Panthers won the NFC South. Sure, Carolina won it at (8-9) while Chicago went (11-6), but first place is still first place, and it was the Panthers’ first one since 2015, so kudos to them! For the record, it was the Bears’ first division title since 2018, so both franchises hope to have turned a corner. The Panthers also nearly knocked off the Rams last season in the Wildcard round, but thanks to an L.A. touchdown with just 38 seconds left in the game, they were sent home 34 to 31. Speaking on the Rams, they played like a bunch of stuffed and buggered bludgers on Thursday in Australia! These two teams will always be linked because of the trade, which prompted the article below and, of course, also led to the Bears getting Caleb Williams. GAME INFO The Bears and Panthers will kick off at 12:00 pm CT from Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte, North Carolina. There’s a chance of a thunderstorm, and the high will be 90 °. TELEVISION The game will be on FOX with Adam Amin and Drew Brees on the call, and if you live in the blue area of this 506sports.com map, then you’ll get to see the game. With Adam Amin on the call this Sunday, our guy Bill Zimmerman asked him to jump on his podcast to help break things down. You can check out the podcast version here or the video version here . Adam was fantastic, as always, so those are a can’t-miss! RADIO ESPN Chicago (1000 AM, 100.3 FM HD2) with Jeff Joniak (play-by-play), Tom Thayer (analyst), and Jason McKie (sideline) on the call, and LATINO MIX 93.5 FM (Spanish) with Omar Ramos. ODDS The visiting Bears are a 3-point favorite, with the game total over/under at 47.5. title: Chicago Bears vs. Carolina Panthers Game Picks and Predictions
summary: The defending NFC North champion Chicago Bears take on the defending NFC South champion Carolina Panthers at Noon (CT) on Sunday, and the Windy City Gridiron crew makes their picks and predictions for the game right here. Lester A. Wiltfong Jr.: Bears will win, 27 to 16, behind 200 scrimmage yards from D’Andre Swift, but Kyle […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 6: Quarterback Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears scrambles out of bounds during the third quarter of an NFL football game against the Carolina Panthers, at Soldier Field on October 6, 2024 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The defending NFC North champion Chicago Bears take on the defending NFC South champion Carolina Panthers at Noon (CT) on Sunday, and the Windy City Gridiron crew makes their picks and predictions for the game right here. Lester A. Wiltfong Jr.: Bears will win, 27 to 16, behind 200 scrimmage yards from D’Andre Swift, but Kyle Monangai poaches 2 TDs away from him. The defense bends but doesn’t break, and Montez Sweat picks up a sack. Caleb Williams finishes at 64% completion, and “those” analysts complain it’s not 70%. Jacob Infante: Bears win 24-20. I think Carolina keeps things closer than most Bears fans are willing to admit, but Chicago still has the better roster, in my opinion. In classic Cardiac Bears fashion, Caleb Williams leads the team on a touchdown drive late in the fourth quarter, and an interception by Dillon Thieneman on a Bryce Young two-minute drill gives Chicago its first win of the year. Gary Baugher Jr.: 28-17 Bears. Bears pick up 350+ yards of offense, 2 passing TDs, and 2 rushing TDs. Bryce Young turns the ball over twice, and Tetairoa McMillan goes for 100+ on us, but otherwise we’re pleasantly surprised by our Week 1 defense. Josh Sunderbruch: Bears 30-26 with missed opportunities on both sides of the ball for Chicago to make it more definitive. Caleb has a touchdown in the air and on the ground. Motivated Dayo gets the strip sack, and JVDB gets the recovery. Sam Householder: Bears 24-20. It feels like a sleepy week one where sometimes it’s a bit messy, but overall a close game, and the Bears pull it out in the end. Jaylon Johnson gets a pick; Caleb throws a TD to Luther Burden and runs one in himself. Donald Gooch: Bears win 36-17. Caleb throws for 300 yards with touchdowns to Loveland and Rome. Swift goes off for 125 yards and a TD. On defense, Sweat and Booker notch sacks, and JJ gets an interception. The Bears’ run defense surprises everyone with its competence. Great start to the season. Superfans: Week 1 is often sloppy as both teams try to shake off the offseason rust, which is why this game is going to be a nail-biter. Caleb will fall short of 300 yards at only 299, and Loveland will only catch one touchdown. However, Rome and Luther and Kmet will each get a tuddy of their own. The Bears’ rushing attack will plod along as neither Swift nor Monangai can hit the century mark. They do, however, combine for 198 rushing yards and 2 TDs. A late peanut punch by T.J. Edwards followed by a scoop-and-score by Austin Booker allows the Bears to squeak by, 49 to 17. What is your prediction for Bears vs. Panthers?

title: Bears fans are confident the team is headed in the right direction
summary: We’re coming off one of the most exciting seasons in Chicago Bears history, and the offense is primed to be even more potent in year two of Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams working together. So it shouldn’t surprise you that our Week 1 fan survey shows 87% of us are confident the franchise is headed […]
full_text: Jul 31, 2026; Lake Forest, IL, USA; Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson talks to quarterback Caleb Williams (18) during Training Camp at Halas Hall. Mandatory Credit: Kamil Krzaczynski-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect We’re coming off one of the most exciting seasons in Chicago Bears history, and the offense is primed to be even more potent in year two of Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams working together. So it shouldn’t surprise you that our Week 1 fan survey shows 87% of us are confident the franchise is headed in the right direction. But a new season always brings hope, and it’s not just our fans who are confident; the other three NFC North fanbases mostly believe their favorite team is headed in the right direction too. The Reacts results for the Minnesota Vikings hit 60% this week. Green Bay Packers fans are 73% confident in their team. And fans of the Detroit Lions, who watched their team go from first in 2024 to worst in 2025, are at 89% With the entire NFC North kicking off their season tomorrow, I wanted to get one last look at their win totals from our friends at FanDuel Sportsbook . The Lions are at 10.5 wins, with the over at -125 and the under at +105. The Packers are -110 for over 9.5 wins and -110 for under. The Bears are also at 9.5 but are +105 for over and -130 for under. FanDuel has the Vikings over 8.5 Wins at -120, and under at even-money odds at +100. If you missed it, on Friday the Bears gave D’Andre Swift a 3-year, $33.75 million contract extension that includes $27.5 million guaranteed. The 27-year-old Swift is coming off his most productive season running the ball with 1,087 yards and 9 touchdowns. But it wasn’t just his numbers that impressed in 2025; it was his decisiveness when running the ball. Swift matured as a runner, as he took what the defense gave him, including knowing when to lower his shoulder and get the tough yards when needed. If you think Swift is going to have another productive season, his over/under for rushing yards at FanDuel is 800.5. Unless he’s hurt, that number seems likely. If you think the Bears are going to get off the bus running on Sunday against the Carolina Panthers, you can get Swift to go over 100 yards at +370.

title: 2026 NFL Power Rankings
summary: With week one upon us, let’s begin our NFL Power Rankings for the season. We started this last season, and we updated it at approximately 25%, 50%, 75%, and at the end of the regular season. Last season at the end of the regular season, we had the Seahawks first, the Patriots second, the Rams […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - FEBRUARY 08: Sam Darnold #14 of the Seattle Seahawks celebrates with the Vince Lombardi Trophy after winning Super Bowl LX against the New England Patriots at Levi's Stadium on February 08, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. The Seattle Seahawks defeated the New England Patriots 29-13. (Photo by Ronald Martinez/Getty Images) | Getty Images With week one upon us, let’s begin our NFL Power Rankings for the season. We started this last season, and we updated it at approximately 25%, 50%, 75%, and at the end of the regular season. Last season at the end of the regular season, we had the Seahawks first, the Patriots second, the Rams third, and the Broncos fourth. We also had three of the four divisional round losers ranked between 5 and 8. Not too bad. Let’s begin the rankings this season. Even though these rankings are out on a Saturday and four teams have played already, we are not looking at those two games in these rankings. These are the rankings I expected from these teams before the season kicked off. 1. Seattle Seahawks The Rams are the hot team to place atop the power rankings, but when the defending champions return most of their team, you gotta beat the man to be the man. 2. LA Rams Tough to not have the Rams in the top three. They certainly have all the makings to be the best team in the NFL this year. 3. Buffalo Bills It’ll be curious to see how Joe Brady looks as the head man, but I think Josh Allen and DJ Moore are poised to have a big year together, and this offense should roll. 4. Baltimore Ravens I think things just didn’t fire last year, and I think the Ravens will look like the team we are used to seeing over the last several years. 5. Denver Broncos I still don’t think Bo Nix is a guy that can lead a team to a Super Bowl, but the Broncos have a formidable roster and should contend all season long. 6. San Francisco 49ers It’s crazy to have three teams from the same division in the top six, but until I see the 49ers fall apart, I think their demise has been greatly exaggerated. 7. New England Patriots I expect some regression from this team this year, but tough to put the AFC Champions much lower than this. 8. Houston Texans The defense is legit. If CJ Stroud looks like 75% of the QB he was as a rookie, this team will be a serious problem. 9. Chicago Bears The defense is big-time concerning, but this offense is going to be one of the top three in the league, which should make for a lot of fun football games. 10. Kansas City Chiefs I will need to see the Chiefs below .500 again to believe that the window is totally closed on Andy Reid and Patrick Mahomes. 11. Los Angeles Chargers With Jim Harbaugh, Justin Herbert, and now Mike McDaniel, it’s tough to think this team won’t be back in the AFC Playoffs. 12. Philadelphia Eagles The Cowboys are the trendy pick to win the East, but I still give the (slight) edge to Philly to win the division. This is a big year for Jalen Hurts; if he struggles, his future here may be in doubt. 13. Dallas Cowboys They have plenty of pieces. But I need to see elite play to believe it from this squad. Until I see it, this is still the Cowboys, and they haven’t exactly been reliable. 14. Jacksonville Jaguars It may just be decades of bias against the Jaguars, but this is a team I need to see back atop the AFC South to think they’ve fully turned the corner. They feel closer to a .500 team to me. 15. Minnesota Vikings If the Vikings went 9-8 with JJ McCarthy, Carson Wentz, and Max Brosmer last year, there’s no reason to think they can’t be better with Kyler Murray. 16. Cincinnati Bengals Another trendy preseason pick; I need to see it come together before I believe it. Another team that I think is closer to .500 than a Super Bowl contender. 17. Detroit Lions I think the Super Bowl window has closed on the Lions already, but they are still a playoff contender. I think we will learn how important Ben Johnson really was to their success. 18. Green Bay Packers The Packers are a consensus top-10 team on most power rankings, but I think this team has the most questions of anyone in the North. With Micah Parsons out for several games and Josh Jacobs on the Commish list, this has the makings of a year where they struggle more than people expect them to. 19. Pittsburgh Steelers This is basically the same team except Aaron Rodgers is a year older, and they downgraded the head coach. I don’t think the Steelers are a sleeper team; I think they finally have a losing record for the first time in a long, long time. 20. New Orleans Saints We haven’t ranked any NFC South teams, and the Saints are my pick to win a terrible division. I think Tyler Shough is a legit QB1 in this league. Not sure if he’s anything more than top 16 or so when he settles in, but that’s still going to work. 21. Tampa Bay Buccaneers The Bucs really faded down the stretch last year, and I think that’s probably closer to reality right now. Baker needs to play as he did in the first half for a full season for this to change. 22. New York Giants The Giants are improved, but I don’t think they will be some surprise playoff team. They will keep games closer and be entertaining in plenty of ways, but I think they are a year away. 23. Carolina Panthers This is the make-or-break year for Bryce Young, and I think it’s probably going to be a break, and the Panthers will decide to draft a QB next year. 24. Indianapolis Colts The Colts were the NFL darlings for the first half of the season, but I just don’t believe in Daniel Jones and think they are closer to the team that faded in the second half than the surprise team of the first half. 25. Washington Commanders Jayden Daniels needs to recoup all his magic that vanished last year for this team to have a chance. 26. Las Vegas Raiders I hope Fernando Mendoza plays sooner rather than later. Sitting for a few games to get used to the weekly NFL routine is fine, but sitting for 10 or 12 games or the whole season does not help a rookie QB. 27. Tennessee Titans I think the Titans have some parts, and I think Robert Saleh is a better coach than he gets credit for, but they are still a bad organization, and I don’t pick bad orgs to win many football games. 28. Cleveland Browns The worst QB situation in the league by far. The Deshaun Watson contract is the worst in the history of sports. Not the NFL. Sports. 29. Atlanta Falcons I don’t believe in this team. I think their QB approach this season is baffling. And I think this will be the Saquon Barkley Giants 2.0. You don’t pick the running back if the team is nowhere close to winning. Bijan Robinson makes no sense here. 30. New York Jets Some people like the Jets, but it’s the Jets, and it’s Geno Smith who didn’t look like he could play anymore. The Jets are the first team that I think is trying to March to Arch. 31. Arizona Cardinals The Jets tried to cover up their tanking; the Cardinals are about as open about it as any other team (except one). You don’t start Jacoby Brissett if you are actually trying to win more games than you lose. #MarchToArch 32. Miami Dolphins The only team being more obvious about it than the Cardinals. If you are a good player on Miami, you probably weren’t back this year (why did they keep Devon Achane?). The only thing that can save them is if Malik Willis has a magical season and plays like a top-10 QB.

title: Chicago Bears @ Carolina Panthers: Week 1 Players to Watch
summary: The NFL season is always evolving. Week 1 offers more unknowns than any other, especially when considering new players, coaches and schemes. In this weekly series, I’ll feature one player from the Chicago Bears opponent on each side of the ball who I think is integral to their team’s success. Like seasons past, you won’t […]
full_text: CHICAGO, IL - NOVEMBER 09: Derrick Brown #95 of the Carolina Panthers lines up during an NFL football game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on November 9, 2023 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL season is always evolving. Week 1 offers more unknowns than any other, especially when considering new players, coaches and schemes. In this weekly series, I’ll feature one player from the Chicago Bears opponent on each side of the ball who I think is integral to their team’s success. Like seasons past, you won’t see any quarterbacks, as the nature of the position always makes them critical for a team’s success. I’ll also try and mix in a few under the radar players form time to time. Let’s start with the Carolina Panthers offensive player that I will be focused on. Offense: Jonathon Brooks, RB The Panthers are a team known for grinding out tough yards on the ground and keeping the chains moving. A year ago it was Rico Dowdle leading the charge due to injuries to starter Chuba Hubbard and second year back Jonathon Brooks. Fast forward a year and the Panthers front-office felt comfortable enough in the recovery of both Hubbard and Brooks to let 2025 leading rusher Dowdle leave in free-agency. While I absolutely expect Hubbard to be the bell cow in week one, Brooks is the type of talent that can break the game open with a short pass to the house or couple 20+ runs to get the offense moving and keep Chicago off-balance. By all accounts Brooks has had an excellent summer and the Carolina coaches couldn’t stop raving about hi and it’s easy to understand why. The 6’0” 210lb back out of Texas was universally lauded as the top back in the ‘24 class, despite suffering a knee injury that ended his collegiate career early and set his pro career back some. If he is finally healthy enough to play like himself, I expect his 4.4 speed, impressive acceleration and underrated receiving ability to be problematic for the opposition all season. It just so happens that ends up being Chicago this week. If newly acquired Devin Bush and Co. can keep him in check, I like Chicago’s chances to outscore the Panthers big. But if he provides the spark his coaches have seen in camp, this could be another high-scoring shootout. Defense: Derrick Brown, DT In my opinion, Derrick Brown is easily one of the top 5 DTs in the entire league and has only played Chicago twice in his six-year career – both losses – but made his impact in each game. In his last contest against the Bears in 2023, Brown notched 10 tackles (9 solo) with 2 TFL and 2 QBH. As a DT, that is insane. Former Bear RG Teven Jenkins highlighted Brown after their battle that day and compared the former Auburn Tiger to All-Pro Dexter Lawrence. If that name sounds familiar, it should. Lawrence just wreaked havoc on our current offensive line in their joint practices this summer and appears to have single-handedly revamped the Cincinnati Bengals defense. Considering Derrick Brown has some reinforcements going in to battle with him this time around, Chicago must come ready to play. I will be eagerly observing how new Center Garret Bradberry holds up against the 6’5”, 320lb monster. But no doubt, Joe Thuney and Jonah Jackson will help out as well. If they can hold their own against Brown and allow Caleb to have time to operate in the passing game while giving the RBs time and space to maneuver in the run game, this one should be no problem for Chicago. But if Brown once again does his best Dexter Lawrence impression, watch out Bears fans. What about you? Which Carolina player will you be watching closely this week?

title: Bears Looking to Turn Offseason Work Into Results in Week 1
summary: As the Chicago Bears head into Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season, the anticipation is finally giving way to football. With the Bears set to open their season Sunday against the Carolina Panthers, head coach Ben Johnson met with the media Friday before the regular-season opener.  With kickoff just days away, Johnson reflected on […]
full_text: Aug 22, 2026; Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson stands on the sidelines during the second half in the game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Katie Stratman-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect As the Chicago Bears head into Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season, the anticipation is finally giving way to football. With the Bears set to open their season Sunday against the Carolina Panthers, head coach Ben Johnson met with the media Friday before the regular-season opener. With kickoff just days away, Johnson reflected on training camp and the offseason as a whole. Throughout camp, Johnson’s tone regarding the team has been noticeably different than it was last offseason. He has shown a great deal of optimism around this team. That optimism appears to stem, in large part, from the work Johnson has seen from his players throughout the offseason. He’s spoken highly of their willingness to put in the extra time, hard work, and effort it takes to become a real contender this year. Johnson pointed to the effort he’s seeing on a regular basis, noting that it gives the Bears a better chance to succeed on Sundays. Ben Johnson believes the Bears are practicing at a championship level entering 2026. Sarah Denicolo has more.“Here’s what I’m excited about: how hard [the players] are working on a regular basis right now,” Johnson said. “I think I made a comment last year about we’re not practicing at a championship level yet, and I’m not saying that this year. These guys, the work that they’re putting in throughout the week, it doesn’t guarantee you a win on Sunday, but it gives you a darn chance. So, I’m happy about what I’m seeing from all those guys, and as a result of that, they all get better.” #Bears HC Ben Johnson on the team going into this year: “Here’s what I’m excited about: I think I made a comment last year about how we’re not practicing at a championship level yet. I’m not saying that this year.” pic.twitter.com/kzBoGgMoMk — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) September 11, 2026 In the first few weeks of last season, the Bears played sloppy football. A plethora of penalties and mistakes highlighted a lack of attention to detail, something Johnson acknowledged when he said the team was not yet practicing at a championship level. This year, however, Johnson is pleased with the meaningful progress the team has made in that area. The difference isn’t simply about how hard the Bears are working. It’s about developing the habits necessary to consistently execute at a high level. Developing a strong work ethic and attention to detail were points of emphasis for the team during the offseason, along with game management and end-of-half situational football, as Johnson noted during Friday’s presser. “We’ll see if we can bring that to light or not, but it takes some coordination of all three phases working together,” Johnson said. On Sunday’s season opener, we’ll see how the hard work the Bears’ players and coaches have put in throughout the offseason translates to the regular season. Will that work immediately translate into improved execution, or will the team need a few weeks to fully gel? Either way, Sunday will provide the first real test of whether the progress Johnson has seen throughout the offseason can carry over when the games count.

Bengals News Joe Giles-Harris, Tanner Hudson Elevated | BENGALS ROSTER UPDATE The Bengals today elevated LB Joe Giles-Harris and TE Tanner Hudson from the practice squad to the active roster for tomorrow’s game against Tampa Bay. What to know before betting on the Cincinnati Bengals this season Playoff odds to recommendations and more, The Enquirer’s Shelby Dermer breaks down what to know before placing a bet on the Cincinnati Bengals season. title: 4 key matchups to watch for in Bengals vs. Buccaneers
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals will kick off their 2026 season Sunday when they host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. It will be one of the best games of the opening week, as the Bucs are favored to win the NFC South, while the Bengals are expected to contend with the Baltimore Ravens atop the AFC North. If […]
full_text: Cincinnati Bengals offensive tackle Amarius Mims (71) walks off the field after a loss to the Baltimore Ravens Sunday October 6, 2024 at Payor Stadium. The Bengals lost 41-38 in overtime. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Cincinnati Bengals will kick off their 2026 season Sunday when they host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . It will be one of the best games of the opening week, as the Bucs are favored to win the NFC South, while the Bengals are expected to contend with the Baltimore Ravens atop the AFC North. If the Bengals are going to start 1-0, here are four matchups they need to win. Amarius Mims vs. Rueben Bain Jr. Bain was the Buccaneers’ first-round pick during the 2026 NFL Draft. He surprisingly fell to the 15th overall pick and was not pleased. He will be playing with a chip on his shoulder when the Buccaneers face off against Cincinnati on Sunday. For the Bengals, Amarius Mims is looking to continue ascending toward an All-Pro season. There are just not many offensive linemen with his combination of size and athleticism. The expectation is that Bain and Mims will be matched up for much of the afternoon this week. This could be a classic battle of the unstoppable force versus the immovable object. If Mims can keep Bain from wrecking shop, the Bengals receivers should be able to feast on the Buccaneers secondary. Dexter Lawrence vs. Bucs Interior O-Line The Buccaneers interior offensive line consists of Ben Bredeson, Graham Barton, and Cody Mauch. All three players will have their hands full with the Bengals’ massive defensive tackle addition in Dexter Lawrence. Lawrence commands a ton of attention, and that will continue on Sunday. If Lawrence can still create havoc on the interior with all of that attention, it is going to open up the rest of the Bengals’ revamped defensive line to make plays. Lawrence should help free up his fellow defensive linemen, but also allow for the young second-year linebackers to have opportunities to make splash plays against the run near the line of scrimmage. Chase Brown vs. Alex Anzalone and Josiah Trotter Chase Brown will be used in a variety of ways to get the ball in his hands. The Bengals would love to find ways to get him matched up against Trotter out in space as a receiver. Trotter was the Buccaneers’ second-round draft pick this past season. He is a classic downhill thumper against the running game, but was susceptible to giving up big plays against him in the passing game at Missouri. If the Bengals can exploit that matchup this week, Chase Brown should have a massive week one game. The Buccaneers also added veteran Alex Anzalone this offseason at linebacker. Anzalone had previously played for the Detroit Lions. Orlando Brown Jr. vs. Yaya Diaby With Mims drawing the matchup with Bain a lot on the right side of the Bengals’ offensive line, it will be Orlando Brown Jr. going up against Diaby on Joe Burrow’s blindside. Diaby had seven sacks during the 2025 season. I would expect the Bengals to employ a lot of Drew Sample and Erick All over on that side of the field during this game. Brown Jr. was credited with allowing 46 pressures, nine sacks, and 10 recorded penalties during the 2025 season. He has to play better this season in order for the Bengals to achieve the goals they want to achieve this season. That needs to start on Sunday against Diaby and the Buccaneers’ defense.

title: Browns 2026 season: What a good Week 1 would actually look like
summary: Winning is always the main goal each week; however, the Cleveland Browns have several other factors to consider in Week 1 when determining whether the team delivered a strong performance. The team should look prepared. There has been significant transition within the organization over the past few months, including a new coaching staff and continued changes within the […]
full_text: Winning is always the main goal each week; however, the Cleveland Browns have several other factors to consider in Week 1 when determining whether the team delivered a strong performance. The team should look prepared. There has been significant transition within the organization over the past few months, including a new coaching staff and continued changes within the quarterback room. The hope is that all of these changes don’t result in a messy showing. Penalties, poor game management, turnovers, and missed assignments could indicate that the team is not organized or fully prepared for the season ahead. A lot of these things were things readers noted they were looking forward to: Another key factor will be whether the offense can consistently move the ball. For several seasons, the Browns have often started games with an impressive scripted opening drive, only for the offense to struggle and stall for much of the rest of the game. It will be encouraging to see whether the offense can sustain consistent drives throughout the game while creating opportunities for different players to make an impact. With expectations low among both fans and the media this season, it will be important to see the level of effort the team brings to this matchup. It won’t be just about the big moments and highlights shared on social media. It will ultimately come down to whether individual players consistently execute the little things necessary to give the team a chance to win. We asked one other question to Browns fans this week, and it involved them predicting how things will go in Week 1. Overall, the fanbase is not predicting a win, as 76% of them selected Jacksonville to win, compared to 24% for the Browns. Our DBN staff is a tad more optimistic when we made our predictions this week . There was also one national poll this week that had some relevancy to the Browns, asking which team was most likely to go from worst to first this season. The Detroit Lions ran away with the vote, understandably so. The Browns were all the way at the bottom, lumped into a tiny fraction of the vote with the Jets and Cardinals. title: Browns DC Mike Rutenberg: ‘We’re arriving with bad intentions’
summary: The Cleveland Browns will sport a new defensive look when they take the field on Sunday for their Week 1 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars.  Some of those changes are by design: defensive end Jared Verse replaces Myles Garrett, linebacker Quincy Williams replaces Devin Bush, and defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg takes over for Jim Schwartz.  […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - AUGUST 27: Defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg of the Cleveland Browns looks on prior to a preseason game against the New England Patriots at Huntington Bank Field on August 27, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images The Cleveland Browns will sport a new defensive look when they take the field on Sunday for their Week 1 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Some of those changes are by design: defensive end Jared Verse replaces Myles Garrett, linebacker Quincy Williams replaces Devin Bush, and defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg takes over for Jim Schwartz. There were some unexpected changes, however, most notably along the defensive line, after defensive end Alex Wright, who was expected to be a starter, was lost for the season to a torn Achilles tendon. That led general manager Andrew Berry to bring in veterans Sam Williams and Derek Barnett, and Rutenberg to experiment with Michael Hall Jr. at defensive end. Rutenberg had his weekly press conference on Thursday and addressed several topics. Here are four takeaways from what he had to say. The impact of Jared Verse There are no bigger shoes to fill for a defensive player than those of Myles Garrett, who picked up his second Defensive Player of the Year Award in 2025 after bagging an NFL-record 23 sacks. Garrett is now with the Los Angeles Rams, while Verse is in Cleveland and bringing his own style to the defense, according to Rutenberg : “(Jared’s) such a unique guy. He’s really like a unicorn in that he sets a standard with his play style and who he is. Really, what we saw early is what we continue to get. He sets that standard from the jump, in meetings, great questions, great insight. And then on the practice field, his standard of not only performance but style, and how hard he plays, has been the same every day. It’s really cool to see.” Working in the new guys on the defensive line Adding veterans is nice, especially for a team that is in the second year of a youth movement, but adding them so close to the start of the season is not always ideal. Especially with everyone on the defense already working with a new defensive coordinator and not necessarily able to quickly bring the new guys up to speed. But so far everything has gone smoothly with Barnett and Williams, according to Rutenberg : “It’s awesome to get new guys. The nature of this league is that you get new players, and those guys have worked as hard as you could possibly imagine. They’ve worked their butts off. Derek’s obviously been in it. Sam’s had experience in it. Those guys are pros, man. They approach it the right way. We’ve got a great defensive line coaching staff, starting with Jacques (Cesaire), Ralph (Street), Laroy (Reynolds), Shaq (Wilson), and together they’re preparing really hard. It’s really cool to see.” finding a way to win on defense @GetSpectrum | #DawgPound pic.twitter.com/pREF2cg2NZ — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) September 10, 2026 A defense with bad intentions All through training camp and the preseason, Rutenberg has talked about how “the ball is oxygen,” and the defense needs it to survive. He also wants his defense to have a very particular mindset when it takes the field : “When the ball is thrown, we’re arriving with bad intentions. We’re built off that. We choose violence in everything we do, and it doesn’t have to be a tackle; ball’s in the air, we’re knocking it out. That’s what we’re built off. We do our job so my brother can do his; I do mine and a little bit more. And our guys have done that. They do it in practice; they do it in walk-through. It’s awesome to see. “I’m excited to watch us play as hard as possible. I can’t wait just to watch us celebrate together. I can’t wait to see our preparation hopefully come to life. We’re built off violence, and that’s what we’re looking for in every play.” The ultimate goal Far too often, fans and media focus on sacks and turnovers as the only sign that a defense is successful. Those are fun, no doubt, but pressuring a quarterback into a bad throw is just as helpful. And turnovers are not something that a defense can control. For Rutenberg, however, there is only one clear goal : “Win. Win. I want to help the Browns win. I learned that from Jeff Ulbrich, man. Raheem Morris used to say, ‘help the team win on defense. Find a way to help the team win on defense.’ It’s a team game; we’re a team staff, Browns helping Browns, man. I want to help this team win.” The Browns and Jaguars kick off the NFL season on Sunday at 1 p.m. Stay with Dawgs By Nature throughout the weekend for full coverage, and be sure to download the app to enhance your gameday experience. summary: There was a time when the NFL and college football schedules would overlap for most of the start of the season. Now, with Week 0 and NIL running wild in college-ish sports, and the NFL moving the schedule in whatever way they see fit, including a Wednesday night game to open the season, the schedules […]
full_text: COLUMBUS, OHIO - AUGUST 30: Quarterback Arch Manning #16 of the Texas Longhorns tackled by Linebacker Arvell Reese #8 of the Ohio State Buckeyes and Defensive end Caden Curry #92 of the Ohio State Buckeyes during the game at Ohio Stadium on August 30, 2025 in Columbus, Ohio. (Photo by Jason Mowry/Getty Images) | Getty Images There was a time when the NFL and college football schedules would overlap for most of the start of the season. Now, with Week 0 and NIL running wild in college-ish sports , and the NFL moving the schedule in whatever way they see fit, including a Wednesday night game to open the season, the schedules are not so intertwined. For the Cleveland Browns, Week 1 of the NFL season brings them down to Jacksonville, Florida , to take on the Jaguars, followed by another trip to Florida in Week 2 versus the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. For the Ohio State Buckeyes, Week 2 of their season sees a huge matchup with the Texas Longhorns on Saturday night. The eyes of the football world will be upon the game due to the importance of the matchup between the top-ranked Buckeyes and the fourth-ranked Longhorns. NFL draft prospects, starting with QB Arch Manning , will be all over the field, which will create even more attention from the pro level. Given the timing of the game, a night contest in Austin, GM Andrew Berry will not be in attendance to watch one of the assumed top quarterbacks in the 2027 NFL draft. title: Browns keeping all 4 QB’s could pay off sooner rather than later as NFL injuries start
summary: The deadline for all 32 teams in the NFL to trim their rosters to 53 has passed, and Week 1 has started. During the first major roster decisions, the Cleveland Browns were one of the many teams that had difficult decisions to make. The one decision that surprised everyone is the QB room. There was […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - JUNE 10: Deshaun Watson #4, Shedeur Sanders #2, Dillon Gabriel #6 and Taylen Green #15 of the Cleveland Browns run a drill during the Cleveland Browns Mandatory Minicamp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on June 10, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The deadline for all 32 teams in the NFL to trim their rosters to 53 has passed , and Week 1 has started. During the first major roster decisions, the Cleveland Browns were one of the many teams that had difficult decisions to make. The one decision that surprised everyone is the QB room. There was a lot of speculation about how the Browns were going to handle the room, but the team decided to surprise everyone. Quarterbacks Deshaun Watson, Dillon Gabriel, Shedeur Sanders, and Taylen Green all stuck around. Watson, Sanders, and Green are on the 53-man roster, while Gabriel deals with a back injury that seemed to pop up out of nowhere. The Browns aren’t the only team that kept four quarterbacks around: 4 teams (Browns, Eagles, Vikings, Falcons) carrying 4 QBs is… something. — Nate Tice (@Nate_Tice) August 30, 2026 Could that decision soon pay off? Excluding Watson, due to his contract, the other QB’s on this roster were the talking point in terms of whether to keep them or not. Let’s start with Shedeur Sanders. Sanders, who is the most popular QB in the room and the backup to Watson has been discussed at length. From “if he will be the starter” or “if the team will cut him”, it’s always a conversation. The information that we have gathered surrounding Sanders is that the team never planned to cut him at any point. In terms of trading Sanders, the team may not have received too many calls before the season started. Another quarterback that has been the talk of trade rumors is Gabriel. As the QB battle between Sanders and Watson continued throughout training camp, Gabriel found himself on the outside looking in. Gabriel’s ceiling has already been defined as a backup quarterback. Considering that the Browns took another QB in this past draft, Gabriel became the talk of many trade/cut rumors. The 53-man roster has come out, and Gabriel was placed on the IR, keeping him around. The Browns placed QB Dillon Gabriel on IR with a back injury. So, he will miss at least the first four games of the season and Cleveland carries 3 QBs on its 53-man roster: Deshaun Watson Shedeur Sanders Taylen Green — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) August 30, 2026 Taylen Green, who the team drafted in the sixth round, was a tricky situation. Green is uber athletic but raw as a passer. Considering how Green looked in the preseason finale, if the Browns chose to cut Green the talented quarterback probably wouldn’t have cleared waivers, as it’s likely another team would’ve claimed him. Like Gabriel, Green had rare opportunities to get practice reps, but when he got them, he made the most of it. Now, with two games in the books for the 2026 NFL season, the need for quarterbacks around the league has already picked up. Sam Darnold was injured in the first half of the first game of the season. While he’s expected to be back soon, the vagueness of his hip injury is something to monitor. Former Cleveland HC Kevin Stefanski is already starting his third-string quarterback, Cooper Rush, with Michael Penix Jr. and Tua Tagovailoa hurt heading into their first contest. While Watson’s contract makes him untradeable, the Browns decision to keep all four quarterbacks around could pay off if teams continue to see attrition at the position around the league. Could the stability of Gabriel intrigue a team enough to fork over a Day 2 or high Day 3 draft pick and/or a quality player, once the diminutive QB is off IR? Could the upside and excitement of either Sanders or Green see a team make a play for a different Cleveland backup? The Browns may not have the quarterback of their future on the roster, but it is possible the depth of options they have at the position means they have the quarterback of another team’s immediate future.

title: 5 things to watch when the Cowboys play the Giants
summary: The time has finally arrived. The Dallas Cowboys are going to play a regular-season football game, and what better way to kick off their 2026 season than opening things up with a familiar foe, the New York Giants. Starting the year with a nice road win is a great way to get things going, but […]
full_text: The time has finally arrived. The Dallas Cowboys are going to play a regular-season football game, and what better way to kick off their 2026 season than opening things up with a familiar foe, the New York Giants. Starting the year with a nice road win is a great way to get things going, but it won’t be easy. These revamped Giants have upgraded their skill positions and upgraded their head coach, bringing in Super Bowl champion John Harbaugh from Baltimore. There are many things to occupy our attention, but here are five things to watch when the Cowboys travel to MetLife Stadium on Sunday night. 1. Confusing Jaxson Dart The Giants have a fearless, playmaking quarterback who has brought excitement back to Jersey with an impressive rookie résumé of big plays. Whether he’s dazzling with his arm or taking off and strutting his smash’em, crash’em rushing appeal, he somehow finds a way to get it done. When he’s in rhythm, he can be an efficient operator with quick decisions and well-placed intermediate throws. And if he doesn’t like what he sees, he’ll go off script and use the legs to extend plays and see what develops. The hope is Dart won’t like what he sees after the ball is snapped. The second-year quarterback can be a little Jekyll-and-Hyde, with the Hyde part possibly coming out if he is forced off of his primary look. Jeckyl : Dart led the league in big-time throws while under pressure (10.2%) Hyde: He was bottom in the league in turnover-worthy plays (15) Cowboys’ new defensive coordinator, Christian Parker, will face his first test subject as the team employs its new deceit defense, disguising their intentions and then rotating late. Dart is the perfect victim. The goal is to make him hold on to the ball too long, and when he tries to play hero, step in front of his receiver and make him pay. Snap your fingers, and the ball goes to Dallas. 2. Interior attack The Cowboys’ defense was notoriously bad last season, but no NFC team allowed more rushing yards last year than the Giants. They surrendered 145 rushing yards per game. Making matters even worse is the team traded away their best interior defender in Dexter Lawrence who was shipped to Cincinnati right before the NFL draft. New York will once again face challenges in the interior of their defense. Fortunately for them, they’ll avoid having to face one of the best guards in the league, as we recently learned that the Cowboys would be without Tyler Smith for the first part of the season as he undergoes thumb surgery. In his place, Dallas will send out backup guard T.J. Bass. Despite Smith’s absence, the Cowboys will look to attack inside behind the power of Tyler Booker and Cooper Beebe. Look for running back Javonte Williams to follow his lead blocks and use a physical rushing attack to keep the Cowboys offense out of third-and-long situations. And that is important because of item number three. 3. Pressure from the edge As bad as the Giants defense is inside, they are equally impressive on the edge. Veteran Brian Burns is an absolute force, and they also have some recent draft picks in Abdul Carter and Kayvon Thibodeaux who can do some damage. This is a very dynamic trio of edge rushers. If the Giants are to have success against the Cowboys on Sunday night, it will come in the form of putting Dak Prescott on the ground. Both tackle positions have always been an area of concern, with left tackle Tyler Guyton offering up mixed results while right tackle Terence Steele can be downright awful in pass protection. The Cowboys also have a mystery at swing tackle and no longer have the Tyler Smith “break glass in case of emergency” option available. There is a range of outcomes where this one could get a little messy. If the Giants’ defensive coordinator can deploy some creative pressure packages, that could be the ticket to getting the Cowboys’ high-powered offense off the field. 4. New guy excitement The Cowboys front office has spent the last year loading, uploading, and re-loading defensive talent to the point where they don’t even have enough numbers to go around, and they have to bribe players from the offensive side. Unlike the 2025 unit that started the season, this new-look group has Quinnen Williams, Caleb Downs, Rashan Gary, Von Miller, Jaylen Thompson, and Cobie Durant. And the list goes on. If some of these new guys waste no time making their presence felt, it will do wonders in building excitement for this football team. Whether it’s a Miller sack, a pass breakup by Thompson or Durant, or, quite honestly, anything positive from the rookie Downs, seeing these new investments produce immediate dividends will set the tone for the season, where they can finally turn the page on what was a dreadful defense. 5. Breaking the Banks The second season of the amazing wide receiving duo of CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens will be full of excitement. All eyes will be on a great matchup between Pickens and Giants cornerback Greg Newsome II, as these two are very familiar with each other from their time in the AFC North. It should be a physical battle with those two fighting for every contested pass. Look for the Cowboys to turn to their other alpha, Lamb, and utilize his shiftiness to create separation and cause problems for the other Giants cornerback, Deonte Banks. If Klayton Adams moves him around and constantly forces help over the top, it opens the door for some unattended receivers flying down the seam. With so much attention given to the Cowboys’ top dogs, don’t be surprised if Ryan Flournoy or KaVontae Turpin come up with a huge play in this one.

title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 1
summary: It is the final day of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS - JANUARY 16: Tom Landry, manager of the Dallas Cowboys is carried off by his team during Super Bowl VI against the Miami Dolphins at Tulane Stadium in New Orleans, Lousiana on January 16, 1972. (Photo by Focus On Sport/Getty Images) | Focus on Sport via Getty Images It is the final day of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. Welcome to the final day of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. Super Bowl VI was the afternoon the Dallas Cowboys finally became champions. Years of playoff heartbreak, two championship-game losses to Green Bay and defeat in Super Bowl V had created the unwanted label of being a team that could never win it all the way. Dallas erased it permanently by dominating Miami and lifting the first Lombardi Trophy in franchise history. There’s no better way to end a countdown than right here. Sunday, January 16, 1972 Tulane Stadium, New Orleans, Louisiana Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 24, Miami Dolphins 3 The Cowboys entered New Orleans on a nine-game winning streak, but Miami presented a serious challenge. Don Shula’s Dolphins had gone 10-3-1 and featured Bob Griese, Larry Csonka and Paul Warfield. On this day, though, Dallas made them look ordinary. The defense created the first breakthrough. Csonka lost his first fumble of the season and Chuck Howley recovered it, allowing Dallas to move into position for Mike Clark’s nine-yard field goal and a 3-0 lead. It was an early indication of how completely the Cowboys defense would control the game. Then came perhaps the defining defensive image of the first Cowboys championship. With Miami facing third-and-nine and Dallas still leading 3-0, Griese scrambled desperately away from pressure. Bob Lilly pursued him across the field before finally dragging him down for a 29-yard loss. More than half a century later, it still stands as the longest negative play from scrimmage in Super Bowl history. Dallas turned its control into a touchdown during the second quarter. Roger Staubach directed a 76-yard drive and finished it with a seven-yard touchdown pass to veteran Lance Alworth, increasing the advantage to 10-0. Miami finally responded just before halftime when Garo Yepremian converted a 31-yard field goal, leaving the Cowboys ahead 10-3 at the break. Any hope Miami had of changing the game disappeared immediately after halftime. Dallas took the opening kickoff of the third quarter and travelled 71 yards in eight plays, leaning heavily on its powerful ground attack. Duane Thomas completed the drive with a three-yard touchdown run, pushing the lead to 17-3. From there, the Doomsday Defense tightened its grip. Miami could not establish its running game, Griese was under constant pressure and the Dolphins never reached the end zone. Early in the fourth quarter, Howley intercepted Griese at midfield and returned the ball 41 yards to the Miami nine. Three plays later, Staubach found Mike Ditka for a seven-yard touchdown that completed the scoring at 24-3. Staubach was named Super Bowl MVP after completing 12 of 19 passes for 119 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions. The numbers were not huge because they did not need to be. Dallas controlled the game on the ground, protected the football and allowed Staubach to play the efficient, composed football that became one of his trademarks. The Cowboys rushed for a then Super Bowl record of 252 yards. Thomas led the way with 95 yards on 19 carries, while Walt Garrison added 74. Miami knew Dallas wanted to run and still could not stop it. The combination of that ground attack and the Doomsday Defense meant the Dolphins spent almost the entire afternoon playing on Dallas’ terms. The defensive numbers were even more impressive. Miami managed only 185 total yards and three points, while Dallas became the first team in Super Bowl history to prevent its opponent from scoring a touchdown. The Dolphins turned the ball over three times, and their only points came from Yepremian’s field goal. This game takes the number one spot because everything that followed was built upon it. The Cowboys would eventually win five Super Bowls, become one of the NFL’s most recognizable franchises and earn the “America’s Team” identity during the Landry era. But there could be no second, third, fourth or fifth Lombardi without the first. Super Bowl VI was the moment Dallas stopped being the team that nearly won and became the Dallas Cowboys, champions of the NFL. #Cowboys vs #Dolphins 1972 Super Bowl VI Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 24, Miami Dolphins 3 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/ugJy9fPaVu — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) September 12, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game Dallas became the first defense in Super Bowl history to hold an opponent without a touchdown. Miami’s three points remain tied for the fewest ever scored by a team in a Super Bowl.
