title: Cowboys vs Giants: Writer predictions for opening week
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are back! And, of course, it’s another start to the season where the Cowboys roll into MetLife Stadium to take on the New York Giants. The Giants have many questions heading into the 2026 season with a whole new coaching staff after a season where they managed to win only four games. […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - JANUARY 04: Daniel Bellinger #82 of the New York Giants in action during the game against the Dallas Cowboys at MetLife Stadium on January 04, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The New York Giants won 34-17. (Photo by Ishika Samant/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys are back! And, of course, it’s another start to the season where the Cowboys roll into MetLife Stadium to take on the New York Giants. The Giants have many questions heading into the 2026 season with a whole new coaching staff after a season where they managed to win only four games. Let’s break it down then get to some predictions. When New York has the ball Expect the Giants to make the running game the starting point of their new offense. John Harbaugh has brought in coaches with a history of building physical rushing attacks, while fullback Patrick Ricard and first-round offensive lineman Francis Mauigoa were added to help them play that way. Cam Skattebo gives them a powerful runner, but quarterback Jaxson Dart is just as important. Dart rushed for 487 yards and nine touchdowns as a rookie, so Dallas cannot simply chase the running back and forget about the quarterback. The biggest opportunity for New York comes when Dallas starts worrying too much about the run. The Cowboys allowed 4,735 passing yards and 31 passing touchdowns last season, and Dart finished the year by completing 22 of 32 passes for 230 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions in a 34-17 win over Dallas. If Malik Nabers is cleared to play following his ACL recovery, his matchup against the Dallas secondary becomes even more important, although his Week 1 availability remains uncertain. The Giants’ route to victory is to keep Dallas guessing with the running game and Skattebo, use Dart as a runner, then attack downfield when the Cowboys bring extra defenders toward the line. When Dallas has the ball Dallas should make New York prove immediately that its run defense has improved. The Giants surrendered 2,470 rushing yards last season, while Javonte Williams ran for 1,201 yards and scored 11 rushing touchdowns for Dallas. Running the football also has another benefit this week because the Cowboys will be without All-Pro guard Tyler Smith following thumb surgery. T.J. Bass will replace him, so giving the offensive line manageable situations rather than asking it to pass protect on every play makes sense. That becomes even more important because New York can rush the passer. Brian Burns produced 16.5 sacks last season and the Giants recorded 48 as a team, with Abdul Carter another dangerous player coming off the edge. Dallas should counter that with quick throws, play-action and plenty of CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. If Dallas can establish Williams early, it becomes much harder for Burns and Carter to attack Prescott without worrying about the run. From there, the Cowboys have the receiving talent to challenge a Giants secondary that allowed 3,908 passing yards last season. The current MetLife forecast is warm and humid rather than showing signs of severe weather, so conditions should not prevent Dallas from attacking through the air if Prescott’s protection holds up. Now onto the predictions from your BTB writers… Tom Ryle (0-0) Ugh. Week 1 predictions are such a shot in the dark. But I’m expecting the Cowboys to be a little more reserved with Tyler Smith out, and I think the defensive improvements show up. DAL 27 NYG 19 Brandon Loree (0-0) The Cowboys are favored in this game, and rightfully so. History alone suggests Dallas has a high probability of winning. However, the Christian Parker-led new-look defense could be the thing that makes or breaks the night. The one area of the New York Giants offense the Cowboys need to be prepared for is Jaxson Dart and his scrambling ability. According to NFL Pro, Dart had 18 explosive runs in 2025, tied with Patrick Mahomes for most in the league, and a 61.6% rushing success rate, the highest among QBs with at least 35 carries last season. The Cowboys have struggled in this area for multiple seasons. If they remain disciplined and put a lid on it, the defense could have a dominant night. At the end of the day, Dallas is the better and more prepared team on paper and should lead to a strong 28-17 win in New Jersey. Dyllan Rivers (0-0) Even with Tyler Smith out, the Giants just don’t have the horses to keep up with the high-powered Cowboys offense. Give me the Cowboys 34-17 Matt Holleran (0-0) While optimism is high about Dallas’ new-look defense, it may take some time for Christian Parker’s unit to settle in. New York’s offense will not be an easy test in Week 1, and I see Dallas struggling to slow down the Giants’ offense. The connection of Prescott and Lamb keeps Dallas in the game, but a costly turnover in the fourth quarter seals the Cowboys fate. Give me New York, 26-23. Mike Poland (0-0) The Cowboys have played the Giants 13 times to open the season, and the Cowboys are 11-2 in those games. Add in that Dak is 14-3 against Giants all time, and the historical trend shows this game tilts heavily toward Dallas. Cowboys win this 27-20.

title: Malik Davis injury opens the door for Emari Demercado
summary: Javonte Williams had a very good season for the Dallas Cowboys in 2025 under offensive coordinator Klayton Adams. His 1,201 rushing yards ranked ninth in the NFL. However, he did start to wear down a bit towards the end of the season. That was due to carrying the ball 252 times as the next closest […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - JANUARY 04: Arizona Cardinals running back Emari Demercado #31 carries the ball in the second half of an NFL game between the Arizona Cardinals and the Los Angeles Rams on January 4, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, CA. (Photo by Greg Fiore/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Javonte Williams had a very good season for the Dallas Cowboys in 2025 under offensive coordinator Klayton Adams. His 1,201 rushing yards ranked ninth in the NFL. However, he did start to wear down a bit towards the end of the season. That was due to carrying the ball 252 times as the next closest at the running back position was Malik Davis with 52. Speaking of Davis, he earned the RB2 role during training camp as he left Jaydon Blue and Phil Mafah in his rearview, which setup an opportunity for him to have a bigger role this season and take some of the responsibility off of Williams. Unfortunately, Davis suffered a hip injury on Friday that will require surgery and will have him on the shelf for quite some time, Fortunately for the Cowboys, they recently signed veteran Emari Demercado. Demercado has been in the league since 2023. After going undrafted, he was signed by the Arizona Cardinals, and he spent three seasons on their roster. This is an important factor because the aforementioned Adams was there for the first two years as the Cardinals offensive line coach, and he was vital in their rushing attack being one of the better ones in the league over that span. In his first year, the Cardinals finished fourth in rushing yards and fourth in yards per game thanks to the unique gap runs designs that Adams implemented. A year later in 2024, the Cardinals finished in the top 10 in both categories. Demercado, although he was a backup with the Cardinals, was able to shine under that system. He racked up 284 yards on 58 carries as a rookie, and then followed it up with 223 yards on just 24 carries in 2024, averaging an amazing 9.3 yards per rush. The familiarity with what Adams likes to do in the run game is a big reason why the Cowboys signed Demercado, and now, he gets to work with Adams again who clearly has brought out the best in him during his short NFL career. He had 20 runs of double-digit yardage during his stint with the Cardinals, which accounted for 15.9% of his 126 carries. Also, Demercado has been a reliable pass blocker as he’s only allowed eight pressures in 104 pass-blocking reps. The Cowboys also have Hunter Luepke on the roster, as well as Israel Abanikanda who is on the practice squad and may get a call up. Even so, Demercado has a lot more experience and production than both combined. He’s the guy that’s best suited to give Williams some relief, and that will be important later in the year as the Cowboys hopefully make a run at the playoffs. Losing Davis was a pretty big blow, but the Cowboys need to be given a lot of credit for bringing in Demercado as insurance. Now, he gets his chance to be an even bigger part of the Cowboys’ offense, which is expected to once again be near the top of the NFL.
author: Matthew Lenix

title: Dallas Cowboys draft: College football’s top targets in Week 2
summary: It’s never too early to start thinking about potential draft picks of the Dallas Cowboys in the future. Here are some prospects that could be interesting who are playing this weekend. Ohio State at Texas This is the main event of Week 2 and features two players likely to be selected near the beginning of […]
full_text: AUSTIN, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 05: Colin Simmons #1 of the Texas Longhorns reacts after a fumble recovery in the second half against the Texas State Bobcats at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium on September 05, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s never too early to start thinking about potential draft picks of the Dallas Cowboys in the future. Here are some prospects that could be interesting who are playing this weekend. Ohio State at Texas This is the main event of Week 2 and features two players likely to be selected near the beginning of the 2027 NFL Draft. Ohio State and Texas both won comfortably in their opening games, but this matchup will provide a much stronger test. Key Dallas Targets: Ohio State: Jeremiah Smith, Wide Receiver The 6-foot-3, 223-pound junior produced 87 receptions for 1,243 yards and 12 touchdowns last season, taking his career total to 2,558 yards and 27 scores in only two years. His size, speed and body control make him extremely difficult to cover one-on-one. Smith can run away from defensive backs, win contested catches and adjust to passes thrown outside his frame. He is especially dangerous after the catch because he has the strength to run through contact without losing his speed. The challenge against Texas will show how Smith handles physical coverage and extra defensive attention. The Longhorns will know where he is on every snap, so his ability to create separation when the defense is designed to stop him will be important. Why The Cowboys Care George Pickens is playing under the franchise tag, and Dallas has not given him a long-term contract. That leaves his future beyond this season uncertain. Smith could eventually give the Cowboys another dominant receiver alongside CeeDee Lamb and allow the offense to remain aggressive through the air. Smith is expected to be selected very early, meaning Dallas might need to move up to get him. Texas: Colin Simmons, Edge Rusher Simmons has 21 sacks, 29.5 tackles for loss and six forced fumbles already on his college record, and he finished 2025 with 12 sacks and earned first-team All-SEC honours. His first-step speed is his greatest weapon. Simmons can explode past an offensive tackle before the blocker has properly settled into position. He can also bend around the corner while maintaining his balance and closing quickly on the quarterback. This game gives Simmons an opportunity to face an Ohio State offensive line filled with NFL-level talent. Scouts will want to see whether he can still create pressure when an opponent slides protection toward him. Why The Cowboys Care Dallas added Rashan Gary to start opposite Donovan Ezeiruaku, but a team can never have too many pass rushers, even with rookie addition Malachi Lawrence. Simmons would bring the burst and natural finishing ability needed to become a major part of the Cowboys’ defensive front. Gary is an established veteran, while Simmons could give Dallas a younger and cheaper long-term option on the edge while Lawrence continues to develop in his second year. Oklahoma at Michigan Oklahoma travels to Ann Arbor to face a Michigan team that narrowly escaped with a 13-12 victory over Western Michigan last week. This game features a powerful defensive tackle and a productive running back who could address future needs in Dallas. Key Dallas Targets: Oklahoma: David Stone, Defensive Tackle Stone is a 6-foot-3, 315-pound defensive tackle with an impressive combination of strength and quickness. He can hold his position against double-team blocks, but he is also athletic enough to attack the gap between two offensive linemen. His hands are powerful, allowing him to knock blockers backwards or remove their grip before moving toward the ball. Stone is still developing his pass-rush plan, but his ability to collapse the middle of the pocket can prevent quarterbacks from stepping forward to avoid outside pressure. Why The Cowboys Care Stone could become the next powerful interior defender the Cowboys use in their three-man front. His size would help protect the linebackers against the run, while his quickness could provide pressure directly in front of the quarterback. That ability to affect both the running and passing games would make him a valuable early-round target and makes an already strong front even more formidable. Michigan: Jordan Marshall, Running Back Marshall rushed for 932 yards and ten touchdowns in 2025 despite playing in only 11 games. He averaged 6.2 yards per carry and showed that he can handle contact without losing his ability to produce explosive runs. Marshall has the build to run between the tackles. He reads his blocks patiently, makes one cut and then accelerates into open space. He is also willing to finish runs by lowering his shoulder rather than constantly trying to escape toward the sideline. Why The Cowboys Care Dallas re-signed Javonte Williams, but the team still needs to consider the long-term future of the position. Jaydon Blue has gone, while Malik Davis is better suited to a supporting role which he will prove this year how well he can handle that role (depending on his injury). Marshall could provide a physical option who keeps the offense on schedule and helps Dallas control games. He would not need to carry the entire workload immediately, making him a possible second-day selection who could begin in a rotation before earning a larger role.
author: Mike Poland

title: What has you pumped for the Broncos vs. Chiefs matchup on Monday Night Football?
summary: Broncos Country, we are just one sleep away from the Denver Broncos taking on the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday Night Football to start their 2026 season. It’s been a long offseason, but the rubber is about ready to hit the road. I’m an enjoyer of most all sports, but the National Football League just […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - DECEMBER 25: Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix (10) before the snap in the third quarter of a Christmas Day NFL game between the Denver Broncos and Kansas City Chiefs on December 25, 2025 at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Broncos Country, we are just one sleep away from the Denver Broncos taking on the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday Night Football to start their 2026 season. It’s been a long offseason, but the rubber is about ready to hit the road. I’m an enjoyer of most all sports, but the National Football League just hits different. I’m so glad football is back. There truly isn’t anything quite like it in the world of sports. With that being said, I thought I’d ask what as you pumped for the season opener? Feel free to let me know your thoughts in the comment section. Here are a few things I’m stoked for. The debuts of Jaylen Waddle and Jonah Coleman on offense The Broncos had their share of ups and downs on the offensive side of the ball in 2025. The aerial attack had issues early on in the year—similarly to 2024. Moreover, the run game slowed down immensely in the second stretch of the season when J.K Dobbins’ promising season came to a halt after a hip drop tackle. Truth be told, there weren’t many games where Denver had both aspects firing on all cylinders. To defeat the Chiefs on Monday Night Football, Denver has to start off fast, and they need to be able to attack Steve Spagnuolo’s defense efficiently in both phases. This offseason, they made two additions to help elevate their offensive production to the next level. The first was wide receiver Jaylen Waddle. A tried-and-true beater versus zone coverage, Waddle has a chance to make an immediate impact in the Broncos’ offense improving an aspect of their passing game they struggled with in ‘25. I’m hoping he can make an impact on Monday night—a long distance touchdown from Bo Nix on the road in Arrowhead would be a fabulous way to kick off his tenure with the team. The second was Jonah Coleman. He’s the Broncos’ insurance policy for Dobbins this year. In my opinion, Coleman will greatly improve their red zone rushing attack and improve their efficiency in short yardage situations. I’m not sure what kind of role he will have in his regular season debut, but I’d like to see him get an opportunity to show his promise in key situations against the Chiefs. These are the two offensive players I’m excited to watch perform the most. Their success and impact will be extremely important for the offense to reach new heights in ‘26. The rise and impact of Eyioma Uwazurike on defense For better or worse, the offseason and training camp comes with a lot of hype. Over the course of the summer, we had numerous reports of players who have impressed without camp. One constant in those conversations from both players and coaches was defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike. Last season, he had the best outing of his career. On Monday Night Football , he will be a starter alongside Zach Allen and D.J. Jones on the defensive trenches for the Broncos. Uwazurike’s size and length are both imposing and enticing, and I’m very excited to see how he performs against a Chiefs’ offensive line which may wind up starting an undrafted rookie free agent at tackle. Stopping Kenneth Walker III and Kansas City’s revamped rushing attack will be mission critical for Denver to earn a victory in primetime. The former Iowa State standout will need to perform well for that to happen. I expect them to run the ball a lot, especially with Patrick Mahomes coming off an ACL injury. In ‘25, the Broncos had a Top 3 rushing defense with respect to yards allowed and yards per carry. With John Franklin-Myers’ departure, the rise of Uwazurike will be essential for the unit to be as successful combating the run this season. I’m hoping he can help set the tone and tenacious play for the defense up front. He has all the traits to do so and I’m a believer in what he can accomplish this season. Extending the winning streak versus the Chiefs to four games Let’s be honest. Battling the Chiefs has been an ongoing struggle for the Broncos for ages. Prior to the ’25 season, Denver had dropped seventeen of eighteen games to Kansas City. It’s always tough losing to division rivals, but losing that many (including sixteen straight) was one of the darkest chapters in franchise history. Though coming off three victories in a row and fresh off their first AFC West crown in a decade, nothing has me more pumped than the prospect of Denver starting off the season 1-0 and extending their winning streak against the Chiefs to four games. Despite their success last season, the Broncos knows they fell short of their ultimate goal. This year, it’s all about proving themselves again. Opening week is a blank slate for every team looking to embark on their gridiron journey for a Lombardi Trophy. For many, it’s an unrealistic fool’s errand—but for the Broncos—it’s a reality. Starting off the season with a big victory should give them a much-needed boost of confidence facing one of the toughest schedules of any team in the National Football League to start the year. It’s time for the Broncos to show everyone who the top team in the AFC West is. They can do that with a victory in primetime against their longtime nemesis. Let’s go!
author: Christopher Hart

title: Broncos at Chiefs: The No Bull Week 1 Preview
summary: Week 1 is here. Our Broncos are going to be rocking the all-white uniforms in Kansas City to kick off the first week of their season.  I haven’t been this excited for the first game of a season since 2013, when the Denver Broncos got the revenge matchup against the Baltimore Ravens and completely embarrassed […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - DECEMBER 25: Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton looks on from the sideline during an NFL football game against the Kansas City Chiefs at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium on December 25, 2025 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 1 is here. Our Broncos are going to be rocking the all-white uniforms in Kansas City to kick off the first week of their season. I haven’t been this excited for the first game of a season since 2013, when the Denver Broncos got the revenge matchup against the Baltimore Ravens and completely embarrassed them on the national stage. What this game means to the Chiefs Last season was an embarrassment for the Kansas City Chiefs and their fans, and they are ready to wash the taste of it from their mouths. Patrick Mahomes suffered a torn ACL and LCL in his left knee last December against the Chargers, and their hopes rest on Mahomes returning to MVP status this season. This game isn’t anything close to integral for their season. The Chiefs have 3 winnable games in their first 4 starts (Broncos, Colts, at Dolphins, and at Raiders), with this game being their most dangerous. More than anything, they are more interested in giving the Broncos a deficit that would hopefully shake the Broncos’ resolve. What this game means to the Broncos The Broncos under Sean Payton have had a rough start to each of their past 3 seasons. They have a very tough schedule through the first 6 weeks of the season (at Chiefs, Jaguars, Rams, at 49ers, at Chargers, Seahawks). The Broncos need a fast start if they want to keep working off the momentum they built last season. Going into Arrowhead and stunning the Chiefs would set them up with great morale heading into the rest of the gauntlet of a schedule they have. Losing at Arrowhead wouldn’t be great for them, but let’s be real: it would be somewhat expected with Andy Reid having months to scheme and game plan for this matchup, along with the home-field advantage. When the Broncos are defending Passing It is honestly nigh impossible to know exactly how to call this. Patrick Mahomes and how well he is able to move has a high impact on how well their offense is going to execute. Until he has more than a one-season hiccup in his play, you have to respect him as one of the top 3 quarterbacks in the NFL. As far as receiving options go, the Chiefs have Travis Kelce, Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy, and Tyquan Thornton. Kenneth Walker III is also very effective at catching passes out of the backfield. The Broncos have the NFL’s best corner in Patrick Surtain and arguably the NFL’s most talented playmaking slot corner in Ja’Quan McMillian. Riley Moss is an excellent corner when he isn’t drawing pass interference calls. I also love how our safeties play and are able to impact the passing game. Having both a healthy Brandon Jones and Talanoa Hufanga is a huge help against an offense as potent as Reid’s Chiefs. The biggest impact to this matchup is going to be in the trenches. You already know the Broncos bring the heat with All-Pros Nik Bonitto and Zach Allen. The bigger problem for the Chiefs is the defense called by Vance Joseph, who brings heat from any angle, any player, at any time. He’s one of the NFL’s best defensive coordinators and has his team absolutely dialed in on making it almost impossible to know where his blitzes are coming from at times. The Chiefs are down starting Left Tackle Josh Simmons and have a dinged-up Trey Smith at Guard. They also have yet to figure out the key to slowing down Joseph’s defense. The Broncos poured on pressure last season, to the tune of 4 sacks and 18 pressures in the past two games. Advantage: Broncos Rushing The biggest impact of rushing for the Chiefs is going to be Super Bowl winning runningback Kenneth Walker III. If they can block up holes for him, he’s capable of making huge plays to turn the game at any point. He’s every bit as capable of keeping them ahead of schedule as a back who averaged 4.6 ypc last season. The Broncos do bring a front that is excellent against the run overall. They only gave up a 100-yard rusher twice last season (Colts and Bills). The Broncos also gave up only 3.9 ypc last season, which ranked them 3rd best in the NFL. The big unknown here is how well the Chiefs’ run blocking does to open things up for Walker. Last season, they weren’t spectacular by any stretch of the imagination. This begs the question of whether that was due to a lack of running back talent or ability on the line. This game is going to show us which, as Walker brings a ton of talent to bear. Advantage: Chiefs When the Broncos are on offense Passing Bo Nix is no Patrick Mahomes, but damn if he isn’t on his ass, especially when you look at how he matured and played last season. We’ve seen this preseason and training camp enough to know that Nix is on point and his ankle is well healed. The story of the offseason for the Broncos is the addition of Jaylen Waddle to the wide receiver room. To my eyes, that changes everything for this offense. Watching the team muddle about with an inconsistent Troy Franklin, an undersized Marvin Mims, and slower Pat Bryant at the #2 position has been rough. I think everything in this offense gets better just by Waddle being on the field. He’s arguably a #1 WR talent, has phenomenal speed, superb hands, and changes speed at an elite level. In short, Jaylen Waddle is a PROBLEM. The Chiefs then have to pick their poison when Waddle is on the field at the same time as #1 WR Courtland Sutton and the rest of the receivers (who I think are very capable as #3 or #4 options). The area of weakness in the receiving game is the tight end room for the Broncos. One of Nix’s shortcomings is that he doesn’t lean enough on throws to tight ends over the middle of the field. Evan Engram and Adam Trautman are good tight ends, but neither has been noteworthy in the receiving game. The other big story in the passing game for the Broncos is the Chiefs losing both starting cornerbacks this past offseason, with Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson going to the Rams. To help bolster their defensive backfield, they brought back aging L’Jarius Sneed, 1st-round pick Mansoor Delane, and 4th-round pick Jadon Canady. Having a rebuilt cornerback room is likely to lead to some choppy waters for the Chiefs if their pass rush is unable to get home (which they won’t…the Broncos’ line is one of the best in the NFL at pass blocking). Advantage: Broncos Rushing The Broncos’ line on paper has looked like a good running line for a couple of years now. The problem has been that it hasn’t been a stable factor through a whole season. They tend to start slow and have been hampered by a lack of running back talent in recent years. This offseason, the Broncos re-signed JK Dobbins and drafted Jonah Coleman as a fix for the running back room. For me, the jury is out on Dobbins until he proves he can stay healthy through the season. I do love the signing of Coleman, though. He was a very productive back in every facet of the game in Washington and is one of the most ready prospects that were available in the draft this year to hit the ground running. The Chiefs have been capable of stopping the run under Steve Spagnola, giving up an average of 4 ypc, which puts them in the top-10 of the NFL as a run defense goes. The Broncos are healthy up front, and last season with this line and Dobbins, they were tearing it up offensively. Advantage: Broncos Broncos keys to the game Score early, score often The Broncos need to get on the board early and quiet the crowd at Arrowhead. Sure, they can win without this, but getting up by multiple scores is the easiest way for them to ensure a win. Contain the run Kenneth Walker is likely going to be productive. The big thing for the Broncos defense is that they need to keep him hemmed in and not let him make explosives in the run game. Create turnovers The Chiefs have a huge advantage at Arrowhead. The…

title: Broncos captains show what leadership means in Denver
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! The ultimate sign of respect is being named a captain. It shows that teammates want and trust these guys as their leaders. They want to follow the players whom they name a captain. When the time comes, teammates know these guys will do whatever it takes for the team. Earlier this […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 02: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos congratulates Courtland Sutton #14 after a touchdown in the first half against the Houston Texans at NRG Stadium on November 02, 2025 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! The ultimate sign of respect is being named a captain. It shows that teammates want and trust these guys as their leaders. They want to follow the players whom they name a captain. When the time comes, teammates know these guys will do whatever it takes for the team. Earlier this week, the Denver Broncos named their nine team captains . The Broncos’ captains for 2026 are quarterback Bo Nix, wide receiver Courtland Sutton, guard Quinn Meinerz, cornerback Pat Surtain II, linebacker Alex Singleton, nose tackle DJ Jones, safety Talanoa Hufanga, safety/special teamer Devon Key, and kicker Wil Lutz. HC Sean Payton has announced our 2026 captains as chosen by the players. ⭐️ pic.twitter.com/0jWwJfHkyB — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) September 9, 2026 “It’s an honor to be a captain on our team because it’s voted by the players,” Nix said to the media earlier this week. “It’s a special honor when your peers and teammates vote you to be one of the leaders of our team. We have several leaders and to be named one … It’s a great responsibility, and with that comes a lot of opportunity, but also it’s a big weight to carry. “It’s not something to be thrown around lightly. My leadership style has evolved as I’ve gotten older because I’ve experienced more and understood what it’s like to essentially get someone to follow you. That’s what a leader is. I’ve gone from an action-based leader when I first got here because, honestly, I was just trying to swim, and not drown, and do my role and do my part on the team while also leading by action. I feel like now I can sort of lead a little bit more vocally because I’m a little more aware and have a few more things under my belt that I can fall back on.” For Sutton, this is the sixth consecutive year he’s been named a captain in Denver. “I’ll tell you all the same thing I told the team,” Sutton said to the media. “There’s an immense amount of gratitude that comes from being named captain. To be able to have your peers and the guys that you share work with, locker room, practice, film, games, bus rides, flights, the whole nine, you share those moments with, for them to, not just myself, but the rest of the guys that were named captains, to look at us and say, ‘We trust that you guys are going to help guide us in the right direction and we believe in you guys to be the anchor for us, for the ship to be going into the direction we want to go towards.’ I just have a lot of gratitude and thankfulness that, I know it’s the same, but that comes from being named captain for another season.” For Broncos head coach Sean Payton, the captains’ responsibilities are fairly simple. He also doesn’t meet with them regularly. “No, I think it’s a sign of just the leadership within the locker room,” Payton said to the media. “I don’t have a council meeting with them, for instance, every two or three weeks, but I think it’s just a recognition of how they’re seen by their peers. They all lead differently. There are a number of guys who are going to be significant leaders for us who aren’t wearing a patch. So I think the first thing is just being authentic and being yourself.” Players like Lutz know the expectations that come with being named a captain by their teammates and what it means. “It means a lot. I think when you’re voted as a captain by the guys that you come to work with every day, and you spend a lot of time with, I think that’s the ultimate sign of respect, and I don’t take it lightly. It’s pretty cool.” Broncos links

title: Broncos vs. Chiefs: 3 Players to Watch in Week 1
summary: The Denver Broncos head to Arrowhead Stadium to take on the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday Night Football. This will be a huge Week 1 test for the Broncos who are looking to start the season on a high note and defend their AFC West title. Here are three players that will need to perform […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - DECEMBER 25: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos runs the ball for a touchdown against the Kansas City Chiefs during the third quarter at Arrowhead Stadium on December 25, 2025 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos head to Arrowhead Stadium to take on the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday Night Football . This will be a huge Week 1 test for the Broncos who are looking to start the season on a high note and defend their AFC West title. Here are three players that will need to perform well in order for that to happen. Bo Nix — Quarterback Entering his third season with the Broncos, quarterback Bo Nix is poised for his best season to date. In his first two seasons, the former first-round pick has shown a lot of moxie, produced at a high level, and developed a penchant for fourth quarter comebacks. This offseason, Denver added multiple playmakers on the offensive side of the ball to help further his development. Alongside that, Offensive Coordinator Davis Webb has been working hard all offseason to craft a play calling dynamic suited to his strengths. Additionally, working alongside him to help improve areas where he can be more efficient. Steve Spagnuolo’s defense was a Top 10-unit last season. Going up against them will be tough challenge for Nix and the Broncos’ offense who are hoping to start off much faster and better than the past two seasons. With several new additions to their revamped secondary, I expect Denver to challenge Kansas City through the air and look for some explosive plays down the field. Jaylen Waddle — Wide Receiver The Broncos made a splash sending a first and third round pick to the Miami Dolphins to acquire wide receiver Jaylen Waddle. His addition to their wide receiver corps gives them a dynamic talent who should bolster the productivity and efficient of the group. I’m hopeful we can see that happen in Week 1 versus the Chiefs. As mentioned earlier, Kansas City has some new starters in their secondary. It’d be smart to challenge that early and often. Unleashing Waddle in his first regular season game with the Broncos will likely be a part of the gameplan. His flexibility to play inside and out should cause some issues for their defense. Whether it’s dialing up the deep ball with his deep speed or letting him make plays after the catch with his elusiveness, finding a way to feed Waddle will be crucial to come out of Arrowhead with a notch in the win column. Nik Bonitto — Edge Rusher The Broncos have topped the National Football League in sacks in back-to-back seasons. A big reason for that has been the play of fifth-year edge rusher Nik Bonitto. After a slow start to his NFL career, Bonitto has dialed up the heat on opposing quarterbacks the past two years, notching 13.5 sacks in 2024 and 14 sacks in 2025. With Jonathon Cooper sidelined on the NFL Commissioner’s Exempt List to start the year, there is more pressure on Bonitto to help create pressure on Patrick Mahomes. There is a chance starting left tackle Josh Simmons won’t be able to play due to a lower back injury. If that transpires, either Jaylon Moore or undrafted rookie free agent Khalil Benson will be protecting Mahomes’ blindside. Either way, that should provide Bonitto with a favorable matchup and opportunity to register some big plays. The Broncos’ chances of victory will catapult if he can create some havoc in the backfield with sacks—or even better—finding a way to force a fumble to give the defense a big takeaway.

summary: The Denver Broncos will open their season on the road on prime time with a Monday Nighty Football matchup against their heated rival in the Kansas City Chiefs. full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - DECEMBER 25: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos runs the ball during an NFL football game against the Kansas City Chiefs at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium on December 25, 2025 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos will open their season on the road on prime time with a Monday Nighty Football matchup against their heated rival in the Kansas City Chiefs. Patrick Mahomes has missed two of the last five games against Denver while the Broncos have run up the wins against Kansas City winning four of those including both where Mahomes didn’t play. Bo Nix has only lost once against the Chiefs with that game coming down to a blocked Wil Lutz field goal that would have won the game. It is probably going to be a tough, hard fought game that could go either way. The kind of prime time game the NFL loves and I’m here for it! Game Overview Denver Broncos at Kansas City Chiefs Monday, September 14, 2026 at 6:15 P.M. Mile High time Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Missouri ATS Betting Lines: Kansas City -2.5 Moneyline Odds: Denver +116 / Kansas City -136 Over/Under: 43.5 Note: All odds courtesy of FanDuel Sportsbook. Collectively, our Mile High Report staff is predicting a Broncos 30-17 road win on Monday Night Football over the Chiefs in Week 1. We all predicted wins, but here is where we each landed individually on the score: Broncos 24, Chiefs 22 While I think the Broncos have the better roster and the Chiefs are in a transition period after a dominant run, they are still the Chiefs and its prime time at home with Patrick Mahomes fully healthy. Anything can – and probably will – happen. That said, I’m still a Broncos fan and I see this game coming down to a failed two-point conversion to end the game. Go Broncos! – Tim Lynch Broncos 33, Chiefs 17 The Broncos kick the season off in style with an explosive offensive showing. The addition of Waddle and the return of Dobbins bring tears to the eyes of Chiefs fans in attendance. The Broncos defense is still stout, but has trouble keeping Walker hemmed in early. – Sadaraine Broncos 45, Chiefs 16 Bo Nix ruins Mahomes return by throwing 4 touchdowns. Waddle roasts the Chiefs DBs for two, Sutton does what he does for another and Pat Bryant let’s the world know he’s the real deal with another. Dobbins rushes for 100, Jonah gets his 1st career touchdown and the Broncos defense does what it does vs. Mahomes. 3 turnovers, 4 sacks, and the Broncos destroy the Chiefs on Monday Night. – Scotty Payne Broncos 24, Chiefs 13 The big story is obviously going to be the return of Patrick Mahomes after his recovery from his knee injury. That will be the storyline, but the Broncos will be celebrating a return of their own. The big question will be about Bo Nix and his ankle. But that’s not the only concern for Denver. After a season of close calls and comebacks, the defending AFC West champs will get a “prove it” game right away. Winning in KC is never easy, but you better believe that Sean Payton will have his team ready to prove 2025 was no fluke. – Adam Malnati Broncos 24, Chiefs 17 This primetime matchup should wind up being one of the best of the Week 1 slate. I believe it’s going to be a close game just like we saw on both occasions last year. I’m hoping Bo Nix can air it out going up against a revamped secondary with three new starters. Additionally, I think the Broncos’ pass rush could be poised for a big game especially if Josh Simmons doesn’t play. That means they would have an UDFA starting at one of their tackle positions. With those things in mind, I’m giving Denver the slight edge and am picking them to start their season off with a big victory. – Chris Hart Broncos 27, Chiefs 17 Nix and the Broncos want to send a message. It’s Nix, new offensive play caller Davis Webb, and the offense who will steal the show on Monday Night Football. – Ian St. Clair What is your score prediction for the Broncos-Chiefs game? title: Future Broncos: 3 Prospects to Watch in Week 2 of 2026 NCAA Football season
summary: Week 1 of the NCAA Football season in the books. Last week, we took a look at a trio of potential first-round prospects that could be of interest to the Denver Broncos in the 2027 NFL Draft. This week we will cover three more players, with varying degrees of potential round placement, for the Week […]
full_text: OXFORD, MISSISSIPPI - SEPTEMBER 27: Will Echoles #52 of the Mississippi Rebels reacts against the Louisiana State Tigers at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium on September 27, 2025 in Oxford, Mississippi. (Photo by Randy J. Williams/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 1 of the NCAA Football season in the books. Last week, we took a look at a trio of potential first-round prospects that could be of interest to the Denver Broncos in the 2027 NFL Draft. This week we will cover three more players, with varying degrees of potential round placement, for the Week 2 slate of games. Will Echoles — Defensive Tackle — Ole Miss The defensive line is a key of the Denver Broncos. It’s a position they have acquired quality free agents such as Zach Allen, Malcolm Roach, D.J. Jones. Additionally, the have utilized some early round draft picks (Sai’vion Jones, Tyler Onyedim) the couple of years to address long-term. It’s certainly not a primary need for the Broncos. However, Eyioma Uwazurike is in a contract season and D.J. Jones will be 32 next year and carries over a $14.5 million cap hit. With that in mind, taking a look at this year’s class of defensive tackles is worth considering. Fortifying the defensive line is always a smart move, which makes it potentially in play if the right player is on the clock when the Broncos are picking next April. One player I’m bullish on is Ole Miss defensive tackle Will Echoles. After a quiet freshman campaign, the former four-star recruit was a fifteen-game starter for the Rebels last season and notched 68 tackles, 11.5 tackles for loss, and 5 sacks. For his efforts, he earned AP first-team All-SEC honors and topped all P4 conference players with 39 quarterback pressures and 35 defensive stops. He just turned 20 years old and there is no doubt his best football is ahead of him. He is a force against the run and shows great upside as an interior pass rusher. While had a bit of a rough outing in the Rebels’ close Week 1 victory over Louisville, Echoles should have a chance to dominate against Charlotte tonight. If he can put it all together this season, I would not be surprised if he wound up being a Top 15 pick next April. Peyton Bowen — Safety — Oklahoma The Broncos enter their 2026 season with Brandon Jones and Talanoa Hufanga slated as their starting duo. It’s an underrated group, and they also brought back Taylor Rapp who will eventually see time as a depth player for them this season. Though it’s important to note Jones will be a free agent at the end of the season, with Hufanga following suit in 2027. As far as the rest of the players at the position, their roster is rounded out by Tycen Anderson, Devon Key, and J.L. Skinner. That trio has largely been career contributors on special teams—with their potential as foundational starters in the future unlikely. The team also has ‘26 NFL Draft selection Miles Scott on their practice squad. I’ll admit that safety isn’t a premium position to address in the draft. History shows you can find quality starters at the position on Day 2, even as well as Day 3. One layer I think who will wind up hearing his name called a lot earlier than you think is Oklahoma Sooners standout Peyton Bowen. After spending his first two years in Norman as mostly a backup contributor and special teams’ player, Bowen became a full-time starter in ’25 and was a second-team All-SEC selection. He posted 47 tackles, 7 pass breakups, and 2 interceptions. His size (5’11 and 200 pounds) doesn’t stand out, but his football play on the field does. Bowen’s football intelligence and positional versatility are huge positives. I feel he has true potential as a single-high player but is also someone who has the chops to man down the nickel position in the NFL. That duality will be highly coveted by scouts and general managers in the coming months looking to bolster their franchise’s secondary. He’s just consistent with most everything he does, which is a reason I’ll be keeping a close eye on him as the collegiate season continues. You can catch Bowen in action against the Michigan Wolverines in today’s early slate of games. Vicari Swain — Cornerback — South Carolina Fans might not want me to talk about the potential of Denver opting to use an early round selection on a cornerback in the 2027 NFL Draft, but here we are. I do expect one of Ja’Quan McMillian or Riley Moss to get an extension with the team. However, it seems unlikely both will earn well-deserved extensions. The good thing is they have 2025 first-round pick Jahdae Barron already as an in-house replacement option for one of them. He has been cross trained at both the slot and boundary spots. While some were down on his lack of impact as a rookie, I’m optimistic about his NFL potential. The Broncos are facing a situation where their All-Pro return specialist Marvin Mims Jr. may depart in free agency after this season. Finding players with his dynamic return ability are rare. That’s why I thought I’d bring up South Carolina cornerback Vicari Swain—who is an impressive cover corner who makes big plays on defense but is also one of the nation’s elite punt return specialists. During his first two seasons with the Gamecocks, Swain (6’0”, 193 pounds) was primarily a backup player. Last season, he appeared in every game and had three starts. Even though he wasn’t a full-time starter, his impact (especially at slot) was evident with 28 tackles, 1 sack, 2 forced fumbles, along with 2 interceptions and 5 pass breakups. He also had 19 punt returns for 302 yards and three touchdowns. This season he is poised to make a greater impact for his team. As of now, most outlets have Swain as Day 2 selection. While he doesn’t have a tough matchup this week, you can catch him this evening when South Carolina hosts Towson.

title: 2026 NFL predictions: Super Bowl 61 opponents, winner
summary: Week 1 of the NFL’s 2026 season is upon us, and all 32 teams are still holding hope that this could be their special year. Us in Detroit have been holding that hope longer than almost anyone, but it no longer feels like a distant dream. The Detroit Lions have been in the Super Bowl […]
full_text: SAN FRANCISCO, CA - FEBRUARY 09: The Super Bowl LXI logo is seen during a press conference after Super Bowl LX on February 9, 2026 at Moscone Center in San Francisco, CA. (Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Week 1 of the NFL’s 2026 season is upon us, and all 32 teams are still holding hope that this could be their special year. Us in Detroit have been holding that hope longer than almost anyone, but it no longer feels like a distant dream. The Detroit Lions have been in the Super Bowl conversation for four years running, which is more than the previous six decades combined. But will this finally be the year that we can use the words “Detroit Lions” and “Super Bowl” in a sentence that doesn’t involve the words “never,” “missed,” or “crazy”? Here are our staff’s predictions for Super Bowl 61: Previous 2026 Detroit Lions predictions: Offensive MVP predictions Defensive MVP predictions Breakout Player of the Year Rookie of the Year NFC North winner, Lions’ 2026 regular season record Who will win Super Bowl 61 for the 2026 NFL season? Morgan Cannon: Lions over Bills After the Lions narrowly take care of business against the Los Angeles Rams in the NFC Championship game, they meet another team that is on the search for their first Lombardi trophy in franchise history: the Buffalo Bills. And after a back-and-forth game where there are plenty of fireworks between the two high-powered offenses, the Lions emerge victorious in a 38-31 win over the Bills. The championship parade down Woodward becomes the stuff of legend, and Detroit finally gets to celebrate the way they deserve to. Al Karsten: Lions over Texans The Detroit Lions will battle the Houston Texans in Super Bowl LXI at SoFi Stadium, just two weeks after the Lions beat the Rams in that very same stadium in the NFC Championship Game and after the Texans went through the Bills at their new Highmark Stadium. It’ll be a grind-your-teeth-down, bare-knuckle fight for three quarters, with both defenses holding the advantage before the Lions’ offense finally breaks through and erupts for two fourth-quarter touchdowns. Detroit will capture its first Lombardi Trophy with a decisive 24-13 victory, while Jared Goff takes home Super Bowl MVP honors, narrowly edging out Aidan Hutchinson—who will have made a nest and raised a family while living in the Texans’ backfield for four quarters. Brandon Knapp: Rams over Ravens Feels like this is the first super team I’ve seen in the NFL, and it’s the Rams last shot before they have to take things apart to get back up. I believe Matthew Stafford, Aaron Donald, and Davante Adams all retire after this season, and the Rams are doing everything they can to send them out on top. Anthony Balaj: Broncos over Lions Sean Payton vs. Dan Campbell is the storyline. Broncos win by a field goal. Ryan Mathews: Bengals vs. Lions The Super Bowl will be a contest between the Cincinnati Bengals and Detroit Lions. The winner will be the one who scores more points than the other team. John Whiticar: Ravens over 49ers The Rams and Seahawks are favorites to come out of the NFC, but I think the 49ers are a legitimate challenger too; they were surprisingly good for how snakebit they were last season. As for the AFC, I think the Ravens might finally get over the hump with a new head coach; I think their offense and defense could both be top five units. Give me the Ravens to win it all. Erik Schlitt: Rams over Bills I’m going to keep things chalk with my prediction this season (according to most gambling sites) and pick the Rams beating the Bills in the Super Bowl. I’m not as in love with the Rams as most NFL media is, but on paper right now, it’s hard to bet against them. Jeremy Reisman: 49ers over Broncos Full disclosure: I’m the only one who made their picks after the first few Week 1 games, so I’m a cheater and a phony. But to be fair, I’ve always been a pretty firm believer in the 49ers and Kyle Shanahan ( and I picked them to beat the Rams ). If they can get even just a smidge of injury luck this year (off to a bad start), they’ll be as good as anyone. For the second straight year, I’m taking the Broncos as the AFC Super Bowl contender, because they probably should’ve made it last year, and they’re arguably even better on paper this season.

title: Detroit Lions elevate DL from practice squad, re-sign Levi Onwuzurike
summary: The Detroit Lions have made their final roster moves for their Week 1 matchup against the New Orleans Saints, and it’s all focused on getting their defensive line ready. The Lions announced on Saturday that they have elevated veteran defensive lineman Ben Stille from the practice squad, and they’ve also re-signed Levi Onwuzurike to the […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OH - AUGUST 13: Detroit Lions defensive tackle Ben Stille (72) walks off the field at halftime during the preseason game between the Detroit Lions and the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Cincinnati, OH. (Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Detroit Lions have made their final roster moves for their Week 1 matchup against the New Orleans Saints, and it’s all focused on getting their defensive line ready. The Lions announced on Saturday that they have elevated veteran defensive lineman Ben Stille from the practice squad, and they’ve also re-signed Levi Onwuzurike to the practice squad— one day after releasing him from the 53-man roster . Starting with Onwuzurike, it’s not surprising to see him back on the team. As a vested veteran, Onwuzurike’s $1.215 million contract would have become fully guaranteed had he been on the 53-man roster during Detroit’s Week 1 game. It’s very possible the Lions bring Onwuzurike back on the 53-man squad next week, but it’s notable that he was not elevated for Sunday, so he will not play this week. Instead, the Lions opted for Stille, who plays a very similar role to Onwuzurike. A former undrafted player out of Nebraska, Stille has played in just 18 games since entering the league in 2022, and he did not play a single game in 2025. This will be his first NFL action since Week 9 of the 2024 season, when he was with the Arizona Cardinals. Stille was added about a week into Lions training camp, and he made a quick impression with his strength and versatility. “He’s a pro, smart, really smart,” Lions coach Dan Campbell said two weeks ago. “He’s got versatility, strong, very strong. He can shed blocks, shock, shed, make plays, kind of knows himself, knows what he is, knows his own limitations and can play fast enough to cover up for some of those. But that’s what’s the intrigue with him is the versatility, man. He can play some big end, we think; he can play the nose certainly, and then three if you needed it. So the more you can do and the more that you can prove you can do, that is always going to help your case.” Interestingly enough, the Lions opted not to elevate Seth McLaughlin from the practice squad. That means Detroit will go into the game without a clear backup center behind Juice Scruggs, although they did give starting right guard Tate Ratledge some center reps in training camp as an emergency plan.

title: Detroit Lions create massive cap space with 2 contract restructures
summary: Last week, we noted that the Detroit Lions were in danger of starting the 2026 season over the salary cap. They were almost certain to have to restructure a contract or two to not only become cap compliant, but to have enough cap space to potentially make any roster moves during the season. According to […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 22: Amon-Ra St. Brown #14 of the Detroit Lions celebrates with Penei Sewell #58 after catching the ball against the Baltimore Ravens during the fourth quarter at M&T Bank Stadium on September 22, 2025 in Baltimore, Maryland. | Getty Images Last week, we noted that the Detroit Lions were in danger of starting the 2026 season over the salary cap . They were almost certain to have to restructure a contract or two to not only become cap compliant, but to have enough cap space to potentially make any roster moves during the season. According to Jason Fitzgerald of Over The Cap, the Lions restructured two contracts, creating so much cap space that they have the second-most cap room of any team in the NFL . The two contracts they adjusted were the two most expected restructures: Penei Sewell and Amon-Ra St. Brown. Here’s how the restructures worked: Penei Sewell Previous 2026 salary: $19.9 million salary New 2026 salary: $1.3 million Restructured “signing bonus”: $18.6 million What’s important to note here is that the Lions are not getting rid of cap space; they’re moving it. They took $18.6 million of Sewell’s 2026 salary and converted it to a signing bonus. That bonus now gets spread over the next five years in equal cap-hit installments of $3.72 million, and that cap hit is now immovable. It stays there, and it’s guaranteed. So here were Sewell’s old cap hits: 2026: $28,000,000 2027: $32,000,000 2028: $34,000,000 2029 : $27,000,000 2030 (VOID): $0 Now here are his new cap hits: 2026: $13,120,000 (down $14,880,0000) 2027 : $35,720,000 (up $3.72M) 2028 : $37,720,000 (up $3.72M) 2029: $30,720,000 (up $3.72M) 2030 (VOID): $3,720,000 (up $3.72M) So, in short, it creates nearly $15 million in cap space this year, while adding nearly $15 million to future years. Amon-Ra St. Brown The Lions used the exact same tactic with Brown’s contract, converting $26 million of his $27.5 million salary into a signing bonus. Here are the before-and-after cap hits of that move: Before: 2026: $33,110,000 2027: $28,980,000 2028: $26,010,000 2029 (VOID) : $16,700,000 After: 2026: $12,310,000 (down $20,800,0000) 2027 : $34,180,000 (up $5.2M) 2028 : $31,210,000 (up $5.2M) 2029 (VOID): $27,100,000 (up $10.4M) Note: In 2029, two of the new signing bonus prorations of $5.2 million hit against the cap, although if Detroit opts to extend St. Brown, only $5.2 million would hit in 2029, and the other $5.2 million would stay in 2030 on his new contract. In total, the Lions created $35,680,000 in cap space for 2026, but, again, that cap space was simply moved to future years, not eliminated entirely. Per OverTheCap, the Lions now have over $38 million in cap space, second only to the San Francisco 49ers ($45.5M).

title: New Orleans Saints vs. Detroit Lions Week 1 preview: 3 key stats
summary: As enjoyable as NFL free agency, the NFL Draft, organized team activities, training camp, preseason, and 53-man roster coverage can be, nothing beats an NFL Sunday—and Week 1 is one of the most fulfilling and anticipated days of the year. The Detroit Lions need this Week 1. They need it to wash away the ghosts […]
full_text: As enjoyable as NFL free agency, the NFL Draft, organized team activities, training camp, preseason, and 53-man roster coverage can be, nothing beats an NFL Sunday—and Week 1 is one of the most fulfilling and anticipated days of the year. The Detroit Lions need this Week 1. They need it to wash away the ghosts of last year’s opener and fully bury the disappointment of last season for everyone in the organization and the fan base. And to get back to playing Dan Campbell football, the Lions will take on the team that helped cultivate Campbell into the coach he eventually became in Detroit. The New Orleans Saints entered last season much like the narrative surrounding the 2026 Arizona Cardinals: written off and considered a favorite to land the first overall pick in the NFL Draft. But New Orleans’ season became a tale of two halves. The Saints were a plucky bunch that started 1-8 before finishing on a 5-3 tear. That makes them a potentially dangerous Week 1 opponent—a team with a decent roster and coaching staff entering Year 2 that has built some belief in itself. That’s something Lions fans should be plenty familiar with. Below are my three key stats and matchups for the Lions’ season and home opener. Note: Unless otherwise indicated, all statistics are sourced from NFL Pro, FTN Fantasy, Pro Football Reference, or Pro Football Focus. Staley’s resurgent renegades A strong finish to one season doesn’t always translate to a team immediately picking up where it left off the next. But without any in-season evidence yet, it’s our best sample to judge what once-heralded defensive mind Brandon Staley’s defensive demons might be trotting out at Ford Field—even with the offseason losses of Deario Davis and Alontae Taylor, along with future Saints Ring of Honor member Cameron Jordan already ruled out. From Weeks 10-18 last season, the Saints finished top 10 in defensive DVOA and top five in passing EPA, rushing EPA, passing success rate, and rushing success rate allowed—including an absurdly low 39.2% offensive passing success rate. During that span, edge rusher Chase Young spent 98.9% of his snaps lined up on the defensive right side, while Carl Granderson spent 88% of his snaps on the defensive left. Young’s 36 total quarterback pressures ranked tied for 11th among all defenders, even with Micah Parsons, while Granderson’s pass-rush win rate jumped from 8.0% early in the season to 12.3%. Even with the addition of Tyree Wilson, there will likely be a steady dose of Young against Penei Sewell and Granderson against rookie Blake Miller. That’s two formidable foes for the Lions’ newly entrenched bookends to kick off the season. Kool-Aid McKinstry also became a completely different player during the second half of the season. After allowing a 120.0 passer rating, 68.1% reception rate, six touchdowns, and committing five penalties early in the year, those numbers plummeted to a 73.3 passer rating, 45.9% reception rate, two touchdowns, and zero penalties over the second half. McKinstry will enter his third season with confidence as the Saints’ CB1. Also notably, linebacker Pete Werner improved from a 50.4 PFF defensive grade in the first half to 67.6 in the second. New third linebacker on the depth chart Danny Stutsman played 147 of his 204 season snaps during the second half and raised his PFF defensive grade from 59.8 to 74.3. Then-rookie safety and now nickelback Jonas Sanker experienced a similar surge, with his run-defense grade climbing from 63.6 to 78.1, which ranked 13th among 67 qualifying safeties from Weeks 10-18. It’s a relatively young defense that began to coalesce within Staley’s system down the stretch and is now being further entrusted to develop into a unit capable of helping guide New Orleans back to the postseason. This is a solid, ascending defense that will challenge the Lions and new offensive coordinator Drew Petzing immediately, providing a proper Week 1 litmus test for whether Detroit’s offense can get back to being a consistently dominant unit. Heat up the gut Stalwart Saints linebacker Demario Davis returned to the New York Jets for his third stint there after a wildly successful eight seasons in New Orleans. Replacing him is a Saints boomerang and the son of former Lions standout Luther Elliss, Kaden Elliss, who will play on the second level alongside Pete Werner and Danny Stutsman. Elliss is one of the most disruptive pass-rushing off-ball linebackers in football, averaging 7.9 pass-rush reps per game over the last four seasons. During that span, Elliss has combined for 19.5 sacks and 42 quarterback hits—as many QB hits as Cameron Jordan—which rank second and first, respectively, among all off-ball linebackers. Last season, Elliss recorded an 18.3% pass-rush win rate, fifth among off-ball linebackers, along with an impressive 17.6% pressure rate. That came one season after he generated a 21.5% pressure rate in 2024, which ranked seventh among off-ball linebackers. Elliss is a one-man demolition crew as a pass-rushing linebacker up the middle. With Bryan Bresee out for the season and the Saints’ remaining defensive tackle group largely unproven or lackluster, Elliss and his attack-mode aggression will provide the toughest test for the Lions’ gelling interior offensive line of new center Juice Scruggs, third-year left guard Christian Mahogany (and possibly Ben Bartch), and second-year right guard Tate Ratledge. Their communication and chemistry in the middle will be key to preventing Elliss from single-handedly submarining a Lions drive or two. Aww, Shoughs The two highest-rated recruits in Oregon’s 2018 recruiting class were Lions sixth-year left tackle Penei Sewell and Saints second-year quarterback Tyler Shough, with Shough intended to be the eventual heir apparent to Justin Herbert. Not everything went according to plan there. However, the Saints’ decision to take Shough early in the second round last year did, as the signal-caller positioned himself to potentially be their long-term answer after taking over as the starter in Week 9 and holding the job through the final nine games. During that span, Shough ranked tied for third with a 69.2% completion percentage, ninth at 7.6 yards per attempt, and ninth with a 95.8 passer rating. Those are impressive top-10 metrics for a rookie quarterback in Year 1 of Kellen Moore’s system. Not only were the Saints the fastest-paced offense in football last season, averaging just 27 seconds between snaps, but Shough also made quick decisions with the football once he became the starter. His 2.71-second average time to throw was the fourth-fastest in the NFL, with Jared Goff ranking first. Shough was particularly successful targeting players out of the slot, with his leading targets there going to Juwan Johnson (28), Chris Olave (24), and DeVaughn Vele (12). On throws to the slot, Shough ranked top 10 in passer rating (10th, 104.6), yards per attempt (sixth, 8.8), completion percentage (fourth, 74.5%), and, most impressively, EPA per dropback (fourth, 0.45) among 33 qualifying quarterbacks. Defending targets to the slot is one of the biggest mysteries for the Lions. Those matchups will likely involve some combination of Christian Izien ( questionable ) and Day 3 rookie Keith Abney II at nickelback, along with still-uncertain coverage responsibilities for linebackers Jack Campbell, Derrick Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez, and Devin White, plus safeties Chuck Clark, Avonte Maddox, and Thomas Harper. Factoring in the communication required to defend a fast-paced offense and quick passing game that frequently attacks the slot, this will provide a much-needed early-season test for Detroit’s middle-of-the-field coverage defenders. All of that comes with one important weakness to keep in mind: Shough short-circuited under pressure. His 25.9% pressure-to-sack rate ranked 29th out of 33 qualifying quarterbacks, potentially providing an avenue for the Lions’ high-upside defensive front to feast against an…

title: Trey Smack is a Big Deal
summary: A lot of people made fun of the Green Bay Packers for drafting a kicker, but there are two immutable facts about kickers. You can acquire a kicker like any other player via free agency, or as a UDFA, or through the draft. Free agency will require paying the kicker a lot of money for […]
full_text: (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images A lot of people made fun of the Green Bay Packers for drafting a kicker, but there are two immutable facts about kickers. If you want to contend, you really do need a good kicker, or at least an average one, and, To have a kicker, you need to, uhm, acquire a kicker. You can acquire a kicker like any other player via free agency, or as a UDFA, or through the draft. Free agency will require paying the kicker a lot of money for a kicker, and UDFA’s cannot necessarily be counted on. You shouldn’t trade into the second round to get a kicker as the Tampa Bay Bucs once did for Robert Aguayo, but spending a sixth-round pick on one seems fine. The argument against drafting kickers is similar to the argument against kickers generally. They’re barely football players; they only play a few snaps a game, they’re not nearly as manly and concussed as everyone else, and the difference between an average kicker and an elite kicker isn’t really THAT big. But it’s never that simple, and even though the range of kicker outcomes CAN be pretty small in terms of expected points added, kickers often find themselves in EXTREMELY high leverage situations. By Win Percentage Added, the difference can be quite stark. Just last year, Brandon McManus honked a PAT and a makeable field goal in a playoff game , the highest leverage situation you can have. While you cannot expect any given kicker to outperform an average kicker year-to-year, the Packers haven’t had an average kicker since Mason Crosby. If Trey Smack is just average, that’s already an enormous baseline upgrade, but there’s a good chance he’s more than that strictly based on leg power. McManus hit a fair share of kicks over 50 yards during his tenure ( 6 for 8 ), but outside of the mile-high air of Denver, his power was average. Smack seems to have a huge leg, as he put on a show in the preseason in Denver, and more impressively, hit two 58-yarders (one of which was negated by a penalty) in Pittsburgh . Kicking power isn’t ALL that matters, but it opens up new scoring opportunities and, importantly, can replace some of your Hail Marys. Hail Mary throws are a 10% proposition at best, and turning a few of those into 50/50 long field goal tries in high-leverage moments can be game-altering. Trey Smack has yet to play a down in the NFL, but all he has to do to be the best Packer kicker in years is to be average. And maybe he won’t be, but his physical tools appear excellent, and with McManus, the Packers didn’t have a ceiling OR floor. Daniel Whelan has basically solved their punting issues, and if they can actually hit some clutch kicks, they may have a net positive special teams performance for the first time in ages.

That’s the magic number for the Green Bay Packers in 2026 — it’s the number of wins that sportsbooks have set for the team as their expected win total, with the over/under in that category being one of the most popular NFL bets before week one of the season. Indeed, FanDuel sportsbook has the Packers’ total at 9.5, which comes right in line with their totals from two of the past three years. Green Bay has won 9, 11, and 9 games the last three years with Jordan Love at quarterback, making the playoffs as the NFC’s number 7 seed in each season. This year, however, the team’s goals are higher. And Packers fans seem to expect better from their team. This week, we asked our readers at Acme Packing Company to predict the team’s win total, and nearly 80 percent of those who responded expect it to be in the double digits. Here’s a look at the results: That’s right, more than half of Packers fans (51%) responding expect the team to be in that 10 or 11 win range, with another quarter (26% to be exact) expecting even bigger things, at 12-plus. The pessimists are few — just 19 percent expect an 8 or 9-win season, with just four percent expecting double-digit losses with 7 or fewer wins. That probably illustrates the confidence level of this team as well. Heading into the season, about three-quarters of fans surveyed said that they’re confident in the direction of the team. What about you? Are you confident enough in a 10-win season to put something up for that prediction?

title: Remembering a Random Game: The Minnesota Vikings
summary: The Green Bay Packers are set to open the season against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday for the 132nd matchup in the history of the storied rivalry. I’m going to try something fun this season and look back on a random game every week by picking a number between 1 and however many times the […]
full_text: (Photo By JUDY GRIESEDIECK/Star Tribune via Getty Images) | Star Tribune via Getty Images The Green Bay Packers are set to open the season against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday for the 132nd matchup in the history of the storied rivalry. I’m going to try something fun this season and look back on a random game every week by picking a number between 1 and however many times the Packers have played that team. This week’s number? 76. Let’s look back on the Packers 76th meeting against the Minnesota Vikings, a game which took place on September 26th, 1999. Entering the Game It was Week 3 of the 1999 season, and the Packers were 1-1, fresh off a 23-15 loss to the Detroit Lions. It was the team’s first year with HC Ray Rhodes, who was hired after Mike Holmgren resigned to accept the HC job in Seattle, which essentially offered him full control of the team as GM and VP of Football Operations. Rhodes was immediately hired by the Packers after being the only candidate to interview. The season prior, QB Brett Favre led the league in completions (347), completion percentage (63%), and passing yards (4,212). The team ended up going 11-5, and losing in the Wild Card round of the playoffs to the San Francisco 49ers (pardon me while I briefly experience a war flashback). It was time to get back to the Super Bowl. Key Moments Down 7-3 in the 2nd quarter, rookie DB Antuan Edwards picked off Vikings QB Randall Cunningham and took it to the house for a 26-yard return. After this, the game briefly became The Field Goalapalooza after 4 straight FGs between the two teams. With 1:56 left to go in the game, the Vikings were on top again, 20-16, after a 10 yard Randy Moss TD. It was time for the Packers to put together a game-winning drive, and they didn’t have much time left. 27 years later, watching this final drive still stresses me out. Brett Favre marched the team down the field, completing passes to players like WR Corey Bradford, RB Dorsey Levens, and WR Bill Schroeder along the way. And suddenly, it was 4th and 1, with 12 seconds left on the clock. Favre found Bradford, who made his way to the end zone, and the game was over. Packers win at home, 23-20, and move to 2-1 on the year. The Outcome The team headed into their Week 4 bye on a high note and won their next matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers as well. Things started to get a bit bumpy after this, and the Packers would go on to lose three straight games, two separate times. The team finished 4th in the NFC Central at 8-8, and narrowly missed the playoffs in what would end up being their only non-winning season between 1992 and 2004. Ray Rhodes was fired the day after the 1999 season ended and replaced by some guy named Mike Sherman. The 132nd matchup between the Packers and Vikings kicks off in Minnesota at 3:25 local time.

title: Packers sign Tucker Kraft to  4-year contract extension on eve of season opener
summary: The Green Bay Packers wanted a deal done. Tucker Kraft wanted a deal done. And so, just ahead of the start of the 2026 NFL regular season, a deal is indeed done, and it appears to be a great deal for both sides. Tucker Kraft is now under contract with the Packers through the 2030 […]
full_text: ASHWAUBENON, WISCONSIN - JULY 31: Tucker Kraft #85 of the Green Bay Packers looks on during the Green Bay Packers training camp at Ray Nitschke Field on July 31, 2026 in Ashwaubenon, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers wanted a deal done. Tucker Kraft wanted a deal done. And so, just ahead of the start of the 2026 NFL regular season, a deal is indeed done, and it appears to be a great deal for both sides. Tucker Kraft is now under contract with the Packers through the 2030 season, having reportedly signed a 4-year extension to keep him in Green Bay. According to multiple media reports, Kraft’s deal comes in at an initial base value of $75 million in new money over those four additional years for an average value of $18.75 million, but it has another $17 million in bonuses and escalators that could make the maximum value of the contract $92 million in total. That base number does not set a new record for tight ends — George Kittle still holds that mark at $19.1 million — but if Kraft hits the bonuses, that would push him well over Kittle’s mark. Interestingly, this structure seems to find a middle ground for both sides: the Packers avoid giving Kraft a market-setting deal with him coming off a torn ACL, but Kraft gets plenty of opportunities to increase his compensation, presumably by hitting various individual and team goals. Kraft’s signing bonus is $26.5 million, according to Adam Schefter, which is likely the only fully guaranteed money in the deal. While he does not get the highest average annual value for a tight end on this deal, that signing bonus is the biggest ever for a player at that position. This compensation now gets added on to his remaining contract for 2026, which had been set to pay him a base salary of $3,624,000 thanks to the NFL’s Proven Performance Escalator program. Perhaps most remarkable is that Kraft seems fully ready to justify this deal despite not played a down of competitive football since tearing his ACL last November. Still, his recovery has been right on schedule, and he is set to be active with minimal if any limitations for Sunday’s season opener against the Minnesota Vikings.
