title: Three Steelers with the most to lose against the Falcons
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers will open the 2026 regular season Sunday against the Atlanta Falcons, marking the beginning of the Mike McCarthy era and the first meaningful opportunity for several players to establish themselves in their new-look roles. While the season opener is only one game, it could carry significant implications for players competing for playing […]
full_text: The Pittsburgh Steelers will open the 2026 regular season Sunday against the Atlanta Falcons, marking the beginning of the Mike McCarthy era and the first meaningful opportunity for several players to establish themselves in their new-look roles. While the season opener is only one game, it could carry significant implications for players competing for playing time. With a number of young players pushing for opportunities, three Steelers in particular have plenty at stake against Atlanta. Dylan Cook Dylan Cook enters the season as Pittsburgh’s starting right tackle, but his grip on the position may not be as secure as it appears. The Steelers’ official depth chart lists Cook ahead of first-round pick Max Iheanachor, who is currently the backup at right tackle. Cook struggled during the preseason and also endured difficulties in Pittsburgh’s playoff loss to Houston last season. With Aaron Rodgers entering the season as the Steelers’ starting quarterback, protecting him will be one of the most important responsibilities if the team wants to contend. That makes Cook’s performance against Atlanta particularly important. If Cook struggles to consistently handle his assignments against backups, Pittsburgh could have a quick trigger with Iheanachor waiting behind him. The rookie has dealt with an injury that limited his preseason opportunities, but his first-round status gives the Steelers every reason to see what he can provide if Cook continues to struggle. The Falcons could also provide a favorable opening matchup. Atlanta enters Week 1 with significant losses along its pass rush, potentially giving Cook an opportunity to settle into his role. Still, Sunday represents an important early test. Roman Wilson Roman Wilson currently appears to have a firm hold on the No. 3 wide receiver role behind DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr., but that position could become increasingly competitive. Wilson has endured an inconsistent first two years, particularly when it comes to his attention to detail and developing chemistry with Rodgers. There have been too many ugly moments for a receiver expected to become a meaningful part of Pittsburgh’s passing game. The team drafted Germie Bernard in round two to compete for the slot spot. Bernard has generated considerable buzz throughout the preseason and represents the most obvious threat to Wilson’s playing time if the third-year receiver cannot turn his opportunities into consistent production. For Wilson, the Falcons game is about more than simply making a few catches. He needs to demonstrate that he can consistently be where Rodgers expects him to be, win his assignments and avoid the mental mistakes that can quickly erode a quarterback’s trust. If that doesn’t happen, Bernard could begin forcing his way into the rotation sooner rather than later. Payton Wilson Payton Wilson is unlikely to completely lose his role, but his playing time could be affected if his inconsistency continues. Wilson flashed significant potential during his first two seasons, but he has also struggled to maintain consistency. Meanwhile, veteran Cole Holcomb put together a strong preseason and gives Pittsburgh another experienced option at inside linebacker. The Steelers retained both Wilson and Holcomb on their 2026 roster alongside Patrick Queen, giving Mike McCarthy and defensive coordinator Patrick Graham multiple options at the position. That competition could make Wilson’s performance against Atlanta especially important. He doesn’t necessarily need to dominate to retain his role, but he needs to show that he can consistently make the right reads, fit the run and hold up in coverage. If Wilson struggles while Holcomb continues to play well, Pittsburgh could begin shifting some of the veteran’s snaps his way. The bigger picture The Steelers have spent the offseason building a roster that blends veterans with young players who could become important pieces of the team’s future. Cook, Wilson and Wilson all enter Sunday with starting or prominent roles, but each also has a legitimate challenger waiting behind him. That makes the opener against Atlanta more than simply the first game of the McCarthy era. For these three players, it could be the first opportunity to either solidify their place on the depth chart—or open the door for someone else to take it. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Steelers Week 1 game picks
summary: It is the eve of the first Sunday of the NFL season, and the Pittsburgh Steelers will host a beat up Atlanta Falcons team that will be playing its third quarterback and is without its top two edge rushers. Anything can happen in the NFL, though, especially when you have one of the league’s top […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - NOVEMBER 19: A closeup view of a Pittsburgh Steelers helmet prior to a game against the Cleveland Browns at Cleveland Browns Stadium on November 19, 2023 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Getty Images It is the eve of the first Sunday of the NFL season, and the Pittsburgh Steelers will host a beat up Atlanta Falcons team that will be playing its third quarterback and is without its top two edge rushers. Anything can happen in the NFL, though, especially when you have one of the league’s top players in the form of Bijan Robinson. Will Atlanta pull off one of the upsets of the week? Or will the Steelers prevail? Here are our Week 1 staff picks. Joey Bray : The Pittsburgh Steelers begin the Mike McCarthy era at Acrisure Stadium against the already hampered Atlanta Falcons. After an oblique injury to Falcons “starter” Tua Tagovailoa in practice on Thursday, it will be Cooper Rush taking the field for Atlanta. Stopping Bijan Robinson is much easier said than done, and there will likely be some growing pains for the Pittsburgh secondary which is already down a starting safety, and their star corner in Joey Porter Jr. has not fully participated in a practice in several months. At the end of the day, this is a game that the Steelers should win. I’ll bank on Aaron Rodgers and the offense to get enough going to hold off whoever the Falcons have playing QB and get to 1-0 on the season. Steelers 24, Falcons 20 Ryan Parish : We still have so many questions about how this roster will come together under Mike McCarthy. We hardly saw the first team offense this summer, and the part we did (the offensive line) still looked to be ironing out the kinks when we saw them last. On the other side of the ball, I still have major concerns about the state of the secondary and the Steelers struggles at times to stop the run. Fortunately, the Falcons are without their top pass rushers from a year ago, and have one of the worst quarterback rooms in the league. For a Steelers roster that is still finding itself and shaking off some rust, that presents a favorable enough match-up that they should be able to get by with a win, even if this game is a sloppy one. Steelers 23, Falcons 16 Ryland Bickley: The Falcons have some pieces and what should be a competent coaching staff in 2026. Still, it’s hard to expect too much from team down its top two pass rushers and starting a Cooper Rush at quarterback Week 1. The Steelers aren’t without their own flaws, however, and given the team’s at-times sloppy preseason, I’d expect a good amount of rust from the starters in the opener. Much like the last time these two teams faced in Week 1, I expect Pittsburgh to earn the win, but without many style points. Steelers 20, Falcons 13 . Mike Nicastro: Although the Falcons are battered and bruised, I don’t anticipate the Steelers to come out guns blazing. I’m worried about the lack of preseason reps for DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr. – and the offensive line at the moment is less than inspiring. But the difference will be the Steelers pass rush against a statue in Cooper Rush. I’ll predict Nick Herbig and Alex Highsmith each record a sack/fumble. Aaron Rodgers and the offense start slow but click in the second half, and Pat Freiermuth will be the star of the show on that side of the ball. Uninspiring, but mission accomplished. Steelers 23, Falcons 16 . Jason Aponte: It doesn’t matter who starts for the Falcons on Sunday. Kevin Stefanski is set up for a rough debut and the Steelers roll to an easy victory to begin the Mike McCarthy era in Pittsburgh. Steelers 27, Falcons 10. Austin Bechtold: I would be stunned if the Steelers lose. Not having Tua or Michael Penix will hurt the Falcons, and the Steelers can focus solely on slowing down Bijan Robinson. The Falcons are also without their top two pass rushers, which should also benefit the Steelers’ offensive line. The Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy reunion starts out with a successful first game and the Steelers win their first Week 1 home contest since 2014. DK Metcalf and Pat Freiermuth combine for three touchdowns in the victory. Steelers 27, Falcons 14 . Jarrett Bailey: I’m not going to pick this game scared. This is a new era of Steelers football that (hopefully) won’t constantly play down to their competition. The Falcons are on their third quarterback, are without their top two edge rushers, and have less talent than the Pittsburgh roster. Make a statement and beat a team you should beat convincingly. If it’s close, that’s a disappointment. Steelers 27, Falcons 9 . Let us know what you think in the comments . Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more! summary: Mike Tomlin revealed the best team he ever coached in a recent interview with the Today Show — and according to the former Steelers head coach, it’s not the 2008-09 team that won Super Bowl XLIII. “The best team I coached, probably, didn’t win,” Tomlin said. “Probably in the mid-teens, 2015-16. Denver won it that […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PA - DECEMBER 20: Antonio Brown #84 of the Pittsburgh Steelers looks into the stands after scoring a touchdown in the fourth quarter of the game against the Denver Broncos at Heinz Field on December 20, 2015 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Mike Tomlin revealed the best team he ever coached in a recent interview with the Today Show — and according to the former Steelers head coach, it’s not the 2008-09 team that won Super Bowl XLIII. “The best team I coached, probably, didn’t win,” Tomlin said. “Probably in the mid-teens, 2015-16. Denver won it that year with Peyton (Manning).” Former #Steelers HC Mike Tomlin says the best team he coached was the 2015 Steelers, who went 10-6 and lost to the eventual Super Bowl champion #Broncos in the Divisional Round. Pittsburgh played that day without Antonio Brown & Le’Veon Bell. (📽️ 'Glass Half Full', Today Show) https://t.co/7EnJLEeZkQ pic.twitter.com/MStmCatoS2 — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) September 8, 2026 The 2015 Steelers went 10-6, led by the league’s fourth-best scoring offense averaging 26.4 points per game. The team finished second in the AFC North, winning in the wild card round over the Cincinnati Bengals but falling in the divisional round to the eventual Super Bowl Champion Broncos. The Steelers fell in Denver, 23-16, in a game wide receiver Antonio Brown, running back Le’Veon Bell, and offensive linemen Kelvin Beachum and Maurkice Pouncey missed with injury. “Sometimes, man, things don’t come together for you,” Tomlin said. The Pittsburgh offense put up strong numbers that year. Quarterback Ben Roethlisberger recorded 3,938 passing yards with 21 touchdowns and 16 interceptions in just 11 starts. Wide receiver Antonio Brown put up a 136-catch, 1,834-yard season with 10 touchdowns. Wide receivers Markus Wheaton and Martavis Bryant each recorded well over 700 receiving yards each, with tight end Heath Miller adding another 535. The Pittsburgh run game that year was led by DeAngelo Williams (907 rushing yards in 10 starts) and Bell (556 yards in six starts). The starting offensive line was made up of Beachum, Ramon Foster, Pouncey, David DeCastro and Marcus Gilbert. On defense, the 2015 Steelers finished 11th in the NFL that year in scoring, led by a core of Cam Heyward, Stephon Tuitt, Lawrence Timmons, James Harrison and Ryan Shazier. Tomlin was reportedly more emotional than usual following the loss in Denver. “That team? That team was as talented as any team I’ve ever been around,” Tomlin told the Today Show. “We had the goods. But that’s what I love and respect about football, man. It’s a single elimination tournament. It’s not best out of seven. We went into that stadium that day without our No. 1 running back and without our No. 1 wideout, and we suffered the consequences of it. That’s life. “But if you ask me the best team I’ve been around, it would probably be that team.”

title: Early 2027 NFL Draft prospects Seahawks fans should keep an eye on
summary: The 2027 NFL Draft is still a long way away. That needs to be the first disclaimer. The college football season has barely started, and a lot will change between now and April. Players will emerge, others will fall, some will declare early, others will return to school, and a handful of prospects who aren’t […]
full_text: COLUMBIA, MO - OCTOBER 11: Cayden Green #70 of the Missouri Tigers blocks during a college football game against the Alabama Crimson Tide on October 11, 2025 at Memorial Stadium/Faurot Field in Columbia, Missouri. (Photo by Joe Robbins/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The 2027 NFL Draft is still a long way away. That needs to be the first disclaimer. The college football season has barely started, and a lot will change between now and April. Players will emerge, others will fall, some will declare early, others will return to school, and a handful of prospects who aren’t even on most early boards right now will eventually become household names. We’ve already seen how quickly that can happen. Early projections for the 2026 NFL Draft had quarterbacks such as Garrett Nussmeier, Drew Allar and Cade Klubnik being discussed as potential first-rounders, with some early projections placing them inside the top 10. They eventually went in the seventh, third and fourth rounds, respectively. And then there was Fernando Mendoza. Mendoza wasn’t the quarterback dominating the early draft conversation. By the time the 2026 draft arrived, he had developed into the No. 1 overall pick. That’s the nature of the NFL Draft. So this isn’t a ranking, and it certainly isn’t a prediction of who the Seattle Seahawks will select. It’s an early watch list — a collection of players worth knowing as the 2026 college football season develops. That is particularly relevant for the Seahawks because Seattle currently projects to have 11 selections in the 2027 NFL Draft , including a significant number of compensatory picks. Even after trading away a fourth-rounder for Beau Stephens and a sixth-rounder for Avery Smith, the Seahawks remain loaded with draft capital. John Schneider therefore has something every general manager wants at this stage of the process: options. Here are some of the names worth watching. 2027 NFL Draft quarterback prospects Quarterback is obviously a position Seattle will monitor, but that doesn’t mean the Seahawks are going into 2027 needing to draft one. Sam Darnold is coming off a Super Bowl-winning season, and there would be little reason to move away from him if he continues playing at that level. Seattle also has Jalen Milroe developing behind him. But there is another part of the equation. Drew Lock is scheduled to become a free agent after the 2026 season. That doesn’t mean Seattle has to replace him with another veteran or draft a quarterback, but it does mean the team’s quarterback room could look different entering 2027. And that’s exactly why the position belongs on this list. If Darnold plays well, Milroe develops and the Seahawks are happy with the direction of the room, quarterback could remain a low-priority position. But if Darnold’s performance declines, Milroe doesn’t develop as hoped, or an elite quarterback unexpectedly falls within Seattle’s reach, the Seahawks need to know exactly what they’re looking at. With 11 projected picks, Seattle would also have the ammunition to move up if the right quarterback becomes available. So the question isn’t “Will Seattle draft a quarterback?” It’s “Could Seattle have a reason to consider one by April?” That’s a very different question. Dante Moore, Oregon Moore is one of the quarterbacks who could force that conversation. The Oregon quarterback entered 2026 with legitimate first-round buzz after an impressive 2025 season, and he has the physical tools scouts look for: arm talent, mobility, accuracy and the ability to make throws from different platforms. The biggest question isn’t whether Moore can make NFL throws, it’s whether he can consistently make NFL reads. Oregon’s offense can create favorable situations for its quarterback, but evaluators will want to see Moore handle more difficult progressions, identify coverage changes and make good decisions when the first read isn’t there. His ability to operate outside structure will be particularly important. If he takes that next step, Moore could become one of the most important quarterbacks in the 2027 class. And that’s precisely why Seattle should be watching, even if the Seahawks don’t currently have an obvious need at the position. Arch Manning, Texas Manning will naturally attract attention because of his family, but the evaluation needs to go beyond the name. He has the physical talent to become a top quarterback, but there are still questions about his processing and occasional hesitation before letting the ball go. If those issues improve, his talent gives him a clear path back toward the top of the quarterback conversation. Trinidad Chambliss, Ole Miss Chambliss is one of the more fascinating quarterbacks in the class because he doesn’t have the same physical profile as some of the bigger names. His Week 1 performance vs. Louisville, however, showed excellent anticipation and timing. He consistently appeared comfortable throwing the ball before receivers were completely open, which is one of the more difficult quarterback skills to teach. The questions are obvious: Can he maintain that against better defenses, and will his size limit his NFL projection? Those are questions for the rest of the season. Darian Mensah, Miami Mensah is another quarterback whose stock could change dramatically. He opened the season with the highest PFF passing grade among FBS quarterbacks, completing 87 percent of his passes for 400 yards and five touchdowns. Through two games, he has twice as many touchdown passes (8) as incomplete passes (4). That doesn’t make him the next Fernando Mendoza, but it does make him someone Seahawks fans should know. The important part of a 2027 quarterback watch list is not deciding who will be QB1 in September, it’s identifying the players whose development could change the entire conversation by April. Running Back Seattle probably isn’t going to spend another first-round pick on a running back. The Seahawks just used the 32nd overall pick on Notre Dame’s Jadarian Price, making him a significant part of their plans for the position moving forward. But that doesn’t mean running back disappears from the scouting board. The situation could change quickly. Kenneth Walker III is no longer in Seattle, while Zach Charbonnet is entering the final year of his rookie contract. If Charbonnet leaves after 2026, Seattle could suddenly need another young back to pair with Price. That makes running back worth monitoring — just probably not at the top of the draft. Seattle has already invested a first-round pick in Price, so a second consecutive Round 1 running back would be difficult to justify unless something unusual happens. A Day 2 or Day 3 back, however, could make plenty of sense. Ahmad Hardy, Missouri Hardy is one of the backs worth watching closely. He’s a compact, physical runner who combines excellent contact balance with the acceleration to turn small openings into explosive plays. His 2025 season put him firmly on the NFL radar, but his receiving development could ultimately determine how high he goes. That’s especially relevant to Seattle. The Seahawks don’t simply need a back who can carry the ball. A player who can stay on the field in multiple personnel packages and contribute as a receiver becomes much more valuable. If Hardy shows that part of his game consistently in 2026, his stock could rise significantly. Kewan Lacy, Ole Miss Lacy might be one of the most interesting backs in the class. He exploded in 2025, rushing for 1,567 yards and 24 touchdowns , while also contributing as a receiver. His vision is one of his biggest strengths. Lacy sees openings quickly and has the burst to exploit them before defenders can close. He’s not a massive back, but he has enough size to handle a significant workload while possessing the explosiveness NFL teams increasingly value. A strong 2026 season could put him firmly into the early-round conversation. Isaac Brown, Louisville Brown is another player…

title: 49ers had zero sacks against the Rams, but still made massive improvements getting to the quarterback
summary: 58. That’s the number of quarterback hits the San Francisco 49ers generated in the 2025 season. That’s not very good. Even in Week 1, when the entire defense was healthy, the 49ers generated a paltry two quarterback hits and a single sack. Week 1 in their win over the Los Angeles Rams? Zero sacks, but […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - AUGUST 20: Osa Odighizuwa #92 of the San Francisco 49ers warms up before the game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on August 20, 2026 in Inglewood, California. The 49ers defeated the Chargers 41-17. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images 58. That’s the number of quarterback hits the San Francisco 49ers generated in the 2025 season. That’s not very good. Even in Week 1, when the entire defense was healthy, the 49ers generated a paltry two quarterback hits and a single sack. Week 1 in their win over the Los Angeles Rams ? Zero sacks, but eight hits. 13 percent of their entire 2025 total. Now, yes, it is Week 1, so it’s fair to look at last year’s Week 1 pressure rate . In 2025, at Seattle Seahawks , the 49ers managed 10 hits, except no player had more than two. In 2026? Four—or three, depending on where you get your stats from— of those eight hits came from Osa Odighizuwa. Don’t confuse that with the five pressures Odighizuwa also generated in the game. Odighizuwa was a wrecking ball through the middle, something the 49ers have sorely needed. So the defensive line, without sacks, looked pretty ferocious. What else did this help? The secondary. Best illustrated by this video below of one Osa Odighizuwa raising all sorts of hell for Matthew Stafford: #49ers DT Osa Odighizuwa in Week 1: 5 pressures 3 hits/2 hurries 74.3 PFF pass-rush grade 22.2% pass-rush win rate Was the team's best pass-rusher in his debut. Liked how Raheem Morris used him on twists a lot, disrupting Stafford's comfort with his quickness/power pic.twitter.com/RYYDvU25PD — Bradley Locker (@Bradley_Locker) September 11, 2026 Chalk this up to the pass rush making the secondary much better, because the quarterback doesn’t have all day to throw in the pocket. Pressures and hits are nice. It’s disappointing that Alfred Collins is out for the season, but the 49ers have even more room for improvement once Mykel Williams comes off the physically unable to perform list. Provided he can get ramped up with little issue. It’s just one game, and we’ll need to look at a larger sample size to see how much time the 49ers are letting their opposing quarterbacks throw the ball, but so far the Odighizuwa acquisition is paying dividends, and with the addition of Nick Bosa back, the secondary can do its work. At the very least, the 49ers secondary had six interceptions in 2025 total. Getting to the quarterback might improve that number. They got their first one on Thursday.

title: 49ers-Rams: Exposing some bad takes made before the game
summary: The San Francisco 49ers went to Melbourne, Australia, and beat the Los Angeles Rams 27-7 on Thursday. The 49ers were three-point underdogs, but the Rams were being seen as the darlings of the NFL. I think ESPN’s Stephen A. Smith said it best the next day when asked if the media overhyped the Los Angeles […]
full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 11: Deebo Samuel Sr. #19 of the San Francisco 49ers celebrates scoring a touchdown in the fourth quarter of the NFL football game against Los Angeles Rams at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 11, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Quinn Rooney/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers went to Melbourne, Australia, and beat the Los Angeles Rams 27-7 on Thursday. The 49ers were three-point underdogs, but the Rams were being seen as the darlings of the NFL. I think ESPN’s Stephen A. Smith said it best the next day when asked if the media overhyped the Los Angeles Rams: “It appears so.” If you’re like me, you like to point out when people are wrong—especially when it’s bad predictions on the 49ers or their rivals. In this case, things were leaning heavily toward the Rams and the “super team” they built. Then the 49ers went to Melbourne, Australia, and beat them 27-7. And for a Week 1 game, it wasn’t very sloppy either. Now don’t get too excited. This was Week 1. I’m the first to tell you never to take stock in Week 1 games because it’s almost a given that teams look sloppy and have rust to knock off. The thing is, the 49ers looked really good. Not sloppy-play, good, but just good. Sure, it’s Week 1, and the 49ers could come back to earth next week, but it’s the Rams, and I can’t help myself. So let’s be petty and make fun of some bad takes made before the game while we have time! Bill Plaschke: “Rams will go undefeated on their way to winning another home Super Bowl title ” We had a couple of those “Rams are running the table” takes going around, but none got more notorious than the Los Angeles Times’ Bill Plaschke and his column on how the Rams are going to go 17-0. I’m going to make a crazy take myself: I don’t think the Rams are running the table. Plaschke went on to tell us this was a “Favorable schedule”. One where the Rams now have the New York Giants at home, then travel to both the Denver Broncos and Philadelphia Eagles. Then they have the Buffalo Bills. I guess you can say that’s “favorable.” Plaschke hasn’t responded on X as of this writing, besides his recent column in the LA Times about the game being a “jet-lagged flop.” Nick Wright: “I think the Niners defense could be really bad” Most of the time when Wright makes a take, you can easily prove it wrong within five minutes, like his statement that you need first-rounders as skill-position players . I’m not going to say he’s wrong in being skeptical of the defense, but “really bad” is the exact opposite of what actually happened. Like many of you, I had questions about Raheem Morris as defensive coordinator—and still do. Unlike many of you, when I saw Nick Sorensen as defensive coordinator in Week 1 of 2024, I grew optimistic immediately and had high expectations. Well, I’m doing the same thing and having big expectations with Morris. That defense was nothing short of impressive, and this is without Mykel Williams, which should be a nice shot in the arm when he gets back. The 49ers didn’t get a sack, but they did get eight quarterback hits (four of which came from Osa Odighizuwa). The result was a flustered Matthew Stafford throwing a pick to Renardo Green. If you think that’s good, remember that’s eight hits in one game. The 49ers had 58 all of 2025 . That’s an average of under four per game. That, my friends, is improvement. Oh, while we’re on the subject: the Rams didn’t have Aaron Donald, but they did have Myles Garrett. Well, kinda. The Rams had zero (0) sacks and two (2) quarterback hits. That zero is also what shows up for Garrett’s stat sheet. That’s some 2025 49ers defense if I ever saw it. This is a 49ers offensive line we’ve all been questioning this offseason, and they got to Purdy twice? Week 1 or Week 15, that’s not good. Congrats on your interception, though. Louis Riddick: “I think there is a significant gap between the two” Riddick was quick to say the roster of the 49ers was a good group, except it was dependent on a fully healthy Trent Williams, Christian McCaffrey, Nick Bosa, and Fred Warner. After that list, he went on to say those are “aging guys—well, besides Fred Warner, obviously.” Well, sure, those are aging guys, but if Fred Warner is not an aging guy, how in the hell is Nick Bosa, a player taken a year later, an “aging” guy? Yes, the 49ers have an older roster, and yes, Bosa has his injury concerns, but aging doesn’t seem like the right word here. To be fair to Riddick, his take came from evaluating the roster’s health by Week 1 and showing the Rams had little issue with health while the 49ers were still working players like George Kittle back. There’s some substance to that, and I can’t disagree. That said, the gap isn’t nearly as significant as we’re led to believe. A week ago, Riddick shared concerns about the roster. This moron from Niners Nation: “I think the Rams win this one. As per usual, this game is going to be competitive as ever.” Let’s really twist the knife on the rhetoric spewed by this guy: As for a winner, I think the Rams win this one. As per usual, this game is going to be competitive as ever and will come down to the wire, as these games usually do. We’ll get the usual offensive showcase between Sean McVay and Kyle Shanahan, but the Rams win and thank Australia for giving them an easier field. Yes, me. I was an idiot. I said there would be an offensive showcase, not a one-sided beatdown (minus a dumb Brock Purdy interception). I wouldn’t have been surprised had the 49ers won that game, but I certainly didn’t see that happening . Logically, I thought they would come up short. And this is what I get for thinking. Competitive? You mean benching Matthew Stafford with under two minutes left was competitive? I mean, didn’t you hear the announcer? They said the Rams had an opportunity with two timeouts and Eddy Piñeiro missing his field goal. So there was hope! In any case, I’ll add my bad take to this list. What are your bad takes on the game that you had to sit through all of August and September? Put them in the comments below.

title: Could Tim Settle be vital to stopping Saquon Barkley, Eagles in Week 1?
summary: There has been plenty of discussion around Washington’s new defensive additions getting after Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts on Sunday, as Sean Mannion works to install his new Eagles offense. Unfortunately, that aspect of the matchup won’t matter if Washington can’t first stop Saquon Barkley and the Eagles’ rushing attack. In recent seasons, the Commanders’ defense […]
full_text: There has been plenty of discussion around Washington’s new defensive additions getting after Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts on Sunday, as Sean Mannion works to install his new Eagles offense. Unfortunately, that aspect of the matchup won’t matter if Washington can’t first stop Saquon Barkley and the Eagles’ rushing attack. In recent seasons, the Commanders’ defense has not been up to the task. Saquon Barkley rushing in four games against the Commanders since joining the Eagles: -26 rushes-146 yards-2 TD -29-150-2 -15-118-3 -21-132-1 pic.twitter.com/PI07reJGBb — Ian Hartitz (@Ihartitz) September 2, 2026 While there have been a number of reasons for Barkley’s success over the last couple of years, including poor tackling and inferior speed in Washington’s linebacker room, the key to stopping Saquon is fairly simple. Gap control. While maintaining gap integrity in the run game is a basic concept, it is far from easy to achieve versus one of the best running backs in the league, running behind a stout offensive line. Several players currently on Washington’s roster have been known to contribute to lapses and big plays in the past, but one big change to the front seven this season is free agent Tim Settle. The 6-foot, 315-pounder has flown under the radar after spending a good portion of camp and the preseason sidelined by injury, but he represents an upgrade to the interior defense Washington fans haven’t seen in quite some time. The Commanders defense has gone through a series of additions on the interior alongside Daron Payne since Settle left in 2022, including Phidarian Mathis, Johnny Newton, Sheldon Day, Javon Kinlaw and Eddie Goldman. Previous groups failed to make much of an impact in the rush defense, as evidenced by the team’s poor ranking versus the run over the last few years . Washington’s defense ranked 30th in run defense last season, 29th in 2024, and 27th in 2023. Meanwhile, Settle was refining his technique and working in a rotational role for the Buffalo Bills before finally becoming a regular part of the Texans’ defensive line in 2024. He started in 29 games at defensive tackle throughout the past two years, recording nearly 50 combined tackles and 6 sacks before going down with a season-ending foot injury in 2025. In 2024, he had the fifth-best run stop win rate in the NFL. The free agent defensive tackle agreed to a 3-year, $24 million agreement with the Commanders this offseason. So what has changed since Settle’s first tenure in Washington? For one, Settle has learned to keep his pad level low and use his hands to generate leverage and maintain gap integrity. While Settle has always been disruptive in the middle, here you can see the difference between Settle’s play style in 2020 compared to last season’s work with the Texans. Tim Settle is someone nobody really talks about because of the depth on this DLine, but every time he comes into the game, he plays really well. He has a 13.8% run stop % which is 5th highest among all interior defensive lineman and his 75.7 run defense grade is 10th highest. pic.twitter.com/fWzXKhPp8r — Nick Akridge (@nick_akridge) October 13, 2020 Tim Settle dump. pic.twitter.com/LSW4fI6Xj2 — Deuce_Redzone (@redzoneinthelab) September 10, 2026 The refinement in his technique has improved his consistency in the run game and ability to maintain gap integrity. Film analyst Mark Bullock also reviewed Settle’s play following his signing, and noted that the defensive tackle demonstrated increased discipline in his game. Having spent some years away and developing, Settle returns to Washington with the ability to play much more disciplined with his assignment and technique. I’m expecting the Commanders to switch to a 3-4 base front under Daronte Jones, and to do that, they need a nose tackle. Settle wouldn’t have been disciplined enough to play that role consistently when he left Washington, but now he’s very much capable of doing the dirty work inside. This “dirty work” includes the ability to not only take on double-teams but also to disrupt running lanes by fighting through them. That is not to say that he can’t penetrate and get into the backfield either, as Settle still possesses the quickness and agility that made him a fifth-round selection by Washington in the 2018 NFL draft. Importantly, he now has the experience to determine which situation calls for each technique and by reading the offensive line he could play a key role in Sunday’s matchup with Philadelphia. Brian Flores has traditionally had his defensive linemen play a one-gap scheme, but current Commanders defensive coordinator and former Flores assistant Daronte Jones could opt for Settle to play more of a two-gap role to clog the interior and prevent offensive linemen from moving to the second level. This would keep the linebackers and hybrid safeties clean in order to provide the necessary run fits. Like his Commanders offensive coordinator David Blough, Mannion is also expected to implement a heavy outside-zone scheme for the Eagles rushing attack this season, so Settle could also penetrate the backfield at either the nose tackle or three-technique if he reads the play moving to the outside. This could disrupt pulling linemen, prevent reach blocks and clog cutback lanes if Barkley tries to bend the run back inside. Quick, effective penetration can be devastating to the timing of an outside zone run. Jones clearly understands that limiting Barkley requires the entire defense to carry out their assignments, play with discipline, and make the necessary tackles. He said as much in his Thursday presser , stating “It’s not a one-man job. It’s a team effort.” However, Tim Settle was brought in to win on the interior of the defensive line, and while there have been plenty of other players tasked with this same assignment, Settle looks to have the game to actually do it. Jones may be planning on using his skill set to provide an anchor point for a number of new players on the second level of the defense as they work to identify and complete their assignments in their first game in the system. Increased speed in the linebacker room will be a huge part of Washington’s defensive plan, but good run defense starts up front by controlling gaps and winning at the line of scrimmage. On Sunday afternoon, Settle will be called on to prove that he can be that player as he takes the field as a Washington Commander for the first time.

title: Commanders survey results: High confidence despite brutal Sept schedule
summary: This week’s Reacts survey conducted by Hogs Haven provides a snapshot of fan confidence in the week prior to the start of the 2026 regular season. We asked two questions in this week’s poll, and the results offer slightly different views that, when taken together, are enlightening. Overall direction The first survey question asked if […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - AUGUST 28: Stefon Diggs #3 of the Washington Commanders looks on before a preseason game against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by G Fiume/Getty Images) | Getty Images This week’s Reacts survey conducted by Hogs Haven provides a snapshot of fan confidence in the week prior to the start of the 2026 regular season. We asked two questions in this week’s poll, and the results offer slightly different views that, when taken together, are enlightening. Overall direction The first survey question asked if readers are confident that the Commanders are headed in the right direction. A solid majority, 70% of respondents, voted yes, compared to just 30% who remain skeptical. This relatively solid vote of confidence shows that most of the community still believes in the long-term vision of the front office and coaching staff. Fans are not just hoping for change; they see an actual foundation being built and hope or expect better results in 2026 and beyond — results that will look much more like Washington’s 2024 season than the 2025 season. Of course, the 30% aren’t sold on something – the roster; the coaching; the general manager, or maybe ‘all of the above’. Those respondents are more likely to see 2025 as being representative of who the Commanders really are, and to perceive 2024 as the outlier. That’s the question that the 2026 season will probably answer for most fans; specifically, whether the success in 2024 was a flukey result of weak schedule and good luck with injuries, or whether 2025 was the fluke, with a poorly constructed roster and ravaging injuries. Optimists are likely to see Jayden Daniels’ rookie success and the trip to the NFC Championship game as reflective of the changes that the Josh Harris ownership group has brought to Washington, while skeptics will point to weak drafts, poor player development and lack of star power outside the QB position as structural issues created by Washington’s front office. The first quarter of the 2026 season The second question in this week’s Reacts survey asked fans to predict the team’s win-loss record after the first four games of the season. The responses showed a remarkably grounded perspective: Visit our partners at FanDuel A combined 81% of voters expect the Commanders to sit at .500 or below after the opening 4 games. While it looks pretty bad, this isn’t really surprising given the factors at play. Flukey opening schedule Firstly, Washington – quite unusually – starts with back-to-back road games against division opponents. It’s common for NFL fans and analysts to project divisional opponents to split each season series, usually with the home team expected to win. This convention would see most NFL fans pencil in a pair of Commanders losses to open the season based on them being road games versus NFC East opponents. That would be a rough start despite the assumption that — according to the theory that has division opponents splitting a season series — Washington would eventually chalk up wins in their home games against the Eagles in Week 8 and the Cowboys in Week 18. While most NFL fans are familiar with the really lousy odds for teams that open 0-2 or 0-3 to make the playoffs, the rarity of an NFL team opening with two divisional road games is so stark that the historical odds can pretty much be thrown out the window. So, while 0-4 would be a true disaster, if the Commanders actually do start 1-3 or 2-2, it should not be viewed as a failure or a sign that progress is stalling. It will, in large part, be a function of NFL calendar dynamics – but what those dynamics taketh away, they also giveth. The silver lining for Washington lies heavily in the back half of the schedule. While the first 9 weeks offer a grueling gauntlet of opponents and travel, from Week 10 to Week 16 the Commanders enter what appears to be a relatively benign 7-week stretch against a less intimidating lineup of opponents that includes the Giants, Cardinals, Titans, Texans, Falcons and Vikings. It’s not just who you play; it’s when you play them Another factor at play in assessing differing challenges and opportunities in the two halves of the season is the fact that Washington is introducing new coaches and schemes on both sides of the ball. While this may offer a bit of ‘surprise factor’ against the Eagles and Cowboys to open the season, it could also mean that the Commanders won’t be playing their best football until November and December. This could be part of the reason why the Commanders’ win-loss record may look a bit grim at the Week 7 bye, but the likelihood of players hitting their stride in the new systems around the time the Eagles visit Landover on November 2 should provide reasons for optimism that the Commanders will be able to stack wins — maybe a lot of wins — between Halloween and New Year’s Eve. This may be one of those seasons where Washington will be digging out of a hole in the latter half of the season, but the team has done that successfully before. After opening 3-6 in 2012, the Redskins won 6 straight games to close out the season, win the division, and get into the playoffs. In 2015, following a 3-5 start, the Redskins won 6 of the final 8 games to finish with a winning record and another NFC East title. While the 2020 team didn’t finish with a winning record, following a 1-5 start, the team won 5 of its final 7 games to clinch its 3rd division crown in 9 seasons. Of course, in Jayden’s rookie season, after a 3-game mid-season skid dropped the Commanders record to 7-5, the team finished the year with 5 consecutive regular season wins to finish 12-5, and followed that up with two playoff road wins to reach the NFC Championship game. This may be one of those seasons where the team will need a lot of Ws after the Week 7 bye to finish the season with a playoff berth. While we’re thinking about “when you play them”, it’s clear that injuries and other random factors can also play a role. For example, most respondents voted in this poll before Seattle’s starting quarterback, Sam Darnold, suffered an injury in the game against the Patriots. He may not be available to play in Week 3 against the Commanders, which could skew the odds. As the new offensive and defensive systems become second nature, the Commanders will be well-positioned to stack victories, build momentum, and finish the year strong. In other words, the kind of rocky start envisioned by most of the respondents in our survey doesn’t preclude a successful season or a spot in the playoffs. That may be at least part of the reason why 70% of you are still confident in the team’s direction. Bill-in-Bangkok post script For my part, prior to kickoff every week of every season, I expect Washington to win every game. To me, that outlook is the essence of sports. I’m not saying that everybody has to fan the way I do, but it’s served me well for about 6 decades now. I read this on a Sports Illustrated article today and it ticked me off a bit: Next to no one is picking the Washington Commanders to hold their own in a hostile Week 1 debut against the Philadelphia Eagles, with even the most devoted D.C. homers admitting that things have looked better for their franchise in recent memory than they presently do heading into the weekend. As if this wasn’t already the Eagles, a team that’s split a pair of Super Bowl appearances over five consecutive postseason berths, the Commanders seem to have only barely limped out of a rocky offseason peppered with mixed storylines. This isn’t where my head is at. Not at all. I’m expecting this iteration of the Commanders to make me — hell, make all of us — proud this season. Washington enters Sunday’s opener with an elite quarterback in Jayden Daniels who was affected by injuries last year, but who proved himself in 2024 and has looked sharp all through training camp. McLaurin is healthy & motivated and paired with Stefon Diggs, who is a year…

Enjoy! Commanders links Articles The Washington Sun Jayden Daniels Is Preparing for His Next Act While it’s unclear what the coming season will bring, one thing feels certain in Ashburn: This is Jayden Daniels 2.0. Daniels spent the offseason strengthening his entire body, particularly his legs, core and hips. He told The Sun he added “eight to 10 pounds” of muscle. But they may be hard to spot: Ever since Daniels was a 135-pound freshman in high school, there has been skepticism around his weight. He’s too skinny. His body won’t hold up. He needs some milk. Daniels, currently listed at 6-foot-4 and 210 pounds, said it’s all a misconception. “I think it’s more so my build,” he said. “I’m heavier than a lot of people actually give me credit for. title: Terry McLaurin among five Commanders key to Week 1 clash vs. Eagles
summary: We’ve got a game that counts on our hands Sunday afternoon, when the Commanders play the Eagles in Philadelphia.   In a word: Finally.   The 2026 NFL regular season is here, when we finally see what all those free-agent signings, NFL draft picks, and new play callers can do for a Commanders team looking […]
full_text: We’ve got a game that counts on our hands Sunday afternoon, when the Commanders play the Eagles in Philadelphia. In a word: Finally. The 2026 NFL regular season is here, when we finally see what all those free-agent signings, NFL draft picks, and new play callers can do for a Commanders team looking to rebound from a 5-12 showing . Starting the season against host Philadelphia is no easy task. It will require quality and consistent execution from both sides of the football, winning tough matchups and finding a way to pull through at the end. We could pick darn near anyone as a key player in this matchup, but we’ll stick to five Commanders (not named Jayden Daniels) to watch heading into this NFC East clash: WR Terry McLaurin Terry McLaurin and Jayden Daniels played less than 15% percent of Washington’s offensive snaps together in 2025 due to various injuries. This year, Washington’s No. 1 receiver and his quarterback have spent months getting in sync, from the offseason program to private workouts in L.A. and all the way through training camp. This duo is ready to show what it can do. Stefon Diggs and Chig Okonkwo (more on him later) have Philly’s respect, which should even out coverage and let McLaurin cook. Offensive coordinator David Blough talked about getting McLaurin 10 targets a game. That was in May , in a pre-Diggs world, but feeding McLaurin over and again, especially early, could open up the rest of the offense. And, when it matters most, Daniels has a guy to be counted on to go make a big play. LB Sonny Styles We all know deep down what Sonny Styles is capable of at the NFL level. The athleticism is there. So is the want to. And the intelligence. Putting all that into consistently excellent execution is a process no rookie gets right all at once, so he probably should’ve been forgiven for less-than-perfect during the preseason. The Ohio State product took it all in stride , learning from his college experience how high expectations can lead to scrutiny. Sonny Styles heard the online criticisms about his initial preseason games. Said a similar scenario unfolded when he switched positions at Ohio State. Part of the deal. Things worked out there. pic.twitter.com/w5cFKo1dJv — Ben Standig (@BenStandig) September 11, 2026 Don’t expect perfection from the No. 7 overall NFL draft pick on Sunday, but it’s fair to predict different looks and assignments than we saw in a super vanilla preseason. Head coach Dan Quinn said the Commanders can’t wait to “unleash” Styles on Sunday. It’s fair to expect Washington to use his coverage ability a ton, plus his speed and size as a blitzer from unconventional locations (or to at least make it look that way). A game of sure tackling and quality coverage will go a long way in helping Washington get a win. C Nick Allegretti Including the veteran center here is a statement of the obvious. Nick Allegretti missed most of training camp and the preseason with a calf strain that wouldn’t get right . He revved things up over the past week-plus and is now physically ready to go. His lack of reps with Jayden Daniels can’t be allowed to negatively impact Washington in this one, so his help with protection calls and checks must be spot on. Then there’s the unenviable task of handling Philadelphia’s defensive front, featuring Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis. Allegretti and the Commanders interior must win consistently at the point of attack – surely with some schematic help – and be impactful on the inside. Major gaffes could lead to game-changing plays. Allegretti must avoid those at all costs. TE Chig Okonkwo The new Commanders tight end is a versatile talent who should be impactful in the passing game, lining up at several different spots in search of favorable mismatches. While Okonkwo can play in the slot, he might be more impactful in-line against Philly, chipping off the edge before heading into routes. There’s a great deal he can do in space and he should be a viable option both up the seam and over the middle of the field. I’d expect offensive coordinator David Blough to use a bunch of multiple tight-end sets, and Okonkwo should be a menace with Washington passing out of them. Such a stage offers the former Tennessee Titan a chance to show why Washington rewarded him with a handsome contract . EDGE K’Lavon Chaisson Both K’Lavon Chaisson (knee) and Odafe Oweh (calf) were limited during the practice week, so it’s possible one of both of them could be on a pitch count. Both guys must perform well with the snaps available, especially with Dorance Armstrong serving a one game suspension. Chaisson finished the 2025 season (with New England) on absolute fire , showing an ability to get after and take down the quarterback. Operating at last year’s level will put added pressure on Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts and force game-changing mistakes, which Washington will need on Sunday, and Chaisson is the big-game player to provide them. We just listed five Commanders players that are a key to victory, but easily could’ve named a bunch more. Let us know who else is essential to the Washington’s cause (and why) in the comments below:

title: Commanders season preview: Stakes are high for Washington, Jayden Daniels
summary: Editor’s note: After posting some insightful stories in The Feed, Hogs Haven’s ShogunofHarlem93 has put together his first story for the main site. He breaks down why this Commanders season is so important for Jayden Daniels, new coordinators David Blough and Daronte Jones (and those that hired them). Every season, I try to set realistic […]
full_text: Editor’s note: After posting some insightful stories in The Feed, Hogs Haven’s ShogunofHarlem93 has put together his first story for the main site. He breaks down why this Commanders season is so important for Jayden Daniels, new coordinators David Blough and Daronte Jones (and those that hired them). Every season, I try to set realistic expectations for this Washington Commanders team. In 2024, my only hope was that Jayden Daniels would prove to be Washington’s franchise quarterback. And boy, did he deliver, leading the Commanders all the way to the NFC championship game. After an offseason of adding talent to a barebones roster, I had incredibly high hopes for 2025. Instead, the season was completely gutted. Injuries, poor decision making and uncompetitive games dragged Washington down to a massive low point, erasing a decade’s worth of renewed optimism. It made last year incredibly hard to stomach. Head coach Dan Quinn saw the writing on the wall and let both of his coordinators go. While most head coaches in his position would hire experienced retreads to save their own skins, Quinn took a massive gamble. He brought in two newcomers: Daronte Jones and David Blough. We have absolutely no clue how this will translate when the games actually matter. The stakes are incredibly high, and every single storyline this year feels like an unprecedented gamble. Will the real Jayden Daniels stand up Jayden Daniels entered the league with a clear mission statement: prove he was the best quarterback in the 2024 NFL draft class. He shattered records and dragged this franchise somewhere it hadn’t been in over 30 years — the NFC Championship Game . Even though they were ultimately handled by a dominant Philly team that went on to win the Super Bowl, the foundation seemed set. Yet, despite the optimism surrounding his progression, the “sophomore slump” narrative still loomed. I blindly dismissed it at the time, firmly believing a slump was impossible because his rookie year was a tale of two entirely different Jaydens. Early in 2024, then-offensive coordinator Kliff Kingsbury relied heavily on first-down screens, RPOs and vertical concepts. At one point, Washington ran an absurd 35% of their first-down plays as screens to protect a highly suspect offensive line. The faster Jayden got the ball out, the better. But in Week 11, the Eagles completely exposed the game plan. Philly squeezed the offense’s lateral spacing and dared Daniels to attack the intermediate middle of the field. While most rookie quarterbacks could’ve hit a wall and coordinators could’ve waited until the offseason to adjust, Washington adapted immediately. Over the following weeks, they challenged the toughest part of the field — the 6-to-10-yard intermediate middle. Their screen frequency plummeted from 35% to 21%, the vertical deep shots were scaled back and they completely rebuilt the offense on the fly without losing momentum. It is impossible to overstate how impressive it was for a rookie to handle that mental adjustment. That mid-season pivot is exactly what made 2025 so incredibly frustrating. We can talk about the injuries and the lackluster supporting cast — points that have been discussed ad nauseam — but when he was on the field, the performance simply wasn’t there. His completion percentage tanked by an alarming 9%. There were costly underthrows, balls skipped into the dirt and while the playmakers around him offered little help, the regression from his rookie brilliance was surreal. To put a 9% completion percentage drop into historical perspective, look at how similar drop-offs impacted other notable quarterbacks: Quarterback Season 1 (Cmp %) Season 2 (Cmp %) Percentage Drop The Following Season (Year 3) Context / Rationale Carson Wentz 2018: 69.6% 2020: 57.4% -12.20% 2021 (IND): 62.4% Lost his job in Philadelphia due to mechanical breakdown; bounced back slightly under Frank Reich in Indy. Kurt Warner 2001: 68.7% 2003: 56.5% -12.20% 2004 (NYG): 62.8% Hand fractures and sudden fumbling issues led to a severe multi-year downward spiral before his Arizona resurgence. Deshaun Watson 2020: 70.2% 2022: 58.2% -12.00% 2023 (CLE): 61.4% A full year away from football followed by a team change to Cleveland severely disrupted his pocket rhythm. Cam Newton 2018: 67.9% 2019: 56.2% -11.70% 2020 (NNE): 65.8% A Lisfranc foot injury limited his 2019 run to just two games, severely skewing his active consecutive volume. Joe Burrow 2022: 70.5% 2023: 59.3% -11.20% 2024 (CIN): 68.3% A severe pre-season calf strain and subsequent torn wrist ligament caused his accurate throw rate to tank temporarily in 2023. Cam Newton 2020: 65.8% 2021: 54.8% -11.00% 2022: Out of NFL Rejoined a highly unstable Carolina offensive structure mid-season, leading to structural accuracy regression. Daniels faces an uphill battle, but history shows a recovery isn’t impossible — especially when you look at guys like Joe Burrow or Kurt Warner who weathered the storm. What makes his current situation so fascinating is that he is learning a brand-new offense simultaneously. Transitioning to a true pro-style system after years in spread and RPO-heavy schemes is a massive hurdle, but the buzz out of training camp has been incredibly positive regarding his mental processing. He took over 500 snaps in camp, an intensive workload designed to fast-track his comfort level. Whether that practice volume translates to wins remains to be seen, but the foundation is there. If JD5 can bounce back and replicate or surpass his rookie efficiency, watch out: he’ll vault right back into the top-10, if not the top-5 quarterback conversation. Defense? DEFENSE!! I can join the crowd and rag on former defensive coordinator Joe Whitt Jr. all day, but let’s be real — he wasn’t the sole reason this defense was completely awful. When your best pass rusher is a nearly 40-year-old Von Miller, you have fundamental problems. The personnel was a total mess. An old, slow defense will get absolutely ripped to shreds in today’s NFL. Even when Quinn took over the defensive play-calling duties they were still getting dismantled, proving a massive overhaul was needed. To Quinn’s credit, he recognized his own limitations, stepped back and brought in a defensive coordinator whose system is a complete departure from the scheme Quinn ran his entire career. Enter Daronte Jones. Outside of his brief stint calling plays at LSU , he’s a first-time NFL coordinator tasked with bringing a chaotic, Brian Flores-style scheme to Washington. To give him a fighting chance, management went all-in, injecting $165.8 million into that side of the ball — the sixth-highest defensive spend in the league. They completely reshaped the roster by signing Odafe Oweh, Tim Settle, K’Lavon Chaisson, Nick Cross and Leo Chenal, while using the draft to secure young talent like Sonny Styles and Joshua Josephs. With up to eight new starters, this unit simply has to outperform the disasters of the past three defensive seasons. Everything will live and die with the defensive line. For the last two years, this team was hellbent on blitzing heavy on first and second down to force third-and-long situations. The fatal flaw? They kept giving up first downs anyway, not to mention working with a completely awful run defense. The new additions must restore order in the trenches and finally unlock the underperforming duo of Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw. With a brand-new scheme and a completely reconstructed starting lineup, this defense is one of the biggest mysteries in the league. New -ish Sheriff in Town When Kliff Kingsbury was initially hired, I wasn’t a fan. I believed his offense was inherently predictable and destined to hit a proverbial wall every season. While his explosive 2024 campaign proved me wrong, he unfortunately reverted to those same stubborn play-calling habits in 2025. His firing wasn’t a shock, though I did assume he’d get one final year to redeem himself. Instead, Quinn opted for a…

title: Why Baker Mayfield's contract means the QB market could burst
summary: Baker Mayfield just got $55 million per year in new money -- which is telling about where the QB market is headed. That's great news for 11 other passers ready for big deals.
full_text:
Fifty-five million dollars per year for Baker Mayfield ? Seriously?! 

 Well, yes and no. Mayfield got his new deal from the Buccaneers on Tuesday, and it was a doozy. But it was also one of those win-win NFL contract outcomes where the player and agent get to brag about one number while the team gets to say, "Yeah, but ..."

 Mayfield was already making $27 million in 2026. He now makes $37 million in 2026, $50 million in 2027, $50 million in 2028 and $55 million in 2029. That's four years and $192 million, which works out to $48 million per year over four years. But the "new money" in the deal -- money he didn't already have coming to him -- totals $165 million, and the Bucs added three years to his existing deal. Over three years, the average of $165 million is $55 million per year.

 That's why both sides can claim victory and call it a win-win.

 But you know who else comes out of this looking like winners? Every other quarterback who is or could be coming up for a contract extension within the next year.

 Mayfield is a really good player. His career looked destined for an early end just a few years after he was the No. 1 pick in the 2018 draft, but he has found a home in Tampa, and it agrees with him. He has averaged 32 touchdown passes and 4,079 yards per season, and he won two NFC South division titles in three years with the Bucs. He has been good for them -- and they've been good for him.

 

 But $55 million per year puts him in a tie with five other guys for third-highest average salary in the league. Dak Prescott makes $60 million per year. Patrick Mahomes ' new-money average in his most recent deal was $64 million. Mahomes is the only quarterback who has even threatened -- let alone passed -- Prescott's salary in the two years since his deal was completed. Mahomes is also the only one with two MVP trophies, three Super Bowl titles and a 17-4 career playoff record. Mahomes is his own category.

 The five who are tied with Mayfield at $55 million? Matthew Stafford (has won a Super Bowl and an MVP award), Joe Burrow (has been to a Super Bowl), Josh Allen (has won MVP), Jordan Love and Trevor Lawrence (uhh ... have excellent timing).

 In eight NFL seasons, Mayfield has made two Pro Bowls, and his highest finish in MVP voting is 11th. His place is among the last two names in that previous paragraph, not the first three. But his presence there is what should finally make it a crossable threshold for the next group. Unlike Love and Lawrence, Mayfield wasn't benefiting from a red-hot extension market at the time he signed. This was a quiet year for top-of-the-market quarterback deals.

 Mayfield had some leverage -- his contract was set to void three days after the Super Bowl and trigger an immovable $30 million dead-money cap charge for 2027 -- but the Bucs could have let him walk and trusted in their ability to find a good, affordable solution. You know, the way they did when Tom Brady retired and they signed Mayfield in the first place. The Buccaneers appear to have done this deal because Mayfield has been a really good quarterback for them, and this is what really good quarterbacks' contracts cost now.

 This is fantastic news for anyone who considers himself a really good NFL quarterback and is (or will be) looking for a contract extension between now and next summer. And there are a lot of people in this category. The 2027 quarterback extension market could be the busiest we've seen in a while. And that is why 2027 should be the year when one or (likely) more quarterbacks try to join Prescott and Mahomes in the $60 million club. Many of them should, at least, get past the $55 million that we will now, for the purpose of this exercise, call the "Baker Line."

 Here's a look at the quarterbacks in those conversations.

 

 

 Lamar Jackson , Baltimore Ravens 
 Jackson enters this season with two years left on his contract. He is making $52 million this year and is scheduled to make $52 million next year. The team approached him about an extension this past offseason, but nothing got done .

 

 Jackson has tremendous leverage because his deal includes a clause that prohibits the Ravens from using the franchise or transition tags on him when he (hypothetically) becomes a free agent in 2028; it also has a no-trade clause. So, even if the Ravens couldn't get an extension done by next offseason and decided to trade Jackson rather than let him play out his contract year, he could pick his destination and veto any trade he didn't like.

 Is he over the Baker Line? He is, by two MVP awards if nothing else. Jackson is the one guy in this group who already has a strong case to surpass Prescott's average annual salary of $60 million. It would be shocking and foolish at this point for him to agree to anything less. Imagine if Jackson were to stay healthy for two more years, play lights-out in both of them and become an unrestricted free agent in spring 2028 with no franchise tag to limit his earnings potential? What would he get ... $70 million per year? $80 million?

 
 

 Drake Maye , New England Patriots 
 Entering his third year in the NFL, Maye will be eligible for a contract extension whenever the Patriots' season ends. Having finished second in MVP voting and led the team to the Super Bowl in his second season, Maye would have had a case to be over the Baker Line if he had been allowed to negotiate an extension this offseason. (CBA rules say you have to wait until after the player's third year.) The Patriots have a fifth-year option for 2028, which would buy them time next spring to work on this.

 Is he over the Baker Line? Right now, probably. Mayfield has never been to the Super Bowl or placed second in MVP voting. If Maye were to suffer a significant injury or experience dramatic regression from his 2025 performance, he might be in a situation similar to the one C.J. Stroud is in right now, with the team picking up the option and waiting to see more before committing. But ( Wednesday night 's fourth-quarter meltdown aside) that feels unlikely.

 
 

 Caleb Williams , Chicago Bears 
 

 Jayden Daniels , Washington Commanders 
 

 Bo Nix , Denver Broncos 
 I'm grouping these three together because they're in very similar situations. Maye's 2024 first-round classmates have yet to reach the Super Bowl (which is why he got his own entry here), but each has shown plenty of the promise that led their teams to draft them where they did.

 

 Daniels won Offensive Rookie of the Year and took the Commanders to the NFC Championship Game in his rookie season, then injuries derailed his second year. Nix helped the Broncos reach the AFC Championship Game last season, though he couldn't play in it because he broke his ankle during one of the final plays of Denver's overtime playoff victory over the Bills the week before. Williams struggled in his first year but really took off last season once the Bears hired Ben Johnson as their head coach. Williams didn't get to the NFC Championship Game, but the Bears took the Rams to overtime the week before in the divisional round.

 All three of these guys can likely count on their teams picking up their fifth-year options next spring for 2028 if they can't get deals done before then. The other 2024 first-rounders were Atlanta's Michael Penix Jr . and Minnesota's  J.J. McCarthy , who don't yet merit much mention in a conversation like this.

 Are they over the Baker Line? It depends. But given their credentials and accomplishments so far, each should get there as long as they show improvement rather than regression in Year 3.

 
 

 C.J. Stroud , Houston Texans 
 The second pick in the 2023 draft had his fifth-year option for 2027 picked up in May, but he still hasn't secured an extension from the Texans, a team that is as proactive and generous as any in the league when it comes to veteran contract extensions.
